records.question: X is crystalline salt of sodium. Solution of X in water turns litmus red produces a gas which turns lime water milky when added to sodium carbonate. With barium chloride solution, X gives a white precipitate which is insoluble in dilute hydrochloric acid. X is
records.sourceExplanation: NaHSO₄ is an acid salt that turns litmus red. It reacts with sodium carbonate to produce CO₂ gas (turns lime water milky). With BaCl₂, it gives a white precipitate of BaSO₄ which is insoluble in dilute HCl.

records.question: The alkanol obtained from the production of soap is
records.sourceExplanation: Soap is produced by saponification of fats and oils with NaOH. The reaction produces soap (sodium salt of fatty acids) and glycerol (propane-1,2,3-triol) as a byproduct.

records.question: The flame used by welders in cutting metals is
records.sourceExplanation: Oxy-acetylene flame produces extremely high temperatures (about 3000°C) needed for welding and cutting metals. It is produced by burning acetylene in oxygen.

records.question: Consecutive members of an alkane homologous series differ by
records.sourceExplanation: In the alkane homologous series, each successive member differs by a CH₂ group. For example, methane (CH₄), ethane (C₂H₆), propane (C₃H₈) differ by CH₂.

records.question: If an element has the electronic configuration 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p² it is
records.sourceExplanation: The element has its last electron in the p-orbital (3p²), making it a p-block element. The configuration shows 4 valence electrons (3s²3p²), which is silicon (group IVA).

records.question: Some copper (II) sulphate pentahydrate (CuSO₄·5H₂O) was heated at 120°C with the following results: Wt of crucible = 10.00g, Wt of crucible + CuSO₄·5H₂O = 14.98g, Wt of crucible + residue = 13.54g. How many molecules of water of crystallization were lost? [H=1, Cu=63.5, O=16, S=32]
records.sourceExplanation: Mass of hydrated salt = 14.98 - 10.00 = 4.98g. Mass of residue = 13.54 - 10.00 = 3.54g. Mass of water lost = 4.98 - 3.54 = 1.44g. Moles of CuSO₄ = 3.54/159.5 = 0.0222 mol. Moles of H₂O lost = 1.44/18 = 0.08 mol. Ratio = 0.08/0.0222 ≈ 3.6 ≈ 4 molecules.

records.question: The three-dimensional shape of methane is
records.sourceExplanation: Methane (CH₄) has sp³ hybridized carbon with four bonding pairs of electrons arranged tetrahedrally around the carbon atom with bond angles of 109.5°.

records.question: An unknown organic compound X has a relative molecular mass of 180. It contains C, H, and O in the atomic ratio 1:2:1. The compound has a sweet taste and melts on heating. In the presence of yeast and in the absence of air, X is converted to compound Y and a colourless gas. Compound Y reacts with sodium metal to produce a gas Z which gives a 'pop' sound with a glowing splint. Y also reacts with ethanoic acid to give a sweet smelling compound W. Compound W is
records.sourceExplanation: X is glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) which ferments to ethanol (Y) and CO₂. Ethanol reacts with sodium to produce hydrogen gas (pop sound) and with ethanoic acid to form ethyl ethanoate, a sweet-smelling ester.

records.question: The molecular formula of X is
records.sourceExplanation: The empirical formula is CH₂O with molecular mass 180. (CH₂O)n = 180 → (12+2+16)n = 180 → 30n = 180 → n = 6. Therefore molecular formula is C₆H₁₂O₆ (glucose).

records.question: The reaction of X with yeast forms the basis of the
records.sourceExplanation: Glucose fermentation by yeast produces ethanol and CO₂. This process is fundamental to the brewing industry for producing alcoholic beverages.

records.question: A mixture of common salt, ammonium chloride and barium sulphate can best be separated by
options: addition of water followed by filtration then sublimation
addition of water followed by sublimation then filtration
sublimation followed by addition of water then filtration
records.answerText: sublimation followed by addition of water then filtration
records.sourceExplanation: NH₄Cl sublimes first and is collected. NaCl dissolves in water while BaSO₄ is insoluble and can be filtered out. NaCl is then recovered by evaporation.

records.question: Which of the following relationships between the pressure P, the volume V and the temperature T, represents an ideal gas behavior?
records.sourceExplanation: For an ideal gas, PV = nRT, so P ∝ T/V. This combines Boyle's law (P ∝ 1/V at constant T) and Charles's law (V ∝ T at constant P).

records.question: In the above experiment (fig1) the litmus paper will initially
records.sourceExplanation: When chlorine gas is passed into water, it forms HCl and HOCl. The acid formed turns blue litmus paper red. The bleaching action of chlorine is due to the liberation of oxygen.

records.question: The colour imparted to a flame by calcium ion is
records.sourceExplanation: Calcium ions give a brick-red or orange-red flame test. This is due to the excitation of electrons in calcium atoms which emit light of characteristic wavelength when returning to ground state.

records.question: In the reaction M + N ⇌ P, ΔH = +Q kJ. Which of the following would increase the concentration of the product?
records.sourceExplanation: Since ΔH is positive (endothermic reaction), decreasing temperature favors the exothermic reverse reaction, which decreases product concentration. Increasing temperature favors forward reaction. A catalyst does not shift equilibrium.

records.question: 2FeCl₃ + SnCl₂ → 2FeCl₂ + SnCl₄
records.sourceExplanation: In reaction 1, Fe (0) changes to Fe²⁺ (+2) - oxidation. In reaction 3, Fe²⁺ (+2) changes to Fe³⁺ (+3) - oxidation. In reactions 2 and 4, iron is reduced.

records.question: In the above experiment (fig.2), a current was passed for 10 minutes and 0.63g of copper was found to be deposited on the cathode of CuSO₄ cells. The weight of AgNO₃ cell during the same period would be [Cu = 63, Ag = 108]
records.sourceExplanation: According to Faraday's second law, masses deposited are proportional to equivalent weights. Eq. wt of Cu = 63/2 = 31.5. Eq. wt of Ag = 108/1 = 108. Mass of Ag = (108/31.5) × 0.63 = 2.16g.

records.question: In the reaction Fe + Cu²⁺ → Fe²⁺ + Cu, iron displaces copper ions to form copper. This is due to the fact that
options: iron is in the metallic form while the copper is in the ionic form
the atomic weight of copper is greater than that of iron
copper metal has more electrons than iron metal
iron is higher in the electrochemical series than copper
records.answerText: iron is higher in the electrochemical series than copper
records.sourceExplanation: Iron is more electropositive (higher in the electrochemical series) than copper. It displaces copper from its salt solution by donating electrons to Cu²⁺ ions, which are reduced to copper metal.

records.question: The correct name of the compound with the structural formula C₂H₅-C(CH₃)=CH₂ is
records.sourceExplanation: The longest chain containing the double bond has 4 carbons (butene). The double bond is at position 1 and a methyl group is at position 2, giving 2-methylbut-1-ene.

records.question: How many isomeric forms are there for the molecular formula C₃H₆Br₂?
records.sourceExplanation: The four isomers are: 1,1-dibromopropane, 1,2-dibromopropane, 1,3-dibromopropane, and 2,2-dibromopropane.

records.question: A piece of burning sulphur will continue to burn in a gas jar of oxygen to give misty fumes which readily dissolve in water. The resulting liquid is
records.sourceExplanation: Sulphur burns in oxygen to form SO₂ (sulphur IV oxide). SO₂ dissolves in water to form sulphurous acid (H₂SO₃), which is trioxosulphate (IV) acid.

records.question: Sodium decahydrate (Na₂SO₄·10H₂O) on exposure to air loses all its water of crystallization. The process of loss is known as
records.sourceExplanation: Efflorescence is the loss of water of crystallization by a hydrated salt when exposed to air. Na₂SO₄·10H₂O loses all its water molecules and becomes anhydrous.

records.question: Which of the following happens during the electrolysis of molten sodium chloride?
records.sourceExplanation: During electrolysis of molten NaCl, Na⁺ ions are reduced at the cathode (gain electrons) and Cl⁻ ions are oxidized at the anode (lose electrons) to form chlorine gas.

records.question: Crude petroleum pollutant usually seen on some Nigerian creeks and waterways can be dispersed or removed by
options: heating the affected parts to boil off the petroleum
mechanically stirring to dissolve the petroleum in water
pouring organic solvents to dissolve the petroleum
cooling to freeze out the petroleum
records.sourceExplanation: Detergents act as emulsifiers and dispersants, breaking oil into small droplets that can be more easily degraded by microorganisms or dispersed in water.

records.question: An element is electronegative if
options: it has a tendency to exist in the gaseous form
its ions dissolve readily in water
it has a tendency to lose electrons
it has a tendency to gain electrons
records.answerText: it has a tendency to gain electrons
records.sourceExplanation: Electronegativity is the tendency of an atom to attract electrons towards itself when in a chemical bond. Elements with high electronegativity readily gain electrons.

records.question: Solution X, Y, and Z have pH values 3.0, 5.0 and 9.0 respectively. Which of the following statements is correct?
options: Y and Z are more acidic than water
Y is more acidic than X
records.sourceExplanation: pH < 7 is acidic, pH = 7 is neutral, pH > 7 is basic. Z has pH 9.0 (basic), X (pH 3.0) is most acidic, Y (pH 5.0) is acidic but less than X. Z is the least acidic (basic).

records.question: Which of these metals, Mg, Fe, Pb, and Cu will dissolve in dilute HCl?
records.sourceExplanation: Metals above hydrogen in the electrochemical series displace hydrogen from dilute acids. Mg and Fe are above hydrogen, while Pb is just below hydrogen and Cu is much below hydrogen.

records.question: Stainless steel is an alloy of
records.sourceExplanation: Stainless steel is an alloy of iron with chromium (about 10-20%) and carbon. Chromium forms a protective oxide layer on the surface, making it corrosion-resistant.

records.question: What volume of 0.50 M H₂SO₄ will exactly neutralize 20 cm³ of 0.1 M NaOH solution?
records.sourceExplanation: H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. Moles of NaOH = 0.1 × 20/1000 = 0.002 mol. Moles of H₂SO₄ = 0.002/2 = 0.001 mol. Volume = 0.001/0.5 = 0.002 L = 2.0 cm³.

records.question: Which of the following pair of gases will NOT react further with oxygen at a temperature between 30°C and 400°C?
records.sourceExplanation: NO₂ and SO₃ are already in their highest oxidation states and do not react further with oxygen under these conditions. SO₂ can be oxidized to SO₃, CO to CO₂, and H₂ to H₂O.

records.question: Some metals are extracted from their ores after some preliminary treatments by electrolysis (L), some by thermal reaction (T), and some by a combination of both processes (TL). Which set-up in the following for the extraction of iron, copper, and aluminium is correct?
records.sourceExplanation: Iron is extracted by thermal reduction (T) in blast furnace. Copper is extracted by electrolysis (L) of its ore. Aluminium is extracted by electrolysis of molten bauxite (TL).

records.question: In the preparation of some pure crystals of Cu(NO₃)₂ starting with CuO, a student gave the following statements as steps he employed. Which of these shows a flaw in his report?
options: Some CuO was reacted with excess dilute H₂SO₄
When the concentrate was cooled, crystals formed were removed by filtration
The crystals were washed with very cold water
The crystals were then allowed to dry
records.answerText: Some CuO was reacted with excess dilute H₂SO₄
records.sourceExplanation: CuO reacts with dilute H₂SO₄ to form CuSO₄, not Cu(NO₃)₂. To prepare Cu(NO₃)₂, CuO should be reacted with dilute HNO₃.

records.question: Which of the following separation processes is most likely to yield high quality ethanol (>95%) from palm wine?
records.sourceExplanation: Ethanol forms an azeotrope with water (95.6% ethanol). To obtain absolute ethanol (>95%), a dehydrating agent like quicklime (CaO) is used to remove the remaining water.

records.question: Increasing the pressure of a gas
options: lowers the average kinetic energy of the molecules
decreases the density of the gas
decreases the temperature of the gas
increases the density of the gas
increases the volume of the gas
records.answerText: increases the density of the gas
records.sourceExplanation: At constant temperature, increasing pressure compresses the gas (Boyle's law), decreasing its volume. Since density = mass/volume, the density increases.

records.question: 2.5 g of a hydrated barium salt gave on heating, 2.13 g of the anhydrous salt. Given that the relative molecular mass of the anhydrous salt is 208, the number of molecules of water of crystallization of the barium salt is
records.sourceExplanation: Mass of water lost = 2.5 - 2.13 = 0.37g. Moles of anhydrous salt = 2.13/208 = 0.0102. Moles of water = 0.37/18 = 0.0206. Ratio = 0.0206/0.0102 ≈ 2.

records.question: 3.06 g of a sample of potassium trioxochlorate (V) (KClO₃) was required to make a saturated solution with 10 cm³ of water at 25°C. The solubility of the salt at 25°C is [K=39, Cl=35.5, O=16]
records.sourceExplanation: Molar mass of KClO₃ = 39 + 35.5 + 48 = 122.5 g/mol. Moles = 3.06/122.5 = 0.025 mol. Volume = 10 cm³ = 0.01 dm³. Solubility = 0.025/0.01 = 2.5 mol/dm³.

records.question: The cracking process is very important in the petroleum industry because it
records.sourceExplanation: Cracking breaks down large hydrocarbon molecules into smaller, more volatile molecules, increasing the yield of gasoline and other engine fuels from crude oil.

records.question: A gas that can behave as a reducing agent towards chlorine and as an oxidizing agent towards hydrogen sulphide is
records.sourceExplanation: SO₂ can be oxidized (acts as reducing agent) with chlorine: SO₂ + Cl₂ + 2H₂O → H₂SO₄ + 2HCl. It can be reduced (acts as oxidizing agent) with H₂S: SO₂ + 2H₂S → 3S + 2H₂O.

records.question: Which of the following solutions will give a white precipitate with barium chloride solution and a green flame test?
records.sourceExplanation: Ca²⁺ gives a brick-red flame test, not green. Cu²⁺ gives a blue-green flame test. The white precipitate with BaCl₂ indicates the presence of SO₄²⁻ ions.

records.question: The mass of an atom is determined by
options: the number of neutrons and protons
the number of neutrons and electrons
records.answerText: the number of neutrons and protons
records.sourceExplanation:
The mass of an atom (mass number) is the sum of the number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus. Electrons have negligible mass.
# JAMB CHEMISTRY PAST QUESTIONS (42–80)

records.question: Which of the following is a neutralization reaction?
options: Addition of trioxonitrate (V) acid (nitric acid) to distilled water
Addition of trioxonitrate (V) acid (nitric acid) to tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid (sulphuric acid)
Addition of trioxonitrate (V) acid (nitric acid) to potassium hydroxide solution
records.answerText: Addition of trioxonitrate (V) acid (nitric acid) to potassium hydroxide solution
records.sourceExplanation: Neutralization is the reaction between an acid and a base to form salt and water. HNO₃ + KOH → KNO₃ + H₂O is a neutralization reaction.

records.question: A jet plane carrying 3,000 kg of ethane burns off all the gas forming water and carbon dioxide. If all the carbon dioxide is expelled and the water formed is condensed and kept on board the plane, then the gain in weight is
records.sourceExplanation: Combustion: 2C₂H₆ + 7O₂ → 4CO₂ + 6H₂O. Moles C₂H₆ = 3000/30 = 100 mol. Moles H₂O = 300 mol, mass = 5400 kg. Moles CO₂ = 200 mol, mass = 8800 kg (expelled). Plane started with 3000 kg ethane, ends with 5400 kg water on board. Gain = 5400 - 3000 = 2400 kg.

records.question: Liquid X reacts with sodium trioxocarbonate (IV) (Na₂CO₃) to give a gas which turns calcium chloride solution milky. X is
records.sourceExplanation: Acids react with Na₂CO₃ to produce CO₂ gas, which turns lime water (calcium hydroxide solution) milky, not calcium chloride. The gas is CO₂, indicating the liquid X is an acid.

records.question: Which of the following statements is FALSE?
options: Copper (II) ion can be reduced to copper (I) ion by hydrochloric acid and zinc
Sodium metal dissolves in water giving oxygen
Carbon dioxide is soluble in water
Lead has a higher atomic weight than copper
records.answerText: Sodium metal dissolves in water giving oxygen
records.sourceExplanation: Sodium reacts violently with water to produce hydrogen gas, not oxygen: 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂. The other statements are true.

records.question: When sodium dioxonitrate (III) (NaNO₂) dissolves is
records.sourceExplanation: The dissolution of sodium nitrite in water is an exothermic process, meaning heat is released. This can be observed by a temperature increase of the solution.

records.question: Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂. The rate of the above reaction will be greatly increased if
options: the zinc is in the powdered form
a greater volume of the acid is used
a smaller volume of the acid is used
the reaction vessel is immersed in an ice-bath
the zinc is in the form of pellets
records.answerText: the zinc is in the powdered form
records.sourceExplanation: Powdering a solid increases its surface area, which increases the rate of reaction by providing more contact area for the acid to react with the zinc.

records.question: Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂. In the above reaction, how much zinc will be left undissolved if 2.00 g of zinc is treated with 10 cm³ of 1.0 M H₂SO₄? [Zn = 65, S = 32, O = 16, H = 1]
records.sourceExplanation: Moles of H₂SO₄ = 1.0 × 10/1000 = 0.01 mol. Moles of Zn reacting = 0.01 mol. Mass of Zn reacting = 0.01 × 65 = 0.65 g. Mass of Zn left = 2.00 - 0.65 = 1.35 g.

records.question: 30 cm³ of 0.1 M Al(NO₃)₃ solution is reacted with 100 cm³ of 0.15 M NaOH solution. Which is in excess and by how much?
records.sourceExplanation: Al(NO₃)₃ + 3NaOH → Al(OH)₃ + 3NaNO₃. Moles Al(NO₃)₃ = 0.1 × 30/1000 = 0.003 mol. Moles NaOH needed = 0.003 × 3 = 0.009 mol. Moles NaOH available = 0.15 × 100/1000 = 0.015 mol. Excess NaOH = 0.015 - 0.009 = 0.006 mol. Volume of excess NaOH = 0.006/0.15 = 0.04 L = 40 cm³.

records.question: Sodium chloride may be obtained from brine by
records.sourceExplanation: Brine is a saturated solution of NaCl. Evaporation of water from brine leaves solid NaCl crystals behind.

records.question: 20 cm³ of hydrogen gas are sparked with 20 cm³ of oxygen gas in an eudiometer at 373 K (100°C) and 1 atmosphere. The resulting mixture is cooled to 298 K (25°C) and passed over calcium chloride. The volume of the residual gas is
records.sourceExplanation: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. 20 cm³ H₂ reacts with 10 cm³ O₂ to form water. Oxygen left = 20 - 10 = 10 cm³. At 25°C, water condenses, so residual gas is oxygen (10 cm³).

records.question: For the reaction NH₄NO₂ → N₂ + 2H₂O, calculate the volume of nitrogen that would be produced at S.T.P from 3.20 g of the trioxonitrate (III) salt. (Relative atomic masses: N = 14, O = 16, H = 1)
records.sourceExplanation: Molar mass of NH₄NO₂ = 14 + 4 + 14 + 32 = 64 g/mol. Moles = 3.20/64 = 0.05 mol. From equation, 1 mol NH₄NO₂ → 1 mol N₂. Volume N₂ at STP = 0.05 × 22.4 = 1.12 dm³.

records.question: Manganese (IV) oxide reacts with concentrated hydrochloric acid according to the equation MnO₂ + xHCl → MnCl₂ + Cl₂ + yH₂O. x and y are
records.sourceExplanation: MnO₂ + 4HCl → MnCl₂ + Cl₂ + 2H₂O. Balancing: Mn: 1 each side, O: 2 → 2H₂O, H: 4 → 4HCl, Cl: 4 → MnCl₂ (2) + Cl₂ (2). So x=4, y=2.

records.question: A molar solution of caustic soda is prepared by dissolving
options: 40 g NaOH in 100 g of water
40 g NaOH in 1000 g of water
20 g NaOH in 500 g of solution
20 g NaOH in 1000 g of solution
20 g NaOH in 80 g of solution
records.answerText: 40 g NaOH in 1000 g of water
records.sourceExplanation: A molar solution contains 1 mole of solute per 1000 cm³ (1 dm³) of solution. 1 mole NaOH = 40 g. Dissolving 40 g NaOH in enough water to make 1 dm³ of solution gives a 1 M solution.

records.question: Which among the elements: 1. Carbon, 2. Oxygen, 3. Copper, 4. Bromine, 5. Zinc will NOT react with either water or steam?
records.sourceExplanation: Copper and bromine do not react with water or steam. Carbon reacts with steam to form water gas (CO + H₂). Oxygen is slightly soluble in water. Zinc reacts with steam to form ZnO and H₂.

records.question: Which of the curves shown in fig 1 represents the relationship between the volume (v) and pressure (p) of an ideal gas at constant temperature?
records.sourceExplanation: For an ideal gas at constant temperature, PV = constant (Boyle's law). The graph of V against P is a rectangular hyperbola. Curve 1 shows this inverse relationship.

records.question: Naphthalene when heated melts at 354 K (81°C). At this temperature, the molecules of naphthalene
options: become mobile as the intermolecular forces are broken
records.answerText: become mobile as the intermolecular forces are broken
records.sourceExplanation: At melting point, the energy supplied breaks the intermolecular forces holding the molecules in a rigid lattice. The molecules become mobile (liquid state) without breaking covalent bonds.

records.question: The ratio of the number of molecules in 2g of hydrogen to that in 16 g of oxygen is
records.sourceExplanation: Moles of H₂ = 2/2 = 1 mol. Moles of O₂ = 16/32 = 0.5 mol. Number of molecules = moles × Avogadro's number. Ratio = 1 : 0.5 = 2:1.

records.question: Which combination of the following statements is correct? 1. Lowering the activation energy, 2. Conducting the reaction in a gaseous state, 3. Increasing the temperature, 4. Removing the products as soon as they are formed, 5. Powdering the reactant if solid
records.sourceExplanation: Lowering activation energy (catalyst), increasing temperature, and powdering solids increase reaction rate. Conducting in gaseous state doesn't necessarily increase rate. Removing products shifts equilibrium but doesn't increase rate.

records.question: The balanced equation for the reaction of tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid with aluminium hydroxide to give water and aluminium tetraoxosulphate (VI) is
records.sourceExplanation: Aluminium hydroxide is Al(OH)₃, aluminium tetraoxosulphate (VI) is Al₂(SO₄)₃. Balancing: 3H₂SO₄ + 2Al(OH)₃ → 6H₂O + Al₂(SO₄)₃.

records.question: The solubility curves of four substances are shown in Fig.2. Which of the four substances would crystallize from a saturated solution cooled from 353 K (80°C) to 323 K (50°C)?
records.sourceExplanation: Substances whose solubility decreases significantly with temperature will crystallize out when cooled. P and Q show large decreases in solubility between 80°C and 50°C.

records.question: Which of the following mixtures would result in a solution of pH greater than 7?
options: 25.00 cm³ of 0.05 M H₂SO₄ and 25.00 cm³ of 0.50 M Na₂CO₃
25.00 cm³ of 0.50 M H₂SO₄ and 25.00 cm³ of 0.10 M NaHCO₃
25.00 cm³ of 0.11 M H₂SO₄ and 25.00 cm³ of 0.10 M NaOH
25.00 cm³ of 0.11 M H₂SO₄ and 50.00 cm³ of 0.50 M NaOH
25.00 cm³ of 0.25 M H₂SO₄ and 50.00 cm³ of 0.20 M NaOH
records.answerText: 25.00 cm³ of 0.11 M H₂SO₄ and 50.00 cm³ of 0.50 M NaOH
records.sourceExplanation: For pH > 7, base must be in excess. Calculate moles of H⁺ and OH⁻. In D: moles H⁺ = 0.11 × 25/1000 × 2 = 0.0055 mol. Moles OH⁻ = 0.50 × 50/1000 = 0.025 mol. Excess OH⁻ = 0.0195 mol, pH > 7.

records.question: In which of the following reactions does hydrogen peroxide act as a reducing agent?
records.sourceExplanation: In this reaction, H₂O₂ is oxidized to O₂ (oxygen in H₂O₂ goes from -1 to 0), so it acts as a reducing agent. In others, H₂O₂ is reduced, acting as an oxidizing agent.

records.question: For the reaction 2Fe³⁺ + 2e⁻ → 2Fe²⁺ + I₂, which of the following statements is TRUE?
records.sourceExplanation: In the reaction 2Fe³⁺ + 2I⁻ → 2Fe²⁺ + I₂, Fe³⁺ gains electrons (reduction), and I⁻ loses electrons (oxidation). I⁻ is oxidized to I₂.

records.question: The diagram above (Fig.3) shows the energy profile for the reaction A + B → C + D. From this diagram, it's clear that the reaction is
records.sourceExplanation: If the products have lower energy than the reactants, the reaction is exothermic. The energy profile shows ΔH = energy of products - energy of reactants is negative.

records.question: In dilute solution, the heat of the following NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O and 2NaOH + H₂SO₄ → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O is
records.sourceExplanation: The heat of neutralization of a strong acid and strong base is approximately -57.3 kJ per mole of water formed. The reactions show formation of 1 mole and 2 moles of water respectively.

records.question: For the reactions: (I) Melon oil + NaOH → Soap + Glycerol, (II) 3Fe + 4H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + 4H₂, (III) N₂O₄ ⇌ 2NO₂. Which of the following statements is true?
options: Each of the three reactions requires a catalyst
All the reactions demonstrate Le Chatelier's principle
The presence of a catalyst will increase the yield of products
Increase in pressure will result in higher yields of the products in I and II only
Increase in pressure will result in higher yields of the products in III only
records.answerText: Increase in pressure will result in higher yields of the products in III only
records.sourceExplanation: In reaction III, increasing pressure favors the side with fewer moles of gas (N₂O₄). In reaction I, pressure has no effect (no gases). In reaction II, pressure has little effect on solids.

records.question: Which of the following methods may be used to prepare trioxonitrate (V) acid (nitric acid) in the laboratory?
options: Heating ammonia gas with tetraoxosulphate (IV) acid
Heating ammonium trioxosulphate (V) with tetraoxonitrate (V) acid
Heating sodium trioxonitrate (V) with tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid
Heating potassium trioxonitrate (V) with calcium hydroxide
Heating a mixture of ammonia gas and oxygen
records.answerText: Heating sodium trioxonitrate (V) with tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid
records.sourceExplanation: Nitric acid is prepared in the lab by heating sodium nitrate (NaNO₃) with concentrated sulphuric acid: NaNO₃ + H₂SO₄ → NaHSO₄ + HNO₃.

records.question: Lime-water, which is used in the laboratory for the detection of carbon (IV) oxide, is an aqueous solution of:
records.sourceExplanation: Lime water is a saturated solution of calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)₂. It turns milky when CO₂ is bubbled through it due to formation of insoluble CaCO₃.

records.question: An element that can exist in two or more different structure forms which possess the same chemical properties is said to exhibit
records.sourceExplanation: Allotropy is the existence of an element in two or more different physical forms in the same physical state, with different structures but same chemical properties.

records.question: Sulphur...
options: Conducts electricity in the molten state
Is usually stored in the form of sticks in water
records.sourceExplanation: Sulphur burns in air with a pale blue flame to form sulphur dioxide (SO₂). It does not conduct electricity and is not stored in water.

records.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true of carbon monoxide?
options: CO is readily oxidized at room temperature by air to form CO₂
CO may be prepared by reducing CO₂ with coke heated to about 1000°C
CO may be prepared by heating charcoal with a limited amount of O₂
CO is a good reducing agent
records.answerText: CO is readily oxidized at room temperature by air to form CO₂
records.sourceExplanation: CO does not readily oxidize at room temperature. It burns with a blue flame when heated. The other statements are true.

records.question: From the reactions: ZnO + Na₂O → Na₂ZnO₂ and ZnO + CO₂ → ZnCO₃, it may be concluded that zinc oxide is
records.sourceExplanation: ZnO reacts with both basic oxide (Na₂O) and acidic oxide (CO₂), showing amphoteric properties. It can act as both an acid and a base.

records.question: An example of a neutral oxide is
records.sourceExplanation: Neutral oxides are neither acidic nor basic. CO is a neutral oxide. Al₂O₃ is amphoteric, NO₂ and CO₂ are acidic, SO₂ is acidic.

records.question: 3Cl₂ + 2NH₃ → N₂ + 6HCl. In the above reaction, ammonia acts as
records.sourceExplanation: In this reaction, ammonia is oxidized (nitrogen goes from -3 to 0). It reduces chlorine (Cl₂ to Cl⁻). Therefore, ammonia acts as a reducing agent.

records.question: In the Haber process for the manufacture of ammonia, finely divided iron is used as
records.sourceExplanation: In the Haber process, finely divided iron acts as a catalyst to increase the rate of reaction between nitrogen and hydrogen to form ammonia.

records.question: An organic compound with a vapour density 56.5 has the following percentage composition: C = 53.1%, N = 12.4%, O = 28.3%, H = 6.2%. The molecular formula of the compound is
records.sourceExplanation: Empirical formula: C = 53.1/12 = 4.425, H = 6.2/1 = 6.2, O = 28.3/16 = 1.769, N = 12.4/14 = 0.886. Divide by smallest (0.886): C = 5, H = 7, O = 2, N = 1. Molecular mass = 2 × vapour density = 2 × 56.5 = 113. Empirical mass = (5×12)+(7×1)+(2×16)+(1×14) = 60+7+32+14 = 113. So molecular formula = C₅H₇NO₂, which is not in the options. The closest option is C. (C₃H₄O₂N)₂. Given the options, C is the intended answer.

records.question: The hybridization of the carbon atom in ethylene is
records.sourceExplanation: In ethylene (C₂H₄), each carbon atom forms three sigma bonds (two with H, one with C) and one pi bond. This requires sp² hybridization with trigonal planar geometry.

records.question: When the kerosene fraction from petrol is heated at high temperature, a lower boiling liquid is obtained. This process is known as
records.sourceExplanation:
Cracking is the process of breaking down larger hydrocarbon molecules into smaller, more volatile ones by heating at high temperatures.
# JAMB CHEMISTRY PAST QUESTIONS (81–150)

records.question: The compound CH₃COOH is
records.sourceExplanation: CH₃COOH is ethanoic acid (also known as acetic acid). The IUPAC name is ethanoic acid.

records.question: Alkaline hydrolysis of naturally occurring fats and oils yields
records.sourceExplanation: Saponification (alkaline hydrolysis) of fats and oils produces soap (sodium salts of fatty acids) and glycerol.

records.question: Which of the following represents a carboxylic acid?
records.sourceExplanation: Carboxylic acids have the functional group -COOH (carboxyl group). R-COOH represents a carboxylic acid.

records.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: Fractional distillation of crude petroleum will give the following hydrocarbon fuels in order of increasing boiling point: Butane < Petrol < Kerosene
H₂C=CH₂ will serve as a monomer in the preparation of polythene
Both but-1-ene and but-1-yne will decolorize bromine readily
But-2-ene will react with chlorine to form 2,3-dichlorobutane
Calcium carbide will react with water to form any alkane
records.answerText: Calcium carbide will react with water to form any alkane
records.sourceExplanation: Calcium carbide reacts with water to produce ethyne (acetylene), not any alkane. The reaction is CaC₂ + 2H₂O → C₂H₂ + Ca(OH)₂.

records.question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about all four of the acids: HBr, HNO₃, H₂CO₃, and H₂SO₄? They
options: react with magnesium to liberate hydrogen
records.answerText: react with magnesium to liberate hydrogen
records.sourceExplanation: HBr, HNO₃, and H₂SO₄ react with magnesium to liberate hydrogen, but H₂CO₃ (carbonic acid) is weak and does not readily react with magnesium to liberate hydrogen.

records.question: If the cost of electricity required to deposit 1 g of magnesium is N5.00. How much would it cost to deposit 10 g of aluminium? (Relative atomic masses: Al = 27, Mg = 24)
records.sourceExplanation: Equivalent weight of Mg = 24/2 = 12. Equivalent weight of Al = 27/3 = 9. Cost is proportional to number of equivalents. For 10 g Al: equivalents = 10/9. For 1 g Mg: equivalents = 1/12. Cost = (10/9) / (1/12) × 5 = (10/9 × 12) × 5 = (120/9) × 5 = 13.33 × 5 = N66.67.

records.question: In an experiment, copper tetraoxosulphate (VI) solution was electrolysed using copper electrodes. The mass of copper deposited at the cathode by the passage of 16000 coulombs of electricity is (Relative atomic masses: Cu = 63.5)
records.sourceExplanation: Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu. Charge = 16000 C. Moles of electrons = 16000/96500 = 0.1658 mol. Moles of Cu = 0.1658/2 = 0.0829 mol. Mass = 0.0829 × 63.5 = 5.26 g. However, the options given include 10.67 g, which is double (maybe using Cu⁺). Since the question says copper electrodes, the deposition could be Cu²⁺, but the answer expected is D. 10.67 g, likely using a different calculation. I'll go with D as per the source.

records.question: R¹⁹, U²⁴, S²⁰, T¹⁹. Which of the following statements is NOT true of the elements R, U, S, T, Y?
options: R is an isotope of hydrogen
R, U, S and T are metals
S will react with oxygen to form SO₂
records.sourceExplanation: R and T have atomic number 19 (potassium, a metal). U is chromium (metal), S is calcium (metal). None are noble gases. So D is false.

records.question: Nitrogen can best be obtained from a mixture of oxygen and nitrogen by passing the mixture over
records.sourceExplanation: Phosphorus reacts with oxygen to form phosphorus pentoxide (P₂O₅), leaving nitrogen gas. This is a common method to remove oxygen from air.

records.question: Water is said to be hard if it
options: has to be warmed before sodium chloride dissolves in it
forms an insoluble scum with soap
records.answerText: forms an insoluble scum with soap
records.sourceExplanation: Hard water contains Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions which react with soap to form insoluble precipitates (scum). This is the characteristic test for hard water.

records.question: Sodium hydroxide (NaOH) pellets are
records.sourceExplanation: NaOH pellets absorb moisture from the atmosphere and dissolve in it to form a solution. This property is called deliquescence.

records.question: A piece of sea shell, when dropped into a dilute solution of hydrochloric acid produces a colourless odorless gas, which turns clear limewater milky. The shell contains
records.sourceExplanation: Sea shells are made of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃). It reacts with HCl to produce CO₂ gas, which turns lime water milky.

records.question: Alkanes
records.sourceExplanation: Alkanes are hydrocarbons containing only carbon and hydrogen. They have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ and are generally unreactive.

records.question: If an excess of a liquid hydrocarbon is poured into a jar of chlorine, and the sealed jar is then exposed for several hours to bright sunlight, all the chlorine gas is consumed. The hydrocarbon is said to have undergone
records.sourceExplanation: Alkanes undergo substitution reactions with halogens in the presence of light. Hydrogen atoms in the hydrocarbon are replaced by chlorine atoms.

records.question: The function of conc. H₂SO₄ in the esterification of ethanoic acid with ethanol is to
records.sourceExplanation: Concentrated H₂SO₄ acts as a catalyst in the esterification reaction between ethanoic acid and ethanol. It also absorbs water, shifting equilibrium to the right.

records.question: An aqueous solution of a metal salt M gives a white precipitate with NaOH, which dissolves in excess NaOH. With aqueous ammonia, the solution of M also gives a white precipitate which dissolves in excess ammonia. Therefore, the cation in M is
records.sourceExplanation: Zn²⁺ gives white precipitates with NaOH and NH₃ which dissolve in excess of both reagents due to formation of soluble complex ions (zincates and ammines).

records.question: The IUPAC name for the compound (CH₃)₂CH-CH₂-CH₃ is
records.sourceExplanation: The longest chain has 4 carbons (butane). A methyl group is attached at carbon 2. So the name is 2-methylbutane.

records.question: At S.T.P, how many litres of hydrogen can be obtained from the reaction of 500 cm³ of 0.5 M H₂SO₄ with excess zinc metal? (Gram molecular volume of H₂ = 22.4 dm³)
records.sourceExplanation: Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂. Moles H₂SO₄ = 0.5 × 500/1000 = 0.25 mol. Moles H₂ = 0.25 mol. Volume H₂ at STP = 0.25 × 22.4 = 5.6 dm³.

records.question: Figure shows part of the periodic Table. Which of the elements belongs to the p-block?
records.sourceExplanation: Elements in groups IIIA to VIIA (13-17) are p-block elements. The figure shows groups I to VII with p-block elements likely being in groups III-VII.

records.question: Which of the following conducts electricity?
records.sourceExplanation: Graphite has delocalized electrons that can move freely, making it a good conductor of electricity. Diamond does not conduct electricity.

records.question: An organic compound contains 72% carbon, 12% hydrogen and 16% oxygen by mass. The empirical formula of the compound is
records.sourceExplanation: C = 72/12 = 6, H = 12/1 = 12, O = 16/16 = 1. Ratio C:H:O = 6:12:1. Empirical formula = C₆H₁₂O.

records.question: 0.499 g of CuSO₄·xH₂O when heated to constant weight gave a residue of 0.346 g. The value of x is [Cu=63.5, S=32.0, O=16, H=1]
In an experiment, which of the following observations would suggest that a solid sample is a mixture? The
options: solid can be ground to a fine powder
density of the solid is 2.25 g/dm³
solid begins to melt until 648 K
solid absorbs moisture from the atmosphere and turns into a liquid
records.answerText: solid begins to melt until 648 K
records.sourceExplanation: A pure solid has a sharp melting point. A mixture melts over a range of temperatures. "Begins to melt until" indicates a range, suggesting a mixture.

records.question: Hydrogen diffuses through a porous plug
options: at the same rate as oxygen
at a slower rate than oxygen
three times as fast as oxygen
four times as fast as oxygen
records.answerText: four times as fast as oxygen
records.sourceExplanation: According to Graham's law, rate ∝ 1/√M. Rate H₂/Rate O₂ = √(M_O₂/M_H₂) = √(32/2) = √16 = 4. So hydrogen diffuses 4 times as fast as oxygen.

records.question: Given the molecular mass of iron is 56 and that of oxygen is 16, how many moles of Iron (III) oxide will be contained in 1 kg of the compound?
records.sourceExplanation: Fe₂O₃ molar mass = 2×56 + 3×16 = 112 + 48 = 160 g/mol. Moles = 1000/160 = 6.25 mol.

records.question: 3.0 g of a mixture of potassium carbonate and potassium chloride were dissolved in a 250 cm³ standard flask. 25 cm³ of this solution required 40.00 cm³ of 0.1 M HCl for neutralization. What is the percentage by weight of K₂CO₃ in the mixture? (K=39, O=16, C=12)
records.sourceExplanation: K₂CO₃ + 2HCl → 2KCl + CO₂ + H₂O. Moles HCl used = 0.1 × 40/1000 = 0.004 mol. Moles K₂CO₃ in 25 cm³ = 0.004/2 = 0.002 mol. Moles K₂CO₃ in 250 cm³ = 0.002 × 10 = 0.02 mol. Mass K₂CO₃ = 0.02 × 138 = 2.76 g. Percentage = 2.76/3.0 × 100 = 92%.

records.question: Figure 2 below represents the solubility curves of two salts, X and Y, in water. At room temperature (300 K)
options: Y is twice as soluble as X
X is twice as soluble as Y
X and Y are soluble to the same extent
X is three times as soluble as Y
Y is three times as soluble as X
records.answerText: X and Y are soluble to the same extent
records.sourceExplanation: At 300 K (room temperature), the solubility curves intersect, meaning both salts have the same solubility.

records.question: If 80 g each of X and Y are taken up in 100 g of water at 353 K, we shall have
options: only 10 g of X and Y undissolve
10 g of X and 16 g of Y undissolved
records.answerText: 10 g of X and 16 g of Y undissolved
records.sourceExplanation: At 353 K, solubility of X is 70 g/100g water and Y is 64 g/100g water. So 10 g of X and 16 g of Y will remain undissolved.

records.question: If the molar mass of X is 36 g, the number of moles of X dissolved at 343 K is
records.sourceExplanation: At 343 K, solubility of X is about 70 g/100g water. In 100 g water, 70 g dissolves. Moles = 70/36 = 1.94 ≈ 2.0 moles.

records.question: Some properties of chemical substances are mentioned below: (i) sour taste (ii) slippery to touch (iii) yields alkaline gas with ammonium salts (iv) has pH less than 7 (v) turns phenolphthalein pink. Which of the above are NOT typical properties of alkalis?
records.sourceExplanation: Alkalis have bitter taste (not sour), slippery feel, turn phenolphthalein pink, pH > 7, and react with ammonium salts to give NH₃ gas. Sour taste and pH < 7 are properties of acids.

records.question: A certain volume of a gas at 298 K is heated such that its volume and pressure are now four times the original values. What is the new temperature?
records.sourceExplanation: Using PV/T = constant. New P = 4P, new V = 4V. (4P × 4V)/T₂ = PV/T₁ → 16PV/T₂ = PV/298 → T₂ = 16 × 298 = 4768 K.

records.question: Hydrogen is not liberated when trioxonitrate (V) acid reacts with zinc because
options: Zinc is rendered passive by the acid
Hydrogen produced is oxidized to water
All nitrates are soluble in water
Trioxonitrate (V) acid is a strong acid
records.sourceExplanation: Nitric acid is a strong oxidizing agent. When it reacts with metals like zinc, hydrogen produced is oxidized to water, and oxides of nitrogen (NO, NO₂) are formed instead.

records.question: The boiling points of water, ethanol, toluene and butan-2-ol are 373.0 K, 351.3 K, 383.6 K and 372.5 K respectively. Which liquid has the highest vapour pressure at 323.0 K?
records.sourceExplanation: The liquid with the lowest boiling point has the highest vapour pressure at a given temperature. Ethanol has the lowest boiling point (351.3 K), so it has the highest vapour pressure at 323.0 K.

records.question: In what respect will two dry samples of nitrogen gas differ from each other if sample 1 is prepared by completely removing CO₂ and O₂ from air and sample 2 is prepared by passing purified nitrogen (I) oxide over heated copper? Sample 1 is
options: in all respects the same as sample 2
colourless but sample 2 has a light brown colour
records.sourceExplanation: Nitrogen from air contains small amounts of rare gases (argon, etc.), making it slightly denser than pure nitrogen prepared from nitrogen compounds.

records.question: Copper sulphate solution is electrolyzed using platinum electrodes. A current of 0.193 amperes is passed for 2 hrs. How many grams of copper are deposited? (Cu=63.5, F=96500 coulombs)
X + Y ⇌ Z is an equilibrium reaction. The addition of a catalyst
options: increases the amount of W produced in a given time
increases the rate of change in concentrations of X, Y and Z
increases the rate of disappearance of X and Y
increases the rate of the forward reaction
decreases the amounts of X and Y left after the attainment of equilibrium
records.answerText: increases the rate of change in concentrations of X, Y and Z
records.sourceExplanation: A catalyst increases the rate of both forward and reverse reactions equally, so equilibrium is reached faster. It does not affect the position of equilibrium.

records.question: What is the formula of sodium gallate if gallium (Ga) shows an oxidation number of +3?
records.sourceExplanation: Gallium in +3 oxidation state forms complex hydroxide. NaGa(OH)₄ has Ga in +3: +1 + x + 4(-1) = 0 → x = +3. So D is correct for a gallate complex.

records.question: If the ONLY pollutants found in the atmosphere over a city are oxides of nitrogen, suspended lead compounds, carbon monoxide and high level of methane, the probable source(s) of the pollution must be
options: combustion of coal and automobile exhaust
combustion of coal, automobile exhaust and biological decomposition
combustion of coal and biological decomposition
records.sourceExplanation: Automobile exhaust produces oxides of nitrogen, lead compounds, and CO. Biological decomposition produces methane. Coal combustion would also produce SO₂, which is not listed.

records.question: A correct electrochemical series can be obtained from K, Na, Ca, Al, Mg, Zn, Fe, Pb, H, Cu, Hg, Ag, Au by interchanging
records.sourceExplanation:
In the correct electrochemical series, Mg is above Al. The given order has Al before Mg, which is incorrect. Interchanging them gives the correct series.
# JAMB CHEMISTRY PAST QUESTIONS (121–200)

records.question: A certain industrial process is represented by the chemical equation 2A(g) + B(g) → C(g) + 3D(g), ΔH = +X kJ/mol. Which of the following conditions will favour the yield of the product?
options: Increase in temperature, decrease in pressure
Increase in temperature, increase in pressure
Decrease in temperature, increase in pressure
Decrease in temperature, increase in pressure
records.answerText: Increase in temperature, decrease in pressure
records.sourceExplanation: ΔH is positive (endothermic), so increasing temperature favors products. The reaction has 2+1=3 moles gas on left and 1+3=4 moles on right. Decreasing pressure favors the side with more gas moles (products).

records.question: 2MnO₄⁻ + 10Cl⁻ + 16H⁺ → 2Mn²⁺ + 5Cl₂ + 8H₂O, which of the substances serves as an oxidizing agent?
records.sourceExplanation: MnO₄⁻ is reduced to Mn²⁺ (Mn goes from +7 to +2), so it acts as the oxidizing agent. It gains electrons from Cl⁻ (which is oxidized to Cl₂).

records.question: In the reaction H₂O(g) + C(s) → H₂(g) + CO(g), ΔH = -243600 kJ, which of the following has no effect on the equilibrium position?
records.sourceExplanation: Adding an inert gas like argon at constant volume does not change the partial pressures of the reactants/products, so it has no effect on equilibrium.

records.question: Which of the following metals will displace iron from a solution of iron(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI)?
records.sourceExplanation: Zinc is more electropositive than iron and will displace iron from its salt solution: Zn + FeSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Fe.

records.question: Complete hydrogenation of ethyne yields
records.sourceExplanation: Ethyne (C₂H₂) with excess H₂ in the presence of a catalyst undergoes complete hydrogenation to ethane (C₂H₆): C₂H₂ + 2H₂ → C₂H₆.

records.question: Which of the following is used in the manufacture of bleaching powder?
records.sourceExplanation: Bleaching powder (calcium oxychloride) is made by passing chlorine gas over slaked lime: Ca(OH)₂ + Cl₂ → CaOCl₂ + H₂O.

records.question: When pollen grains are suspended in water and viewed through a microscope, they appear to be in a state of constant but erratic motion. This is due to
options: a chemical reaction between the pollen grains and water
the bombardment of the pollen grains by molecules of water
records.answerText: the bombardment of the pollen grains by molecules of water
records.sourceExplanation: This is Brownian motion, caused by the random collision of water molecules with the pollen grains. It provides evidence for the kinetic theory of matter.

records.question: The energy change (ΔH) for the reaction CO(g) + ½O₂(g) → CO₂(g) is [ΔHf(CO) = -110.4 kJ/mol, ΔHf(CO₂) = -393 kJ/mol]
The neutralization reaction between NaOH solution and nitrogen (IV) oxide (NO₂) produces water and
records.sourceExplanation: NO₂ reacts with NaOH to form sodium nitrite and sodium nitrate: 2NO₂ + 2NaOH → NaNO₂ + NaNO₃ + H₂O.

records.question: The compound with the formula CH₃COCH₂CH₃ is
records.sourceExplanation: CH₃COCH₂CH₃ has a carbonyl group (C=O) at carbon 2 of the butane chain, making it 2-butanone (a ketone).

records.question: Tetraoxosulphate (VI) ions are finally tested using
records.sourceExplanation: SO₄²⁻ ions give a white precipitate of BaSO₄ with BaCl₂ solution, which is insoluble in dilute HCl or HNO₃. Acidified barium chloride is the confirmatory test.

records.question: The IUPAC name for the compound CH₃-CH(CH₃)-CH=CH-CH₃ is
records.sourceExplanation: Longest chain containing double bond has 5 carbons (pentene). Double bond at position 3, methyl at position 2. Name: 2-methylpent-3-ene.

records.question: Mixing of aqueous solution of barium hydroxide and sodium tetraoxocarbonate(IV) yields a white precipitate of
records.sourceExplanation: Ba(OH)₂ + Na₂CO₃ → BaCO₃ (white precipitate) + 2NaOH. The precipitate is barium carbonate.

records.question: An organic compound decolorized acidified KMnO₄ solution but failed to react with ammoniacal silver nitrate solution. The organic compound is likely to be
records.sourceExplanation: Alkenes decolorize acidified KMnO₄ (Baeyer's test) due to oxidation of the double bond. They do not react with ammoniacal silver nitrate (which is a test for terminal alkynes).

records.question: Solid sodium hydroxide on exposure to air absorbs a gas and ultimately gives another alkaline substance with the molecular formula
records.sourceExplanation: NaOH absorbs CO₂ from air to form sodium carbonate: 2NaOH + CO₂ → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O.

records.question: Which of the following is the functional group of carboxylic acids?
records.sourceExplanation: The functional group of carboxylic acids is the carboxyl group, -COOH (or -C(=O)OH).

records.question: Which of the following substances is the most abundant in the universe?
records.sourceExplanation: Hydrogen is the most abundant element in the universe, making up about 75% of its mass.

records.question: Compound X is
records.sourceExplanation: X does not decolorize bromine (so not unsaturated). It burns to give CO₂ (Y) which turns lime water milky, and H₂O (Z) which gives blue colour with anhydrous CuSO₄. X is an alkane.

records.question: Y and Z are respectively
records.sourceExplanation: Combustion of hydrocarbons in excess oxygen produces CO₂ and H₂O. CO₂ turns lime water milky, and H₂O turns anhydrous CuSO₄ blue.

records.question: Which of the following compounds is NOT the correct product formed when the parent metal is heated in air?
records.sourceExplanation: Sodium reacts with oxygen to form sodium peroxide (Na₂O₂), not sodium oxide (Na₂O), when heated in excess air.

records.question: The atomic number of an element whose cation, X²⁺ has the ground state electronic configuration 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p⁶ is
records.sourceExplanation: X²⁺ has 18 electrons (configuration for Ar). The neutral atom X has 18 + 2 = 20 electrons, so atomic number is 20 (Calcium).

records.question: When marble is heated to 1473 K, another white solid is obtained which reacts vigorously with water to give an alkaline solution. The solution contains
records.sourceExplanation: Marble is CaCO₃. Heating gives CaO (quicklime). CaO reacts with water to form Ca(OH)₂ (slaked lime), which is alkaline.

records.question: Addition of dilute hydrochloric acid to an aqueous solution of a crystalline salt yielded a yellow precipitate and a gas which turned dichromate paper green. The crystalline salt was probably
records.sourceExplanation: Thiosulphate reacts with HCl to give sulphur (yellow precipitate) and SO₂ gas (turns dichromate paper green): S₂O₃²⁻ + 2H⁺ → S + SO₂ + H₂O.

records.question: The process involved in the conversion of an oil into margarine is known as
records.sourceExplanation: Margarine is made by hydrogenating vegetable oils (adding hydrogen to unsaturated fats) in the presence of a nickel catalyst.

records.question: An aqueous solution of an inorganic salt gave white precipitate (i) soluble in excess aqueous NaOH, (ii) insoluble in excess aqueous NH₃, (iii) with dilute HCl. The cation present in the inorganic salt is
records.sourceExplanation: Pb²⁺ gives white precipitate with NaOH which dissolves in excess (amphoteric). With NH₃, precipitate is insoluble in excess (unlike Zn²⁺). With HCl, gives PbCl₂ precipitate.

records.question: Which of the following roles does sodium chloride play in soap preparation? It
options: accelerates the decomposition of the fat and oil
separates the soap from the glycerol
converts the fat acid to its sodium salt
records.answerText: separates the soap from the glycerol
records.sourceExplanation: Sodium chloride (salting out) is added to the soap mixture to decrease the solubility of soap, causing it to separate from the glycerol layer.

records.question: The function of sulphur during the vulcanization of rubber is to
options: act as catalyst for the polymerization of rubber molecules
convert rubber from thermosetting to thermoplastic polymer
form chains which bind rubber molecules together
shorten the chain length of rubber polymer
records.answerText: form chains which bind rubber molecules together
records.sourceExplanation: Sulphur forms cross-links (bridges) between rubber polymer chains, making the rubber stronger, more elastic, and less sticky.

records.question: The movement of liquid molecules from the surface of the liquid to the gaseous phase above it is known as
records.sourceExplanation: Evaporation is the process by which molecules escape from the surface of a liquid into the gas phase.

records.question: What mass of a divalent metal M (atomic mass = 40) would react with excess hydrochloric acid to liberate 22 cm³ of dry hydrogen gas measured at S.T.P? (G.M.V = 22.4 dm³)
records.sourceExplanation: M + 2HCl → MCl₂ + H₂. Moles H₂ = 0.022/22.4 = 9.82 × 10⁻⁴ mol. Moles M = 9.82 × 10⁻⁴ mol. Mass = 9.82 × 10⁻⁴ × 40 = 0.039 g ≈ 0.04 g. The closest option is D (0.4 g might be a typo, expected 0.04 g).

records.question: 10 cm³ of hydrogen fluoride gas reacts with 5 cm³ of dinitrogen difluoride gas (N₂F₂) to form 10 cm³ of a single gas. Which of the following is the most likely equation for the reaction?
records.sourceExplanation: Volume ratios: 10:5:10 = 2:1:2. So 2 volumes HF react with 1 volume N₂F₂ to give 2 volumes of product. Equation: 2HF + N₂F₂ → 2NHF₂.

records.question: The number of atoms of chlorine present in 5.85 g of NaCl is [Na=23, Cl=35.5, Avogadro's Number = 6.02 × 10²³]
records.sourceExplanation: Moles NaCl = 5.85/58.5 = 0.1 mol. Molecules NaCl = 0.1 × 6.02 × 10²³ = 6.02 × 10²². Each molecule has 1 Cl atom, so atoms Cl = 6.02 × 10²².

records.question: How much of magnesium is required to react with 250 cm³ of 0.5 M HCl? [Mg=24]
records.sourceExplanation: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂. Moles HCl = 0.5 × 250/1000 = 0.125 mol. Moles Mg = 0.125/2 = 0.0625 mol. Mass Mg = 0.0625 × 24 = 1.5 g.

records.question: 200 cm³ of oxygen diffuse through a porous plug in 50 seconds. How long will 80 cm³ of methane (CH₄) take to diffuse through the same porous plug under the same conditions? [C=12, O=16, H=1]
records.sourceExplanation: Rate O₂ = 200/50 = 4 cm³/s. Rate CH₄ = Rate O₂ × √(M_O₂/M_CH₄) = 4 × √(32/16) = 4 × √2 = 5.66 cm³/s. Time = 80/5.66 = 14.14 s ≈ 14 s.

records.question: The relationship between the velocity (u) of gas molecules and their relative molecular mass (M) is shown by the equation
records.sourceExplanation: From kinetic theory, u ∝ 1/√M. So u = k/√M = (k²/M)^(1/2). Option D is u = (k/M)^(1/2) which is equivalent.

records.question: An element with atomic number twelve is likely to be
records.sourceExplanation: Atomic number 12 is Magnesium (Mg). It has 2 valence electrons (3s²) and tends to lose them to form Mg²⁺ ions, forming electrovalent (ionic) compounds with valency 2.

records.question: Ionization energy, 2. Atomic radius, 3. Electronegativity, 4. Electron affinity
records.sourceExplanation: Across a period, electronegativity and electron affinity generally increase. Ionization energy also increases, but atomic radius decreases. So 3 and 4 increase.

records.question: When 50 cm³ of a saturated solution of sugar (molar mass 342.0 g) at 40°C was evaporated to dryness, 34.2 g dry solid was obtained. The solubility of sugar at 40°C is
records.sourceExplanation: Moles sugar = 34.2/342 = 0.1 mol. Volume = 50 cm³ = 0.05 dm³. Solubility = 0.1/0.05 = 2.0 mol/dm³.

records.question: Which of the following is an acid salt?
records.sourceExplanation: An acid salt contains replaceable hydrogen atoms. NaHSO₄ (sodium hydrogen sulphate) still has one acidic hydrogen that can be replaced.

records.question: Which of the following solutions will conduct the least amount of electricity?
options: 0.01 M aqueous solution of hexanoic acid
records.sourceExplanation: Sugar is a non-electrolyte (does not ionize), so its solution conducts electricity very poorly. Acids and bases conduct electricity due to ions.

records.question: In the electrolysis of aqueous solution of K₂SO₄ in the above cell, which species migrate to the anode?
records.sourceExplanation: Anions (negative ions) migrate to the anode (positive electrode). SO₄²⁻ and OH⁻ are the anions present.

records.question: How many coulombs of electricity are passed through a solution in which 6.5 amperes are allowed to run for 1.0 hour?
Which of these represents a redox reaction?
records.sourceExplanation: Redox reaction involves both oxidation and reduction. Zn (0) changes to Zn²⁺ (+2) (oxidation), and H⁺ (+1) changes to H₂ (0) (reduction).

records.question: How many electrons are transferred in reducing one atom of Mn in the reaction MnO₂ + 4HCl → MnCl₂ + 2H₂O + Cl₂?
records.sourceExplanation: Mn in MnO₂ has oxidation state +4. In MnCl₂, Mn has +2. Change is +4 to +2, so it gains 2 electrons.

records.question: 20 cm³ of 0.1 mol NH₄OH solution when neutralized with 20.05 cm³ of 0.1 mol HCl liberated 102 Joules of heat. Calculate the heat of neutralization of NH₄OH.
records.sourceExplanation: Moles = 0.1 × 20/1000 = 0.002 mol. Heat liberated = 102 J = 0.102 kJ. Heat per mole = 0.102/0.002 = 51 kJ/mol. Since heat is released, ΔH = -51 kJ/mol.

records.question: What is the consequence of increasing pressure on the equilibrium reaction ZnO(s) + H₂(g) ⇌ Zn(s) + H₂O(g)?
options: The equilibrium is driven to the left
The equilibrium is driven to the right
records.sourceExplanation:
The reaction has equal moles of gas on both sides (1 mol H₂ and 1 mol H₂O). Changing pressure does not affect equilibrium.
# JAMB CHEMISTRY PAST QUESTIONS (170–250)

records.question: The approximate volume of air containing 10 cm³ of oxygen is
records.sourceExplanation: Air contains approximately 20% oxygen by volume. So 10 cm³ oxygen is present in 10/0.2 = 50 cm³ of air.

records.question: The reaction Mg + H₂O → MgO + H₂ takes place only in the presence of
records.sourceExplanation: Magnesium reacts with steam (not liquid water) to produce MgO and H₂. The reaction with cold water is very slow.

records.question: When steam is passed through red hot carbon, which of the following are produced?
records.sourceExplanation: C + H₂O → CO + H₂ (water gas). This is the industrial production of water gas.

records.question: Which of the following contains an efflorescent, a deliquescent and a hygroscopic substance respectively?
records.sourceExplanation: Na₂CO₃·10H₂O is efflorescent (loses water), FeCl₃ is deliquescent (absorbs moisture and dissolves), concentrated H₂SO₄ is hygroscopic (absorbs moisture).

records.question: The tabulated results below were obtained by titrating 10.0 cm³ of water with soap. The titration was repeated with the same sample of water after boiling. | | Before boiling | After boiling | |---|---|---| | Final (cm³) | 25.0 | 20.0 | | Initial (cm³) | 10.0 | 15.0 | The ratio of permanent to temporary hardness is
records.sourceExplanation: Volume of soap used before boiling = 25.0 - 10.0 = 15.0 cm³ (total hardness). After boiling = 20.0 - 15.0 = 5.0 cm³ (permanent hardness). Temporary hardness = 15 - 5 = 10 cm³. Ratio permanent:temporary = 5:10 = 1:2. Not in options. I'll go with C as per source.

records.question: The exhaust fumes from a garage that uses petrol of high sulphur content are bound to contain
records.sourceExplanation: Petrol with high sulphur content produces SO₂ and SO₃ upon combustion, along with CO from incomplete combustion.

records.question: Oxygen-demanding wastes are considered to be a water pollutant because they
options: deplete oxygen which is necessary for the survival of aquatic organisms
increase oxygen which is necessary for the survival of aquatic organisms
increase other gaseous species which are necessary for survival of aquatic organisms
deplete other gaseous species which are necessary for the survival of aquatic organisms
records.answerText: deplete oxygen which is necessary for the survival of aquatic organisms
records.sourceExplanation: Oxygen-demanding wastes consume dissolved oxygen in water during their decomposition, reducing the oxygen available for aquatic life.

records.question: Which of the following will react further with oxygen to form a higher oxide?
records.sourceExplanation: SO₂ can be oxidized to SO₃, and NO can be oxidized to NO₂. CO₂ and H₂O are already in their highest oxidation states.

records.question: In the course of an experiment, two gases X and Y were produced. X turned wet lead ethanoate paper black and Y bleached moist litmus paper. What are the elements in each of the gases X and Y respectively?
options: H and S; C and O
H and Cl; S and O
records.sourceExplanation: X is H₂S (turns lead ethanoate black). Y is Cl₂ (bleaches moist litmus paper). So X contains H and S, Y contains Cl.

records.question: Which of the following sulphides is insoluble in dilute HCl?
records.sourceExplanation: CuS is insoluble in dilute HCl, while ZnS, FeS, and Na₂S dissolve in dilute HCl.

records.question: When chlorine is passed into water and subsequently exposed to sunlight, the gas evolved is
records.sourceExplanation: Chlorine water decomposes in sunlight: 2Cl₂ + 2H₂O → 4HCl + O₂. Oxygen gas is evolved.

records.question: Which of the following metals does NOT form a stable trioxocarbonate(IV)?
records.sourceExplanation: Iron does not form a stable carbonate. FeCO₃ is not stable and decomposes easily.

records.question: Which of the following metals with NaOH to give salt and water only. When Z is treated with dilute HCl, a gas is evolved which gives a yellow suspension on passing into concentrated H₂SO₄. Substance Z is
records.sourceExplanation: Na₂SO₃ reacts with NaOH to give salt and water. With HCl, it gives SO₂ gas.

records.question: Ammonia gas is normally dried with
records.sourceExplanation: Ammonia is basic and reacts with acids. It is dried using quicklime (CaO) which does not react with ammonia.

records.question: What are the values of x, y and z respectively in the equation xCu + yHNO₃ → xCu(NO₃)₂ + 4H₂O + zNO?
records.sourceExplanation: 3Cu + 8HNO₃ → 3Cu(NO₃)₂ + 4H₂O + 2NO. So x=3, y=8, z=2.

records.question: The iron (III) oxide impurity in bauxite can be removed by
options: dissolution in sodium hydroxide and filtration
extraction with concentrated ammonia and reprecipitation
records.answerText: dissolution in sodium hydroxide and filtration
records.sourceExplanation: Bauxite is purified by the Bayer process: Al₂O₃ dissolves in NaOH, while Fe₂O₃ remains undissolved and is filtered off.

records.question: A white solid suspected to be lead trioxonitrate (V), zinc trioxocarbonate(IV) or calcium trioxocarbonate(IV) was heated strongly. Its residue, which was yellow when hot and white when cold, is
records.sourceExplanation: Lead(II) oxide (PbO) is yellow when hot and white when cold. This is a characteristic property of PbO.

records.question: Which of the following compounds would give lilac flame coloration and a white precipitate with acidified barium chloride solution?
records.sourceExplanation: K₂SO₄ gives lilac flame (K⁺) and white precipitate with BaCl₂ (SO₄²⁻ forms BaSO₄).

records.question: How will a metal X, which reacts explosively with air and with dilute acids, be best extracted from its ores?
options: Electrolysis of the solution of its salt
Displacement from solution by an alkali metal
records.sourceExplanation: Highly reactive metals (like Na, K, Mg, Al) are extracted by electrolysis of their molten salts.

records.question: Which of the following is NOT correct for the named organic compound in each case?
options: Butanoic acid solution gives effervescence with Na₂CO₃ solution
Glucose when reacted with Na₂CrO₄ at 0°C will show immediate discharge of colour
When but-2-ene is reacted with dilute solution of KMnO₄, the purple colour of KMnO₄ is discharged readily even at room temperature
When butan-2-ol is boiled with butanoic acid with a drop of concentrated H₂SO₄, a sweet smelling liquid is produced
records.answerText: Glucose when reacted with Na₂CrO₄ at 0°C will show immediate discharge of colour
records.sourceExplanation: Na₂CrO₄ is not a typical oxidizing agent for glucose. Glucose does not react with Na₂CrO₄.

records.question: Which of the following is used as an 'anti-knock' in automobile engines?
records.sourceExplanation: Lead tetra-ethyl (TEL) was used as an anti-knock agent in petrol to improve octane rating.

records.question: What reaction takes place when palm-oil is added to potash and foams are observed?
records.sourceExplanation: Palm oil (fat) reacts with potash (KOH) in saponification to produce soap and glycerol. Foaming indicates soap formation.

records.question: How many isomers can be formed from organic compounds with the formula C₃H₈O?
records.sourceExplanation: C₃H₈O has three isomers: propan-1-ol, propan-2-ol, and methoxyethane (ethyl methyl ether).

records.question: When ethanol is heated with excess concentrated sulphuric acid, the ethanol is
records.sourceExplanation: Ethanol with excess concentrated H₂SO₄ at high temperature (170°C) undergoes dehydration to form ethene (C₂H₄).

records.question: Which of the following compounds is NOT formed by the action of chlorine on methane?
records.sourceExplanation: Chlorine reacts with methane by substitution to form CH₃Cl, CH₂Cl₂, CHCl₃, and CCl₄. C₂H₅Cl is not formed.

records.question: The general formula of an alkyl halide (where X represents the halide) is
records.sourceExplanation: Alkyl halides have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₁X, where X is a halogen.

records.question: Which of the following are made by the process of polymerization?
records.sourceExplanation: Nylon and rubber are polymers made by polymerization. Soap is not a polymer.

records.question: Starch can be converted to ethyl alcohol by
records.sourceExplanation: Starch is hydrolysed to glucose, which is then fermented by yeast to produce ethanol and CO₂.

records.question: A brand of ink containing cobalt (II), copper (II) and iron can best be separated into its various components by
records.sourceExplanation: Chromatography separates components based on their different rates of movement through a stationary phase.

records.question: Which of the following substances is a mixture?
records.sourceExplanation: Sea water is a mixture of water, salts, and dissolved gases. The others are pure substances.

records.question: The number of molecules of carbon(IV) oxide produced when 10.0 g CaCO₃ is treated with 0.2 dm³ of 1 M HCl in the equation CaCO₃ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂ is
records.sourceExplanation: Moles CaCO₃ = 10/100 = 0.1 mol. Moles HCl = 1 × 0.2 = 0.2 mol. Both in stoichiometric proportion. Moles CO₂ = 0.1 mol. Molecules = 0.1 × 6.02 × 10²³ = 6.02 × 10²².

records.question: In the reaction CaC₂(s) + 2H₂O(l) → Ca(OH)₂(s) + C₂H₂(g), what is the mass of solid acetylene gas at S.T.P? [C=12, Ca=40, G.M.V=22400 cm³]
records.sourceExplanation: The question asks for mass of acetylene gas produced. Not enough information given. I'll go with D as per source.

records.question: If the quantity of oxygen occupying a 2.76 liter container at a pressure of 0.825 atmosphere and 300 K is reduced by one-half, what is the pressure exerted by the remaining gas?
records.sourceExplanation: PV = nRT. If the amount of gas (n) is halved at constant V and T, P is also halved. New P = 0.825/2 = 0.4125 atm.

records.question: Which of the following substances has the lowest vapour density? [O=16, Cl=35.5, H=1, C=12]
records.sourceExplanation: Vapour density = molecular mass/2. Molar masses: CH₃COOH=60, C₃H₇OH=60, CH₂Cl₂=85, CH₃CHO=44. Lowest is ethanal.

records.question: If d represents the density of a gas and K is a constant, the rate of gaseous diffusion is related to the equation
records.sourceExplanation: From Graham's law, rate of diffusion is inversely proportional to the square root of density.

records.question: The atomic numbers of two elements X and Y are 12 and 9 respectively. The bond in the compound formed between the atoms of these two elements is
records.sourceExplanation: X (Mg, metal) and Y (F, non-metal) form ionic bonds (MgF₂).

records.question: An element Z contained 90% of ¹⁶Z and 10% of ¹⁸Z. Its relative atomic mass is
The greater the difference in electronegativity between bonded atoms, the
options: lower the polarity of the bond
higher the polarity of the bond
higher the possibility of the substance formed being a molecule
records.answerText: higher the polarity of the bond
records.sourceExplanation: Electronegativity difference determines bond polarity. Greater difference = more polar bond.

records.question: A stream of air was successively passed through three tubes X, Y, and Z containing a concentrated aqueous solution of KOH, red hot copper powder and fused calcium chloride respectively. What was the composition of gas emanating from tube Z?
options: N₂, CO₂ and the inert gases
Water vapour, N₂ and the inert gases
records.sourceExplanation: KOH absorbs CO₂, red hot copper absorbs O₂, CaCl₂ absorbs water vapour. Nitrogen and inert gases remain.

records.question: In the purification of town water supply, alum is used principally to
options: improve the taste of the water
records.sourceExplanation: Alum causes coagulation of suspended particles, making them settle down for filtration.

records.question: Which of the following water samples will have the highest titer value when titrated for the Ca²⁺ ions using soap solution?
options: Rain water stored in a glass jar for two years
Permanently hard water passed through permutit
records.sourceExplanation: Boiling removes temporary hardness but not permanent hardness. So permanently hard water after boiling still has Ca²⁺ ions.

records.question: Oil spillage in ponds and creeks can be cleaned up by
records.sourceExplanation: Detergents emulsify the oil, making it disperse in water and easier to remove.

records.question: The solubility of Na₃AsO₄·(H₂O)₁₂ is 38.9 g per 100 g H₂O. What is the percentage of Na₃AsO₄ in the saturated solution? [As=75, Na=23, O=16, H=1]
records.sourceExplanation: Molar mass Na₃AsO₄ = 208, hydrate = 424. Mass Na₃AsO₄ in 38.9 g hydrate = 38.9 × 208/424 = 19.1 g. Percentage = 19.1/(100+38.9) × 100 = 13.7%.

records.question: In which of the following are the aqueous solutions of each of the substances correctly arranged in order of decreasing acidity?
options: Ethanoic acid, milk of magnesia, sodium chloride, hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide
Ethanoic acid, hydrochloric acid, milk of magnesia, sodium chloride and sodium hydroxide
Hydrochloric acid, ethanoic acid, sodium chloride, milk of magnesia and sodium hydroxide
Hydrochloric acid, sodium hydroxide, sodium chloride, ethanoic acid and milk of magnesia
records.answerText: Hydrochloric acid, ethanoic acid, sodium chloride, milk of magnesia and sodium hydroxide
records.sourceExplanation: Decreasing acidity: HCl (strong acid) > CH₃COOH (weak acid) > NaCl (neutral) > Mg(OH)₂ (weak base) > NaOH (strong base).

records.question: The basicity of tetraoxophosphate (V) acid is
records.sourceExplanation: Tetraoxophosphate (V) acid is H₃PO₄. It has 3 replaceable hydrogen atoms, so basicity is 3.

records.question: If 24.83 cm³ of 0.15 M NaOH is titrated to its end point with 39.45 cm³ of HCl, what is the molarity of the HCl?
records.sourceExplanation:
NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O. Moles NaOH = 0.15 × 24.83/1000 = 0.0037245 mol. Molarity HCl = 0.0037245 / (39.45/1000) = 0.0944 M.
# JAMB CHEMISTRY PAST QUESTIONS (219–300)

records.question: A quantity of electricity liberates 3.6 g of silver from its salt. What mass of aluminium will be liberated from its salt by the same quantity of electricity? [Al=27, Ag=108]
records.sourceExplanation: Equivalent weight Ag = 108/1 = 108. Eq. wt Al = 27/3 = 9. Mass Al = (9/108) × 3.6 = 0.3 g.

records.question: Which of the following statements is CORRECT if 1 Faraday of electricity is passed through 1 M CuSO₄ solution for 1 minute?
options: The pH of the solution at the cathode decreases
The pH of the solution at the anode decreases
1 mole of Cu will be liberated at the cathode
60 moles of Cu will be liberated at the anode
records.answerText: The pH of the solution at the anode decreases
records.sourceExplanation: At anode, OH⁻ is discharged, producing O₂ and H⁺, making the solution acidic (pH decreases).

records.question: What mass of magnesium would be obtained by passing a current of 2 amperes for 2 hrs 30 mins through molten magnesium chloride? [1 faraday = 96500 C, Mg=24]
In the reaction 3CuO + 2NH₃ → 3Cu + 3H₂O + N₂, how many electrons are transferred for each mole of copper produced?
records.sourceExplanation: Cu²⁺ in CuO is reduced to Cu (0). Each Cu gains 2 electrons. For 1 mole Cu, electrons = 2 × Avogadro's number = 1.204 × 10²⁴.

records.question: Z is a solid substance, which liberates carbon(IV) oxide on treatment with concentrated H₂SO₄ or KMnO₄. The solid substance Z is
records.sourceExplanation: Oxalic acid (H₂C₂O₄) with concentrated H₂SO₄ gives CO₂ and CO. It also decolorizes KMnO₄.

records.question: 5 g of ammonium trioxonitrate (V) on dissolution in water cooled its surrounding water and container by 1.6 kJ. What is the heat of solution of NH₄NO₃? [N=14, O=16, H=1]
records.sourceExplanation: Molar mass NH₄NO₃ = 80 g/mol. Moles = 5/80 = 0.0625 mol. Heat absorbed = 1.6 kJ. Heat per mole = 1.6/0.0625 = 25.6 kJ/mol. Endothermic = positive.

records.question: Tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid is prepared using the chemical reaction SO₃(g) + H₂O(l) → H₂SO₄(l). Given the heats of formation for SO₃(g), H₂O(l) and H₂SO₄(l) as -395 kJ/mol, -286 kJ/mol and -811 kJ/mol respectively, the enthalpy change accompanying this reaction is

The times taken for iodine to be liberated in the reaction between sodium thiosulphate and hydrochloric acid at various temperatures are as follows: | Temp (°C) | 25 | 35 | 45 | |---|---|---|---| | Time (seconds) | 72 | 36 | 18 | These results suggest that
options: for a 10°C rise in temperature, rate of reaction is doubled
for a 10°C rise in temperature, rate of reaction is halved
time taken for iodine to appear does not depend on temperature
for a 10°C rise in temperature, rate of reaction is tripled
records.answerText: for a 10°C rise in temperature, rate of reaction is doubled
records.sourceExplanation: As temperature increases from 25 to 35°C (10°C rise), time halves from 72 to 36 seconds, so rate doubles.

records.question: The reaction between sulphur(IV) oxide and oxygen is represented by the equilibrium reaction 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g), ΔH = -196 kJ. What factor would influence increased production of SO₃(g)?
options: Increase in the temperature of the reaction
Decrease in the temperature of the reaction
Decrease in the concentration of SO₂
records.answerText: Decrease in the temperature of the reaction
records.sourceExplanation: Since the reaction is exothermic (ΔH negative), decreasing temperature favours forward reaction, increasing SO₃ yield.

records.question: Which of the following equations correctly represents the action of hot concentrated alkaline solution on chlorine?
records.sourceExplanation: Hot concentrated alkali reacts with chlorine to give chlorate (ClO₃⁻) and chloride ions.

records.question: Magnesium ribbon was allowed to burn inside a given gas P leaving a white solid residue Q. Addition of water to Q liberated a gas which produced dense white fumes with a drop of hydrochloric acid. The gas P was
records.sourceExplanation: Mg burns in nitrogen to form Mg₃N₂ (Q). With water, it gives NH₃ (gas). NH₃ + HCl → NH₄Cl (dense white fumes).

records.question: The best treatment for a student who accidentally poured concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid on his skin in the laboratory is to wash the skin with
records.sourceExplanation: The first aid for acid spills on skin is to wash with plenty of cold water to dilute and remove the acid.

records.question: In which of the following pairs of elements is allotropy exhibited by each element?
records.sourceExplanation: Oxygen has allotropes (O₂, O₃), sulphur has allotropes (rhombic, monoclinic, etc.).

records.question: Which of the following gases can best be used for demonstrating the fountain experiment? (i) Nitrogen (ii) Ammonia (iii) Nitrogen(I)oxide (iv) Hydrogen chloride
records.sourceExplanation: Ammonia (NH₃) and hydrogen chloride (HCl) are highly soluble in water, creating a vacuum that causes the fountain effect.

records.question: When calcium hydroxide is heated with ammonium tetraoxosulphate(VI), the gas given off may be collected by
options: bubbling it through water and then passing it through calcium oxide
passing it directly through calcium oxide
passing it directly through calcium chloride
records.answerText: passing it directly through calcium chloride
records.sourceExplanation: Ca(OH)₂ + (NH₄)₂SO₄ → CaSO₄ + 2NH₃ + 2H₂O. NH₃ is dried by passing through calcium chloride.

records.question: Which of the following elements will form oxide which will dissolve both dilute HNO₃ and NaOH solution to form salts?
records.sourceExplanation: Manganese dioxide (MnO₂) is amphoteric and dissolves in both acids and bases.

records.question: Stainless steel is an alloy of
records.sourceExplanation: Stainless steel is an alloy of iron, carbon, and chromium (at least 10.5% Cr).

records.question: Alloys are best prepared by
options: high temperature arc welding of the metals
electrolysis using the major metallic component as cathode
reducing a mixture of the oxides of the elements
cooling a molten mixture of the necessary elements
records.answerText: cooling a molten mixture of the necessary elements
records.sourceExplanation: Alloys are prepared by melting the constituent metals together and allowing the mixture to cool.

records.question: Corrosion is exhibited by
options: metals below hydrogen in the electrochemical series
records.sourceExplanation: All metals can corrode under suitable conditions.

records.question: Inspite of the electronic configuration 1s²2s²2p², carbon is tetravalent because
options: the electrons in both 2s and 2p orbitals have equal energy
the electrons in both 2s and 2p orbitals are equivalent
the six orbitals hybridize to four
records.sourceExplanation: Carbon undergoes hybridization (sp³) to form four equivalent bonds, making it tetravalent.

records.question: Which of the following compounds will give a precipitate with an aqueous ammoniacal solution of copper(I) chloride?
records.sourceExplanation: Terminal alkynes (with ≡C-H) react with ammoniacal CuCl to give a red precipitate of copper acetylide.

records.question: The efficiency of petrol as a fuel in high compression internal combustion engines improves with an increase in the amount of
records.sourceExplanation: Branched chain alkanes have higher octane numbers and burn more smoothly, reducing knocking.

records.question: A palm wine seller stopped a bottle of his palm wine in his stall and after a few hours the bottle exploded. The reaction that occurred is
records.sourceExplanation: Fermentation of glucose produces ethanol and CO₂. The pressure from CO₂ gas caused the bottle to explode.

records.question: Ethanol reacts with aqueous sodium mono-oxoidate(I) to give a bright yellow solid with a characteristic smell. The product is
records.sourceExplanation: Ethanol reacts with iodine in the presence of NaOH to form iodoform (triiodomethane), a yellow solid.

records.question: The most volatile fraction obtained from fractional distillation of crude petroleum contains
records.sourceExplanation: The most volatile fraction contains gases like methane, ethane, and propane.
