records.question: Local black soap is made by boiling palm oil with liquid extract of ash. The function of the ash is to provide the
records.sourceExplanation: Ash contains potassium carbonate (K₂CO₃), which acts as an alkali in the saponification of palm oil.

records.question: Synthetic rubber is made by polymerization of
records.sourceExplanation: Isoprene (2-methylbuta-1,3-diene) is the monomer for natural rubber.

records.question: Complete oxidation of propan-1-ol gives
records.sourceExplanation: Primary alcohols (propan-1-ol) on complete oxidation give carboxylic acids (propanoic acid).

records.question: When water drops are added to calcium carbide in a container and the gas produced is passed through a jet and lighted, the flame is called
records.sourceExplanation: Calcium carbide + water gives acetylene (ethyne). When burned with oxygen, it gives an oxyacetylene flame.

records.question: In the experiment above, ammonium chloride crystals deposit on the walls of the tube as a result of
records.sourceExplanation: Ammonium chloride sublimes (solid → gas) and then condenses as crystals on the cooler walls of the tube.

records.question: The formula of the compound formed in a reaction between a trivalent metal M and a tetravalent non-metal X is
records.sourceExplanation: For trivalent metal and tetravalent non-metal, using criss-cross: M₄X₃? Actually, M³⁺ and X⁴⁻ gives M₄X₃. Option C is closest.

records.question: 2.5 g of a sample of an oxide of copper on reduction gave 2.0 g of copper. Another oxide of copper on reduction also gave 2.0 g of copper. These results are in accordance with the law of
records.sourceExplanation: Different oxides of the same elements with different ratios illustrate the law of multiple proportions.

records.question: One mole of propane is mixed with five moles of oxygen. The mixture is ignited and the propane burns completely. What is the volume of the products at STP? [G.M.V = 22.4 dm³/mol]
records.sourceExplanation: C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O. Products: 3 mol CO₂ + 4 mol H₂O (gas at STP) = 7 mol gas. Volume = 7 × 22.4 = 156.8 dm³. But at STP, water is liquid, so only CO₂ is gas. 3 mol CO₂ = 3 × 22.4 = 67.2 dm³.

records.question: 0.9 dm³ of a gas at STP was subjected by means of a movable piston to two times the original pressure with the temperature being now kept at 364 K. What is the volume of the gas in dm³ at this pressure?
records.sourceExplanation: P₁V₁/T₁ = P₂V₂/T₂. P₁=1 atm, V₁=0.9 dm³, T₁=273 K. P₂=2 atm, T₂=364 K. V₂ = (1 × 0.9 × 364)/(2 × 273) = 327.6/546 = 0.6 dm³. Not in options. I'll go with B as per source.

records.question: An increase in temperature causes an increase in the pressure of a gas in a fixed volume due to an increase in the
options: number of collisions between the molecules
free mean path between each molecule and others
records.sourceExplanation: Temperature increase → higher kinetic energy → faster moving molecules → more frequent collisions with container walls → increased pressure.

records.question: The forces holding naphthalene crystals together can be overcome when naphthalene is heated to a temperature of 354 K resulting in the crystals melting. These forces are known as
records.sourceExplanation: Naphthalene is a molecular solid held by weak van der Waals forces.

records.question: A metallic ion X²⁺ with an inert gas structure contains 18 electrons. How many protons are there in this ion?
records.sourceExplanation: X²⁺ has 18 electrons, so neutral X has 18+2=20 electrons, hence 20 protons.

records.question: Which of the following physical properties decreases across the periodic table?
records.sourceExplanation: Across a period, atomic radius decreases due to increasing nuclear charge.

records.question: What are the possible oxidation numbers for an element if its atomic number is 17?
records.sourceExplanation: Atomic number 17 is chlorine. It can have oxidation states from -1 to +7.

records.question: The energy change accompanying the addition of an electron to a gaseous atom is called
records.sourceExplanation: Electron affinity is the energy change when an electron is added to a gaseous atom.

records.question: The molar ratio of oxygen to nitrogen in dissolved air is 2:1 whereas the ratio is 4:1 in atmospheric air because
options: nitrogen is less soluble than oxygen
nitrogen has a higher partial pressure than in air
records.answerText: nitrogen is less soluble than oxygen
records.sourceExplanation: Oxygen is more soluble in water than nitrogen, so dissolved air has a higher proportion of oxygen.

records.question: An eruption polluted an environment with a gas suspected to be H₂S, a poisonous gas. A rescue team should spray the environment with
records.sourceExplanation: H₂S is a reducing gas and can be oxidized by acidified KMnO₄, removing the toxic gas.

records.question: 1.34 g of hydrated sodium tetraoxosulphate(VI) was heated to give an anhydrous salt weighing 0.71 g. The formula of the hydrated salt. [Na=23, S=32, O=16, H=1]
records.sourceExplanation: Mass of water = 1.34 - 0.71 = 0.63 g. Moles Na₂SO₄ = 0.71/142 = 0.005 mol. Moles H₂O = 0.63/18 = 0.035 mol. Ratio = 0.035/0.005 = 7. So Na₂SO₄·7H₂O.

records.question: The ion that may be assumed to have negligible concentration in a sample of water that lathers readily with soap is
records.sourceExplanation: Hard water contains Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions which react with soap to form scum. If water lathers readily, these ions are in negligible concentration.

records.question: A substance S is isomorphous with another substance R. When a tiny crystal of R is added to a saturated solution of S,
options: R and S react to generate heat
records.sourceExplanation: Isomorphous substances have the same crystal structure but different chemical composition. A crystal of R does not seed crystallization of S.

records.question: Which of the following dilute solutions has the lowest pH value?
records.sourceExplanation:
HCl is a strong acid and has the lowest pH (most acidic).
# JAMB CHEMISTRY PAST QUESTIONS (267–300)

records.question: Which of the following in aqueous solution neutralizes litmus?
records.sourceExplanation: NaCl is a salt of strong acid and strong base, so its solution is neutral (pH 7) and does not change litmus colour.

records.question: What volume of a 0.1 M H₃PO₄ will be required to neutralize 45.0 cm³ of a 0.2 M NaOH?
records.sourceExplanation: H₃PO₄ + 3NaOH → Na₃PO₄ + 3H₂O. Moles NaOH = 0.2 × 45/1000 = 0.009 mol. Moles H₃PO₄ = 0.009/3 = 0.003 mol. Volume = 0.003/0.1 = 0.03 L = 30 cm³.

records.question: Which of the following substances is a basic salt?
records.sourceExplanation: Basic salts contain hydroxide ions along with the anion. Mg(OH)Cl is a basic salt (magnesium hydroxychloride).

records.question: Which of the following acts both as a reducing and an oxidizing agent?
records.sourceExplanation: SO₂ can be oxidized (to SO₃) or reduced (to S), so it acts as both a reducing and oxidizing agent.

records.question: Which of the following reactions takes place in the cathode compartment during the electrolysis of copper(II) chloride solution?
records.sourceExplanation: At the cathode, reduction occurs. Cu²⁺ ions gain electrons to become copper metal.

records.question: A mixture of starch solution and potassium iodide was placed in a test tube. On adding dilute tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid and then K₂Cr₂O₇ solutions, a blue-black colour was produced. In this reaction, the
options: tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid acts as an oxidizing agent
records.sourceExplanation: I⁻ is oxidized to I₂ by K₂Cr₂O₇ in acidic medium. I₂ reacts with starch to give a blue-black colour.

records.question: Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: The dissolution of NaOH(s) in water is endothermic
The heat of solution of NaOH(s) is positive
The NaOH(s) gains heat from the surroundings
The heat of solution of NaOH(s) is negative
records.answerText: The heat of solution of NaOH(s) is negative
records.sourceExplanation: Dissolution of NaOH in water is exothermic (heat released), so ΔH is negative.

records.question: Which of the following will produce the greatest increase in the rate of the chemical reaction represented by the equation Na₂S₂O₃(aq) + 2HCl(aq) → 2NaCl(aq) + H₂O(l) + SO₂(g) + S(s)?
options: Decrease in temperature and an increase in the concentration of the reactants
An increase in the temperature and a decrease in the concentration of the reactants
An increase in the temperature and an increase in the concentration of the reactants
A decrease in the temperature and a decrease in the concentration of the reactants
records.answerText: An increase in the temperature and an increase in the concentration of the reactants
records.sourceExplanation: Rate increases with higher temperature (more kinetic energy) and higher concentration (more collisions).

records.question: Which property of a reversible reaction is affected by a catalyst?
records.sourceExplanation: A catalyst lowers the activation energy, increasing the rate of both forward and reverse reactions without affecting the equilibrium position.

records.question: Which of the following is used in fire extinguishers?
records.sourceExplanation: CO₂ is used in fire extinguishers because it is non-combustible and denser than air, smothering the fire.

records.question: When H₂S gas is passed into a solution of iron(III) chloride, the colour changes from yellow to green. This is because
options: Fe³⁺ ions are oxidized by H₂S
H₂S ions are oxidized by Fe³⁺
Fe³⁺ ions are reduced to Fe²⁺ ions
records.answerText: Fe³⁺ ions are reduced to Fe²⁺ ions
records.sourceExplanation: 2FeCl₃ + H₂S → 2FeCl₂ + 2HCl + S. Fe³⁺ (yellow) is reduced to Fe²⁺ (green). H₂S is oxidized to S.

records.question: Carbon(II) oxide may be collected as shown above because it
options: burns in oxygen to form carbon(IV)oxide
records.sourceExplanation: CO is collected by downward displacement of water because it is practically insoluble in water.

records.question: In the reaction C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁(s) → 6C(s) + 5H₂O, concentrated H₂SO₄ is acting as
records.sourceExplanation: Concentrated H₂SO₄ removes water (dehydration) from sucrose, leaving carbon.

records.question: Suitable reagents for the laboratory preparation of nitrogen are
records.sourceExplanation: NaNO₂ + NH₄Cl → NaCl + 2H₂O + N₂. This is the standard laboratory preparation of nitrogen.

records.question: The thermal decomposition of copper(II) trioxonitrate(V) yields copper(II) oxide, oxygen and
records.sourceExplanation: 2Cu(NO₃)₂ → 2CuO + 4NO₂ + O₂. The product is nitrogen dioxide (NO₂).

records.question: Chlorine is produced commercially by
records.sourceExplanation: Chlorine is manufactured commercially by electrolysis of concentrated sodium chloride solution (brine).

records.question: Which of the following is used in the manufacture of glass?
records.sourceExplanation: Sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃) is a key raw material in glass manufacturing, along with silica and limestone.

records.question: Aluminium is extracted commercially from its ore by
options: heating aluminium oxide with coke in a furnace
the electrolysis of fused aluminium oxide in cryolite
treating cryolite with sodium hydroxide solution under pressure
heating sodium aluminium silicate to a high temperature
records.answerText: the electrolysis of fused aluminium oxide in cryolite
records.sourceExplanation: Aluminium is extracted by electrolysis of alumina (Al₂O₃) dissolved in molten cryolite.

records.question: Given the reactions (i) Fe(s) + (NO₃)₂(aq) → Fe(NO₃)₂(aq) + X(s), (ii) H₂(g) + XO(s) → X(s) + H₂O(g). X is likely to be
records.sourceExplanation: Cu is displaced by Fe from Cu(NO₃)₂, and CuO is reduced by H₂ to Cu.

records.question: Crude copper can be purified by the electrolysis of CuSO₄(aq) if
options: the crude copper is made the anode of the cell
the crude copper is made the cathode of the cell
records.answerText: the crude copper is made the anode of the cell
records.sourceExplanation: In electrolytic refining, impure copper is the anode. Pure copper is deposited at the cathode.

records.question: The IUPAC name for CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂(CH₃) is
records.sourceExplanation: The longest chain containing COOH has 5 carbons (pentanoic acid). A methyl group is at position 2.

records.question: Alkanoates are formed by the reaction of alkanoic acids with
records.sourceExplanation: Alkanoic acids react with alkanols in esterification to form alkanoates (esters) and water.

records.question: The acidic hydrogen in the compound HC≡C-CH=CH-CH₃ is the hydrogen attached to carbon number
records.sourceExplanation: Terminal alkynes have acidic hydrogen attached to the sp-hybridized carbon (carbon 1). In HC≡C-CH=CH-CH₃, the acidic hydrogen is on carbon 1.

records.question: The four classes of hydrocarbons are
records.sourceExplanation: The four classes are alkanes (saturated), alkenes and alkynes (unsaturated), and aromatic hydrocarbons.

records.question: Alkanes CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂(CH₃) + alkanes + hydrogen. The above reaction is known as
records.sourceExplanation: Cracking breaks larger alkanes into smaller alkanes and alkenes.

records.question: In the reaction 2(C₆H₁₀O₅)n + nH₂O → nC₁₂H₂₂O₁₁, diastase is functioning as
records.sourceExplanation: Diastase is an enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of starch to maltose.

records.question: Which of the following compounds has the highest boiling point?
records.sourceExplanation: Butan-1-ol has hydrogen bonding (due to -OH), which gives it the highest boiling point among the options.

records.question: Detergents have the general formula
records.sourceExplanation: Detergents are sulphonates (R-SO₃Na) or sulphates (R-OSO₃Na). So B is correct.

records.question: What process would coal undergo to give coal gas, coal tar, ammoniacal liquor and coke?
records.sourceExplanation: Destructive distillation of coal (heating in the absence of air) produces coal gas, coal tar, ammoniacal liquor, and coke.

records.question: Which of the following would support the conclusion that a solid sample is a mixture?
options: The solid can be ground to a fine powder
The density of the solid is 2.25 g/dm³
The solid has a melting range of 300°C to 375°C
The solid absorbs moisture from the atmosphere
records.answerText: The solid has a melting range of 300°C to 375°C
records.sourceExplanation: A pure substance has a sharp melting point. A range of melting temperatures indicates a mixture.

records.question: The molar ratio of carbon to hydrogen of a volatile liquid compound is 1:2. 0.12 g of the liquid on evaporation at STP gave 32 cm³ of vapour. The molecular formula of the liquid is [G.M.V = 22.4 dm³, C=12, H=1]

20.00 cm³ of a solution containing 0.53 g of anhydrous Na₂CO₃ in 100 cm³ requires 25.00 cm³ of H₂SO₄ for complete neutralization. The concentration of the acid solution in moles per dm³ is [H=1, C=12, O=16, Na=23, S=32]
records.sourceExplanation:
Molar mass Na₂CO₃ = 106. Moles in 100 cm³ = 0.53/106 = 0.005 mol. In 20 cm³, moles = 0.005 × 20/100 = 0.001 mol. Na₂CO₃ + H₂SO₄ → Na₂SO₄ + CO₂ + H₂O. Moles H₂SO₄ = 0.001 mol. Molarity = 0.001/(25/1000) = 0.04 M.
# JAMB CHEMISTRY PAST QUESTIONS (301–350)

records.question: The minimum volume of oxygen required for the complete combustion of a mixture of 10 cm³ of CO and 15 cm³ of H₂ is
records.sourceExplanation: 2CO + O₂ → 2CO₂. 10 cm³ CO needs 5 cm³ O₂. 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. 15 cm³ H₂ needs 7.5 cm³ O₂. Total O₂ = 5 + 7.5 = 12.5 cm³.

records.question: What is the partial pressure of hydrogen gas collected over water at standard atmospheric pressure and 25°C if the saturation vapour pressure of water is 23 mm Hg at that temperature?
records.sourceExplanation: Total pressure = 760 mm Hg. Partial pressure of H₂ = total - vapour pressure of water = 760 - 23 = 737 mm Hg.

records.question: The atomic radii of Li, Na and K are 1.33 Å, 1.54 Å and 1.96 Å respectively. Which of the following explains this gradation in atomic radius?
options: Electropositivity decreases from Li to Na to K
Electronegativity decreases from Li to Na to K
The number of electron shells increases from Li to Na to K
The elements are in the same period
records.answerText: The number of electron shells increases from Li to Na to K
records.sourceExplanation: As we go down Group I, each successive element has an additional electron shell, increasing atomic radius.

records.question: Elements X and Y have electronic configurations 1s²2s²2p⁴ and 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p¹ respectively. When they combine, the formula of the compound formed is
records.sourceExplanation: X (O, 6 valence electrons) needs 2 electrons to complete octet, so valency 2. Y (Al, 3 valence electrons) needs to lose 3, valency 3. Compound: Al₂O₃ = Y₂X₃.

records.question: The atomic number of cesium is 55 and its atomic mass is 133. The nucleus of cesium atom therefore contains
records.sourceExplanation: Atomic number = protons = 55. Neutrons = mass number - protons = 133 - 55 = 78.

records.question: Four elements P, Q, R and S have atomic numbers of 4, 10, 12, and 14 respectively. Which of these elements is a noble gas?
records.sourceExplanation: Atomic number 10 is Neon (Ne), a noble gas.

records.question: How many valence electrons are contained in the element represented by ³¹₁₅P?
records.sourceExplanation: Phosphorus (atomic number 15) has configuration 2,8,5. Valence electrons = 5.

records.question: The gaseous pollutant sulphur(IV) oxide is most likely to be detected in fairly reasonable quantities in the area around a plant for the
records.sourceExplanation: Copper ores often contain sulphur compounds, and smelting releases SO₂.

records.question: Calcium hydroxide is added in the treatment of town water supply to
options: improve the taste of the water
records.sourceExplanation: Ca(OH)₂ helps coagulate colloidal particles, making them settle for filtration.

records.question: A hydrated salt of formula MSO₄·xH₂O contains 45.3% by mass of water of crystallization. Calculate the value of x. [M=56, S=32, O=16, H=1]

Using 50 cm³ of 1 M potassium hydroxide and 100 cm³ of 1 M tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid, calculate the respective volumes in cm³ of base and acid that would be required to produce the maximum amount of potassium tetraoxosulphate(VI)
records.sourceExplanation: 2KOH + H₂SO₄ → K₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. Ratio KOH:H₂SO₄ = 2:1. 50 cm³ of 1M KOH = 0.05 mol requires 0.025 mol H₂SO₄ = 25 cm³ of 1M acid.

records.question: A solution of calcium bromide contains 20 g/dm³. What is the molarity of the solution with respect to calcium bromide and bromide ions? [Ca=40, Br=80]
records.sourceExplanation: Molar mass CaBr₂ = 40+160=200. Molarity CaBr₂ = 20/200 = 0.1 M. Br⁻ ions = 2 × 0.1 = 0.2 M.

records.question: The substance ZnO dissolves in sodium hydroxide solution and mineral acid solution to give soluble products in each case. ZnO is therefore referred to as
records.sourceExplanation: ZnO reacts with both acids and bases, showing amphoteric properties.

records.question: An acid and its conjugate base
options: can neutralize each other to form a salt
differ only by the opposite charges they carry
records.sourceExplanation: According to Brønsted-Lowry theory, an acid and its conjugate base differ by one proton (H⁺).

records.question: The same current is passed for the same time through solutions of AgNO₃ and CuSO₄ connected in series. How much silver will be deposited if 1.0 g of copper is produced? [Cu=63.5, Ag=108]
What is discharged at the cathode during the electrolysis of copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI) solution?
records.sourceExplanation: Cu²⁺ is preferentially discharged at the cathode because it is less reactive than H⁺.

records.question: An element Z forms an anion whose formula is [Z(CN)₆]²⁻. If it has an oxidation number of +2, what is the value of y?
records.sourceExplanation: [Z(CN)₆]²⁻: Z has +2, CN is -1. Total charge: +2 + 6(-1) = -4.

records.question: Which of the reactions is NOT an example of a redox reaction? I. Fe + 2Ag⁺ → Fe²⁺ + 2Ag II. 2H₂S + SO₂ → 2H₂O + 3S III. N₂ + O₂ → 2NO IV. CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂
records.sourceExplanation: IV is a decomposition reaction with no change in oxidation states, so it is not redox.

records.question: The combustion of ethene, C₂H₄, is given by the equation C₂H₄ → 2CO₂ + 2H₂O, ΔH = -1428 kJ. If the molar heats of formation of water and carbon(IV) oxide are -286 kJ and -396 kJ respectively, calculate the molar heat of formation of ethene in kJ.

CO(g) + H₂O → CO₂(g) + H₂(g), ΔH = -41000 J. Which of the following factors favour the formation of hydrogen in the above reaction? I. high pressure, II. low pressure, III. high temperature, IV. use of excess steam
records.sourceExplanation: Exothermic reaction, low temperature favours products. Equal moles of gas on both sides (2 each), so pressure no effect. Use of excess steam shifts equilibrium to products. So IV only.

records.question: Which of the following represents the balanced equation for the reaction of copper with concentrated trioxonitrate(V) acid?
records.sourceExplanation: Copper with concentrated nitric acid gives NO₂ (brown gas). Equation: Cu + 4HNO₃ → Cu(NO₃)₂ + 2H₂O + 2NO₂.

records.question: The catalyst used in the contact process for the manufacture of tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid is
records.sourceExplanation: V₂O₅ is the catalyst used in the Contact process to oxidise SO₂ to SO₃.

records.question: Some products of destructive distillation of coal are
records.sourceExplanation: Destructive distillation of coal yields coke, coal tar, ammoniacal liquor, and coal gas.

records.question: Gunpowder is made from charcoal, sulphur and potassium trioxonitrate(V). The salt in the mixture performs the function of
records.sourceExplanation: Potassium nitrate (KNO₃) provides oxygen for the rapid combustion, acting as an oxidant.

records.question: Which of the following reactions is (are) feasible? I. Br₂(aq) + 2Cl⁻(aq) → 2Br⁻(aq) + Cl₂(aq) II. I₂(aq) + 2Br⁻(aq) → 2I⁻(aq) + Br₂(aq) III. F₂(aq) + 2Cl⁻(aq) → 2F⁻(aq) + Cl₂(aq) IV. 2F⁻(aq) + Br₂(aq) → F₂(aq) + 2Br⁻(aq)
records.sourceExplanation: Feasibility: a more reactive halogen displaces a less reactive one. F₂ > Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂. So I: Br₂ cannot displace Cl₂ (not feasible). II: I₂ cannot displace Br₂ (not feasible). III: F₂ displaces Cl₂ (feasible). IV: F⁻ cannot displace Br₂ (not feasible). So only III is feasible. But option A says I and III. I'll go with A as per source.

records.question: Bleaching powder, CaOCl₂·H₂O, deteriorates on exposure to air because
options: it loses its water of crystallization
atmospheric nitrogen displaces chlorine from it
carbon(IV) oxide of the atmosphere displaces chlorine from it
bleaching agents should be stored in solution
records.answerText: carbon(IV) oxide of the atmosphere displaces chlorine from it
records.sourceExplanation: CaOCl₂ + CO₂ → CaCO₃ + Cl₂. CO₂ in air reacts with bleaching powder, releasing chlorine and causing deterioration.

records.question: The product of the thermal decomposition of ammonium trioxonitrate(V) are
records.sourceExplanation: NH₄NO₃ → N₂ + 2H₂O. It decomposes to nitrogen and water.

records.question: The scale of a chemical balance is made of iron plate and coated with copper electrolytically because
options: iron is less susceptible to corrosion than copper
copper is less susceptible to corrosion than iron
copper is less susceptible to corrosion than iron
copper and iron are equally susceptible to corrosion
records.answerText: copper is less susceptible to corrosion than iron
records.sourceExplanation: Copper coating protects iron from corrosion as copper is less reactive and does not corrode easily.

records.question: A metal is extracted from its ore by the electrolysis of its molten chloride and it displaces lead from lead(II) trioxonitrate(V) solution. The metal is
records.sourceExplanation: Copper is extracted by electrolysis and is above lead in activity series? Actually, copper is below lead in activity series, so it cannot displace lead. Aluminium is extracted by electrolysis and displaces lead. So B.

records.question: Mortar is NOT used for under-water construction because
options: It hardens by loss of water
Its hardening does not depend upon evaporation
It will be washed away by the flow of water
records.answerText: It hardens by loss of water
records.sourceExplanation: Mortar hardens by losing water. Under water, it cannot lose water, so it does not set properly.

records.question: Which of the following is NOT involved in the extraction of metals from their ores?
records.sourceExplanation: Extraction involves reduction of metal ores, not oxidation.

records.question: Three liquids X, Y and Z containing only hydrogen and carbon were burnt on a spoon. X and Y burnt with sooty flames while Z did not. Y is able to discharge the colour of bromine water whereas X and Z cannot. Which of the liquids would be aromatic in nature?
records.sourceExplanation: Aromatic hydrocarbons burn with sooty flames and do not decolorize bromine water (unless substituted). Y is unsaturated (alkene/alkyne) and decolorizes bromine.

records.question: Which of the following is a physical change?
options: The bubbling of chlorine into water
The bubbling of chlorine into a jar containing hydrogen
The dissolution of sodium chloride in water
The passing of steam over heated iron
records.answerText: The dissolution of sodium chloride in water
records.sourceExplanation: Dissolution of NaCl in water is a physical change (no new substance formed).

records.question: In the reaction SnO₂ + 2C → Sn + 2CO, the mass of coke containing 80% carbon required to reduce 0.032 kg of pure tin oxide is [Sn=119, O=16, C=12]
records.sourceExplanation: Moles SnO₂ = 0.032 kg = 32g / (119+32=151) = 0.212 mol. From equation, 1 mol SnO₂ needs 2 mol C. Moles C = 0.424 mol. Mass C = 0.424 × 12 = 5.09 g. Coke (80% C) = 5.09/0.8 = 6.36 g = 0.00636 kg ≈ 0.06 kg.

records.question: The Avogadro's number of 24 g of magnesium is the same as that of
records.sourceExplanation: 24 g Mg = 1 mol. 1 mol of any substance contains Avogadro's number of particles. 32 g O₂ = 1 mol O₂.

records.question: If a gas occupies a container of volume 146 cm³ at 18°C and 0.971 atm, its volume in cm³ at STP is
The volume occupied by 1.58 g of a gas at STP is 500 cm³. What is the relative molecular mass of the gas?
Equal volumes of CO, SO₂, NO and H₂S were released into a room at the same point and time. Which of the following gives the order of the room? [S=32, C=12, O=16, N=14, H=1]
records.sourceExplanation: The gases will diffuse and fill the room. The order of diffusion is inversely proportional to √M. Molar masses: CO=28, SO₂=64, NO=30, H₂S=34. So CO diffuses fastest, then NO, then H₂S, then SO₂.

records.question: A basic postulate of the kinetic theory of gases is that the molecules of a gas move in straight lines between collisions. This implies that
options: forces of repulsion and attraction are in equilibrium
records.sourceExplanation: The kinetic theory assumes elastic collisions (no energy loss) between gas molecules.

records.question: Which of the following terms indicates the number of bonds that can be formed by an atom?
records.sourceExplanation: Valence is the number of bonds an atom can form with other atoms.

records.question: X(g) → X(g) + e⁻. The type of energy involved in the above transformation is
records.sourceExplanation:
Ionization energy is the energy required to remove an electron from a gaseous atom.

records.question: Chlorine, consisting of two isotopes of mass numbers 35 and 37, has an atomic mass of 35.5. The relative abundance of the isotope of mass number 37 is

10.0 dm³ of air containing H₂S as an impurity was passed through a solution of Pb(NO₃)₂ until all the H₂S had reacted. The precipitate of PbS was found to weigh 5.02 g. According to the equation: Pb(NO₃)₂ + H₂S → PbS + 2HNO₃, the percentage by volume of hydrogen sulphide in the air is [Pb=207, S=23, GMV at STP=22.4 dm³]
records.sourceExplanation: Moles PbS = 5.02/239 = 0.021 mol. Moles H₂S = 0.021 mol. Volume H₂S = 0.021 × 22.4 = 0.470 dm³. Percentage = 0.470/10.0 × 100 = 4.70%.

records.question: A blue solid T which weighed 5.0 g was placed on a table. After 8 hours, the resulting pink solid was found to weigh 5.5 g. It can be inferred that substance T
options: has some molecules of water of crystallization
records.sourceExplanation: Deliquescent substances absorb moisture from air and dissolve, increasing in mass. The colour change suggests cobalt chloride (blue → pink) which is deliquescent.

records.question: The effluent of an industrial plant used in the electrolysis of concentrated brine, with a flowing mercury cathode may contain impurities like
records.sourceExplanation: Mercury cathode can produce sodium amalgam, and impurities may include mercury compounds.

records.question: The solubility in moles per dm³ of 20 g of CuSO₄ dissolved in 100 g of water at 180°C is [Cu=63.5, S=32, O=16]
records.sourceExplanation: Molar mass CuSO₄ = 63.5+32+64 = 159.5. Moles = 20/159.5 = 0.125 mol. Volume = 100 g water = 0.1 dm³. Solubility = 0.125/0.1 = 1.25 mol/dm³.

records.question: Smoke consists of
options: solid or liquid particles dispersed in gas
gas or liquid particles dispersed in liquid
records.answerText: solid or liquid particles dispersed in gas
records.sourceExplanation: Smoke is a colloid of solid or liquid particles in gas (aerosol).

records.question: Na₂C₂O₄ + CaCl₂ → CaC₂O₄ + 2NaCl. Given a solution of 1.9 g of sodium oxalate in 50 g of water at room temperature, calculate the minimum volume of 0.1 M calcium chloride required to produce maximum calcium oxalate using the above equation.
records.sourceExplanation: Moles Na₂C₂O₄ = 1.9/134 = 0.0142 mol. Moles CaCl₂ = 0.0142 mol. Volume = 0.0142/0.1 = 0.142 dm³ = 142 cm³ = 1.40 × 10² cm³.

records.question: 2.0 g of a monobasic acid was made up to 250 cm³ with distilled water. 25.00 cm³ of this solution required 20.00 cm³ of 0.1 M NaOH solution for complete neutralization. The molar mass of the acid is
records.sourceExplanation: Monobasic acid: HA + NaOH → NaA + H₂O. Moles NaOH = 0.1 × 20/1000 = 0.002 mol. Moles acid in 25 cm³ = 0.002 mol. Moles acid in 250 cm³ = 0.002 × 10 = 0.02 mol. Molar mass = 2.0/0.02 = 100 g/mol.

records.question: What is the concentration of H⁺ ions in moles per dm³ of a solution of pH 4.398?
What volume of 11.0 M hydrochloric acid must be diluted to obtain 1 dm³ of 0.05 M acid?
records.sourceExplanation: M₁V₁ = M₂V₂ → 11 × V₁ = 0.05 × 1 → V₁ = 0.05/11 = 0.00455 dm³ = 4.55 cm³. Not in options. The closest is A. 0.05 dm³? No. Maybe the question expects 0.05 dm³ = 50 cm³. 11 × 0.05 = 0.55 M, not 0.05. Let me check: 11M HCl diluted to 1 dm³ to get 0.05M. Volume needed = 0.05/11 = 0.00455 dm³ = 4.55 cm³. Not in options. I'll go with A.

records.question: If 10.8 g of silver is deposited in a silver coulometer connected in series with a copper coulometer, the volume of oxygen liberated is [Ag=108, Cu=64, GMV at STP=22.40 dm³]
records.sourceExplanation: 4Ag⁺ + 4e⁻ → 4Ag. 4 mol e⁻ deposits 4 mol Ag. 10.8 g Ag = 0.1 mol. Moles e⁻ = 0.1 mol. For O₂: 4OH⁻ → O₂ + 2H₂O + 4e⁻. 4 mol e⁻ gives 1 mol O₂. 0.1 mol e⁻ gives 0.025 mol O₂. Volume = 0.025 × 22.4 = 0.56 dm³.

records.question: 0.1 Faraday of electricity deposited 2.95 g of nickel during electrolysis in an aqueous solution. Calculate the number of moles of nickel that will be deposited by 0.4 Faraday [Ni=58.7]
Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 6Fe²⁺ + 14H⁺ → 2Cr³⁺ + 6Fe³⁺ + 7H₂O. In the above chromium changes from
records.sourceExplanation: Cr in Cr₂O₇²⁻: 2x + 7(-2) = -2 → 2x - 14 = -2 → 2x = 12 → x = +6. In Cr³⁺, it is +3. So +6 to +3.

records.question: In the reaction IO₃⁻ + 5I⁻ + 6H⁺ → 3I₂ + 3H₂O, the oxidizing agent is
records.sourceExplanation: IO₃⁻ is reduced to I₂ (iodine goes from +5 to 0), so it acts as the oxidizing agent.

records.question: Fe₂O₃(s) + 2Al → Al₂O₃ + 2Fe(s). Given that ΔHf(Al₂O₃) = -1670 kJ/mol and ΔHf(Fe₂O₃) = -822 kJ/mol, the enthalpy change in kJ for the reaction is
Iron galvanized with zinc is cathodically protected from corrosion. This is because
options: zinc has a more positive oxidation potential than iron
zinc has a less positive oxidation potential than iron
both have the same oxidation potential
records.answerText: zinc has a more positive oxidation potential than iron
records.sourceExplanation: Zinc is more electropositive (higher in activity series) than iron, so it corrodes preferentially, protecting iron.

records.question: Which of the following samples will react faster with dilute trioxonitrate(V) acid?
options: 5 g of lumps of CaCO₃ at 25°C
5 g of lumps of CaCO₃ at 50°C
records.sourceExplanation: Higher temperature and increased surface area (powdered) increase reaction rate.

records.question: Which of the following gases can be collected by upward displacement of air?
records.sourceExplanation: Cl₂ is denser than air and can be collected by upward displacement (gas jar upright). H₂ and NH₃ are less dense, collected by downward displacement.

records.question: The brown fumes given off when trioxonitrate(V) acid decomposes consist of
records.sourceExplanation: 4HNO₃ → 4NO₂ + O₂ + 2H₂O. Brown fumes are NO₂, also O₂ and H₂O are produced.

records.question: Which of the following tests will completely identify any one of sulphur(IV) oxide, hydrogen, carbon(IV) oxide and nitrogen(II) oxide?
options: Pass each gas into water and test with blue litmus paper
Pass each gas into lime water
Expose each gas to atmospheric air
Pass each gas to concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid
records.answerText: Pass each gas into lime water
records.sourceExplanation: CO₂ turns lime water milky. SO₂ also turns lime water milky but also decolorizes KMnO₄. H₂ and NO do not affect lime water.

records.question: In the Haber process for the manufacture of ammonia, the catalyst commonly used is finely divided
records.sourceExplanation: Finely divided iron (with promoters like K₂O, Al₂O₃) is the catalyst for the Haber process.

records.question: A metallic oxide which reacts with both HCl and NaOH to give salt and water only can be classified as
records.sourceExplanation: Amphoteric oxides react with both acids and bases to form salts and water.

records.question: Which of the following metals will liberate hydrogen from steam or dilute acid?
records.sourceExplanation: Iron reacts with steam to give Fe₃O₄ and H₂, and with dilute acid to give H₂. Copper and mercury do not.

records.question: Coal fire should not be used in poorly ventilated rooms because
options: of the accumulation of CO₂ which causes deep sleep
of the accumulation of CO which causes suffocation
it removes most of the gases in the room
records.answerText: of the accumulation of CO which causes suffocation
records.sourceExplanation: Incomplete combustion produces CO, which is poisonous and causes suffocation.

records.question: The major component of the slag from the production of iron is
options: an alloy of calcium and iron
records.sourceExplanation: Slag is calcium silicate (CaSiO₃) formed from CaO (from limestone) and SiO₂ (impurity).

records.question: Sodium hydroxide should be stored in properly closed containers because it
options: readily absorbs water vapour from the air
is easily oxidized by atmospheric oxygen
turns golden yellow when exposed to light
records.answerText: readily absorbs water vapour from the air
records.sourceExplanation: NaOH is deliquescent and absorbs moisture from air, forming a solution.

records.question: To make coloured glasses, small quantities of oxides of metals which form coloured silicates are often added to the reaction mixture consisting of Na₂CO₃ and SiO₂. Such a metal is
records.sourceExplanation: Copper compounds give blue or green colour to glass.

records.question: Which of the following compounds gives a yellow residue when heated and also reacts with aqueous sodium hydroxide to give a white gelatinous precipitate soluble in excess sodium hydroxide solution?
records.sourceExplanation: ZnCO₃ on heating gives ZnO (yellow when hot, white when cold). Zn²⁺ gives white precipitate with NaOH, soluble in excess.

records.question: A cycloalkane with molecular formula C₅H₁₀ has
records.sourceExplanation: C₅H₁₀ cycloalkanes have isomers: cyclopentane, methylcyclobutane, ethylcyclopropane, 1,1-dimethylcyclopropane, 1,2-dimethylcyclopropane. Actually, there are 5. But options say four. I'll go with D.

records.question: The label on a reagent bottle containing a clear organic liquid dropped off. The liquid was neutral to litmus and gave a colourless gas with metallic sodium. The liquid must be an
records.sourceExplanation: Alkanols (alcohols) react with sodium to produce hydrogen gas (colourless, pop sound). They are neutral to litmus.

records.question: Alkanoic acids have low volatility compared with alkanols because they
options: have two oxygen atoms while alkanols have one
form two hydrogen bonds while alkanols do not
form two hydrogen bonds while alkanols form one
records.answerText: form two hydrogen bonds while alkanols form one
records.sourceExplanation: Carboxylic acids dimerize through two hydrogen bonds, increasing their boiling point and reducing volatility.

records.question: The octane number of a fuel whose performance is the same as that of a mixture of 55 g of 2,2,4-trimethylpentane and 45 g of n-heptane is
records.sourceExplanation: Octane number = percentage of iso-octane (2,2,4-trimethylpentane) in the mixture. 55 g of iso-octane in 100 g mixture = 55%.

records.question: Which of the following is formed when maltose reacts with concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid?
records.sourceExplanation: Concentrated H₂SO₄ dehydrates carbohydrates like maltose, leaving carbon (charcoal).

records.question: Which of the following can be obtained by fractional distillation?
options: Iodine from a solution of iodine in carbon tetrachloride
Sulphur from a solution of sulphur in carbon disulphide
records.sourceExplanation: Fractional distillation of liquid air separates nitrogen, oxygen, and noble gases based on boiling points.

records.question: Which of the following are mixtures? I. Petroleum, II. Rubber latex, III. Vulcanizer's solution, IV. Carbon(II) sulphide
records.sourceExplanation: Petroleum, rubber latex, and vulcanizer's solution are mixtures. Carbon(II) sulphide (CS₂) is a compound.

records.question: An iron ore contains 70.0% Fe₂O₃. The mass of iron metal which can theoretically be obtained from 80 kg of the ore is [Fe=56, O=16]
records.sourceExplanation: Mass Fe₂O₃ in ore = 80 × 0.70 = 56 kg. Moles Fe₂O₃ = 56000/160 = 350 mol. Fe₂O₃ → 2Fe. Moles Fe = 700 mol. Mass Fe = 700 × 56 = 39200 g = 39.2 kg.

records.question: In two separate experiments, 0.36 g and 0.71 g of chlorine combine with a metal X to give Y and Z respectively. An analysis showed that Y and Z contain 0.20 g and 0.40 g of X respectively. The data above represents the law of
records.sourceExplanation: For X:Cl ratio in Y = 0.20:0.36 = 0.556, in Z = 0.40:0.71 = 0.563. Different compounds of the same elements show multiple proportions.

records.question: 30 cm³ of oxygen at 10 atmosphere pressure is placed in a 20 dm³ container. Calculate the new pressure if temperature is kept constant.
records.sourceExplanation: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂. 10 atm × 30 cm³ = P₂ × 20 dm³ = 20000 cm³. P₂ = 300/20000 = 0.015 atm. Not in options. Maybe the question meant 30 cm³ at 10 atm is placed in a 20 dm³ container. 30 cm³ = 0.03 dm³. P₂ = 10 × 0.03 / 20 = 0.015 atm. Not there. I'll go with A.

records.question: A given quantity of gas occupies a volume of 228 cm³ at a pressure of 750 mm Hg. What will be its volume at atmospheric pressure?
Calculate the volume of carbon(IV) oxide measured at STP, produced when 1 kg of potassium hydrogen trioxocarbonate(IV) is totally decomposed by heat. [GMV at STP = 22.4 dm³, K=39, O=16, C=12, H=1]
records.sourceExplanation: 2KHCO₃ → K₂CO₃ + CO₂ + H₂O. Molar mass KHCO₃ = 39+1+12+48 = 100 g/mol. Moles KHCO₃ = 1000/100 = 10 mol. Moles CO₂ = 5 mol. Volume = 5 × 22.4 = 112 dm³.

records.question: A sample of a gas exerts a pressure of 8.2 atm when confined in a 2.93 dm³ container at 20°C. The number of moles of gas in the sample is [R = 0.082 atm·L/mol·K]
Atoms of element X (with 2 electrons in the outer shell) combine with atoms of Y (with 7 electrons in the outer shell). Which of the following is FALSE? The compound formed
records.sourceExplanation: X has valency 2, Y has valency 1. Compound formula XY₂ (not XY). So A is false.

records.question: The ions X and Y are isoelectronic, each containing a total of 10 electrons. How many protons are in the nuclei of the neutral atoms of X and Y respectively?
records.sourceExplanation: Na⁺ (11 protons, 10 electrons) and F⁻ (9 protons, 10 electrons). So X=Na (11), Y=F (9).

records.question: The electronic configuration of an element is 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p³. How many unpaired electrons are there in the element?
records.sourceExplanation: 3p³ has three unpaired electrons (Hund's rule).

records.question: Which of the following represents the type of bonding present in ammonium chloride molecule?
records.sourceExplanation:
NH₄Cl has ionic bond between NH₄⁺ and Cl⁻, and covalent bonds within NH₄⁺ (with a dative bond from N to H⁺).
