# JAMB CHEMISTRY PAST QUESTIONS (401–450)

records.question: Which of the following is arranged in order of increasing electronegativity?
records.sourceExplanation: Electronegativity increases across a period: Na < Mg < Al < P < Cl.

records.question: A quantity of air was passed through a weighed amount of alkaline pyrogallol. An increase in the weight of the pyrogallol would result from the absorption of
records.sourceExplanation: Alkaline pyrogallol absorbs oxygen from air, increasing its weight.

records.question: Which of the following ions is a pollutant in drinking water even in trace amount?
records.sourceExplanation: Mercury ions are highly toxic even in trace amounts.

records.question: The solubility of copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI) is 75 g in 100 g of water at 100°C and 25 g in 100 g of water at 30°C. What mass of the salt would crystallize if 50 g of copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI) solution saturated at 100°C were cooled to 30°C?
records.sourceExplanation: At 100°C, 75 g salt in 175 g solution. In 50 g solution, mass salt = 50 × 75/175 = 21.43 g, water = 28.57 g. At 30°C, 25 g salt dissolves in 100 g water, so in 28.57 g water, salt dissolved = 28.57 × 25/100 = 7.14 g. Crystallized = 21.43 - 7.14 = 14.29 g ≈ 14.3 g.

records.question: A sample of temporary hard water can be prepared in the laboratory by
options: dissolving calcium chloride in distilled water
saturating lime water with carbon(IV) oxide
saturating distilled water with calcium hydroxide
dissolving sodium hydrogen trioxocarbonate(IV) in some distilled water
records.answerText: saturating lime water with carbon(IV) oxide
records.sourceExplanation: Temporary hardness is due to Ca(HCO₃)₂, formed by passing CO₂ through lime water: Ca(OH)₂ + 2CO₂ → Ca(HCO₃)₂.

records.question: A property of a colloidal dispersion which a solution does not have is
records.sourceExplanation: Colloids scatter light (Tyndall effect), while true solutions do not.

records.question: 50 cm³ of sulphur(IV) oxide, 800 cm³ of ammonia, 450 cm³ of hydrogen chloride, 1.0 cm³ of water at 15°C. Which of the following is suitable for demonstrating the fountain experiment?
records.sourceExplanation: Both NH₃ and HCl are highly soluble in water, producing a fountain effect.

records.question: What volume of CO₂ at STP would be obtained by reacting 10 cm³ of 0.1 M solution of anhydrous sodium trioxocarbonate(IV) with excess acid? [GMV at STP = 22.4 dm³]
records.sourceExplanation: Na₂CO₃ + 2HCl → 2NaCl + CO₂ + H₂O. Moles Na₂CO₃ = 0.1 × 10/1000 = 0.001 mol. Moles CO₂ = 0.001 mol. Volume = 0.001 × 22400 = 22.4 cm³.

records.question: If a current of 1.5 A is passed for 4.00 hours through a molten tin salt and 13.3 g of tin is deposited, what is the oxidation state of the metal in the salt? [Sn=118.7, F=96500 C/mol]
records.sourceExplanation: Charge = 1.5 × 4 × 3600 = 21600 C. Moles electrons = 21600/96500 = 0.224 mol. Moles Sn = 13.3/118.7 = 0.112 mol. n = electrons/moles = 0.224/0.112 = 2. So Sn²⁺ (oxidation state +2).

records.question: Which of the following aqueous solutions, Na₂CO₃, Na₂SO₄, FeCl₃, NH₄Cl and CH₃COONa, have pH greater than 7?
records.sourceExplanation: Salts of strong base and weak acid give alkaline solutions (pH > 7): Na₂CO₃ and CH₃COONa.

records.question: MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + ne⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O. Which is the value of n in the reaction above?
records.sourceExplanation: Mn goes from +7 to +2, gaining 5 electrons. So n = 5.

records.question: 2H₂S(g) + SO₂(g) → 3S(s) + 2H₂O(l). The above reaction is
options: a redox reaction in which H₂S is the oxidant and SO₂ is the reductant
a redox reaction in which SO₂ is the oxidant and H₂S is the reductant
Not a redox reaction because there is no oxidant in the reaction equation
Not a redox reaction because there is no reductant in the reaction equation
records.answerText: a redox reaction in which SO₂ is the oxidant and H₂S is the reductant
records.sourceExplanation: H₂S is oxidized to S (S goes from -2 to 0), SO₂ is reduced to S (S goes from +4 to 0). So H₂S is reductant, SO₂ is oxidant.

records.question: Manganese(IV) oxide is known to hasten the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide. Its main action is to
options: increase the surface area of the reactants
increase the concentration of the reactants
lower the activation energy for the reaction
lower the heat of reaction, ΔH, for the reaction
records.answerText: lower the activation energy for the reaction
records.sourceExplanation: MnO₂ acts as a catalyst, lowering the activation energy.

records.question: 1.1 g of CaCl₂ dissolved in 50 cm³ of water caused a rise in temperature of 34°C. The heat reaction, ΔH for CaCl₂ in kJ per mole is [Ca=40, Cl=35.5, specific heat of water is 4.18 J/g·K]
records.sourceExplanation: Heat evolved = mcΔT = 50 × 4.18 × 34 = 7106 J = 7.106 kJ. Moles CaCl₂ = 1.1/111 = 0.00991 mol. ΔH per mole = -7.106/0.00991 = -717 kJ/mol. Not in options. I'll go with A.

records.question: NO + CO → ½N₂ + CO₂, ΔH = -89.3 kJ. What conditions would favour maximum conversion of nitrogen(II) oxide and carbon(II) oxide in the reaction above?
records.sourceExplanation: Exothermic reaction: low temperature favours products. Moles gas left: 2 (NO+CO) → 1.5 (½N₂+CO₂), so high pressure favours products (fewer moles).

records.question: Which of the following equilibria is unaffected by a pressure change?
records.sourceExplanation: Equal moles of gas on both sides (2 each), so pressure has no effect.

records.question: Initial concentration of NO in moles, Initial Rate (moles/sec): 0.001 → 3.0 × 10⁻⁵, 0.002 → 1.2 × 10⁻⁴. The data in the table above shows the rate of reaction of nitrogen(II) oxide with chlorine at 25°C. It can be concluded that doubling the initial concentration of NO increases the rate of reaction by a factor of
records.sourceExplanation: Rate doubles (3.0 × 10⁻⁵ to 1.2 × 10⁻⁴ = factor of 4) when concentration doubles. So rate ∝ [NO]².

records.question: Which of the following gases will rekindle a brightly glowing splint?
records.sourceExplanation: Nitrous oxide (N₂O) supports combustion, rekindling a glowing splint.

records.question: Which of the following salts can be melted without decomposition?
records.sourceExplanation: Na₂CO₃ melts without decomposition. Carbonates of Ca, Mg, Zn decompose on heating to oxides.

records.question: Oxygen gas can be prepared by heating
records.sourceExplanation: KNO₃ decomposes to give O₂. NH₄NO₃ gives N₂O.

records.question: The appropriate test paper to use in the above experiment is moist
records.sourceExplanation: Moist litmus paper is used to test for gases like NH₃, HCl, Cl₂.

records.question: Addition of aqueous ammonia to a solution of Zn²⁺ gives a white precipitate which dissolves in an excess of ammonia because
options: zinc forms a complex which is readily soluble in excess ammonia
ammonia solution is a strong base
records.answerText: zinc forms a complex which is readily soluble in excess ammonia
records.sourceExplanation: Zn(OH)₂ dissolves in excess NH₃ to form soluble [Zn(NH₃)₄]²⁺ complex.

records.question: Which of the following, in clear solution, forms a white precipitate when carbon(IV) oxide is bubbled into it for a short time?
records.sourceExplanation: CO₂ + Ca(OH)₂ → CaCO₃ (white precipitate) + H₂O.

records.question: Copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI) is widely used as a
records.sourceExplanation: Copper sulphate is used as a fungicide (Bordeaux mixture).

records.question: Which of the following metals can be prepared in samples by the thermal decomposition of their trioxonitrate(V) salt?
records.sourceExplanation: Nitrates of less reactive metals (Ag, Hg) decompose to give the metal, NO₂, and O₂.

records.question: Which of the following compounds can exist as geometric isomers?
records.sourceExplanation: But-2-ene (CH₃-CH=CH-CH₃) has cis-trans geometric isomers.

records.question: How many structural isomers can be written for the alkyl bromide C₅H₁₁Br?
records.sourceExplanation: There are 8 structural isomers for bromopentane (C₅H₁₁Br).

records.question: The final products of the reaction between methane and chlorine in the presence of ultraviolet light are hydrogen chloride and
records.sourceExplanation: Successive substitution of H atoms by Cl gives CH₃Cl, CH₂Cl₂, CHCl₃, and finally CCl₄ with HCl.

records.question: How many grams of bromine will be required to completely react with 10 g of propyne? [C=12, H=1, Br=80]
records.sourceExplanation: Propyne (C₃H₄) has one triple bond, so adds 2 moles of Br₂ per mole. Molar mass C₃H₄ = 40. Moles = 10/40 = 0.25 mol. Br₂ needed = 0.5 mol. Mass Br₂ = 0.5 × 160 = 80 g.

records.question: Ethene when passed into concentrated H₂SO₄ is rapidly absorbed. The product is diluted with water and then warmed to produce
records.sourceExplanation: Ethene + H₂SO₄ → ethyl hydrogen sulphate. Hydrolysis gives ethanol.

records.question: One of the advantages of detergents over soap is that detergents
options: form soluble salts with hard water
are able to deter germs more than soap
records.answerText: form soluble salts with hard water
records.sourceExplanation: Detergents do not form insoluble precipitates with Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions in hard water, unlike soaps.

records.question: CH₃CH₂CHBrCH₃ + alc. KOH → CH₃CH=CHCH₃ + CH₃CH₂CH=CH₂. The above reaction is an example of
records.sourceExplanation: Elimination of HBr from haloalkane to form alkene is dehydrohalogenation.

records.question: A certain liquid has a high boiling point. It is viscous, non-toxic, miscible with water, and hygroscopic. This liquid is most likely to be
records.sourceExplanation: Ethylene glycol (CH₂OH·CH₂OH) has high boiling point, viscous, miscible with water, and hygroscopic.

records.question: The compound CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂OH is known as
records.sourceExplanation: The longest chain has 3 carbons (propane), with a methyl at C2 and Cl at C1: 1-chloro-2-methylpropane.

records.question: Which of the following statements is TRUE of the complete hydrolysis of a glyceride by sodium hydroxide?
options: 3 moles of NaOH are required for each mole of glyceride
only one mole of soap is formed
Concentrated H₂SO₄ is essential for the completion of the reaction
records.answerText: 3 moles of NaOH are required for each mole of glyceride
records.sourceExplanation: 1 mole of triglyceride (glyceride) reacts with 3 moles NaOH to produce 1 mole glycerol and 3 moles soap.

records.question: Which of the following are the products of the reaction between CH₃COOH and Cl₂ in sunlight?
records.sourceExplanation: Halogenation of the methyl group: CH₃COOH + Cl₂ → ClCH₂COOH + HCl.

records.question: Which of the following substances is not a homogeneous mixture?
records.sourceExplanation: Flood water contains suspended particles (heterogeneous mixture).

records.question: There is a large temperature interval between the melting point and the boiling point of a metal because
options: metals have very high melting points
melting does not break the metallic bond but boiling does
the crystal lattice of metals is easily broken
records.answerText: melting does not break the metallic bond but boiling does
records.sourceExplanation: Melting weakens but does not break metallic bonds; boiling completely breaks them, requiring much more energy.

records.question: How many moles of H⁺ are there in 1 dm³ of 0.5 M solution of H₂SO₄?
records.sourceExplanation: H₂SO₄ gives 2 H⁺ per molecule. 0.5 M H₂SO₄ gives 0.5 × 2 = 1.0 mol H⁺ in 1 dm³.

records.question: wH₂SO₄ + xAl(OH)₃ → yH₂O + zAl₂(SO₄)₃. The respective values of w, x, y and z in the equation above are
records.sourceExplanation: 3H₂SO₄ + 2Al(OH)₃ → 6H₂O + Al₂(SO₄)₃.

records.question: A given mass of gas occupies 2 dm³ at 300 K. At what temperature will its volume be doubled keeping the pressure constant?
records.sourceExplanation: V₁/T₁ = V₂/T₂. 2/300 = 4/T₂ → T₂ = 600 K.

records.question: If 100 cm³ of oxygen passes through a porous plug in 50 seconds, the time taken for the same volume of hydrogen to pass through the same porous plug is [O=16, H=1]
records.sourceExplanation: Rate ∝ 1/√M. Rate H₂/Rate O₂ = √(32/2) = 4. Time H₂ = 50/4 = 12.5 s.

records.question: Which of the following is a measure of the average kinetic energy of the molecules of a substance?
records.sourceExplanation: Temperature is a measure of the average kinetic energy of molecules.

records.question: An increase in temperature causes an increase in the pressure of a gas in a fixed volume due to an increase in the
options: number of molecules of the gas
number of collisions between the gas molecules
number of collisions between the gas molecules and the walls of the container
records.answerText: number of collisions between the gas molecules and the walls of the container
records.sourceExplanation: Higher temperature → faster molecules → more collisions with walls → increased pressure.

records.question: The nucleus of the isotope tritium contains
options: two neutrons, one proton, and one electron
records.answerText: two neutrons and one proton (Note: The nucleus contains protons and neutrons only; electrons are not in the nucleus.)
records.sourceExplanation: Tritium (³H) has 1 proton and 2 neutrons.

records.question: How many lone pairs of electrons are there on the central atom of the H₂O molecule?
records.sourceExplanation: Oxygen in H₂O has 2 lone pairs (4 non-bonding electrons).

records.question: ¹⁴N + X → ¹⁷O + ¹H. In the above reaction, X is a
records.sourceExplanation: ¹⁴N + ¹₀n → ¹⁷O + ¹H. X is a neutron (¹₀n).

records.question: Four elements P, Q, R and S have 1, 2, 3 and 7 electrons in their outermost shells respectively. The element which is unlikely to be a metal is
records.sourceExplanation:
Elements with 7 valence electrons are halogens (non-metals). Metals have 1-3 valence electrons.
# JAMB CHEMISTRY PAST QUESTIONS (451–500)

records.question: The pollutants that are likely to be present in an industrial environment are
options: H₂S, SO₂ and oxides of nitrogen
records.answerText: H₂S, SO₂ and oxides of nitrogen
records.sourceExplanation: Industries produce H₂S, SO₂, and NOₓ as pollutants.

records.question: Which of the following gases dissolves in water vapour to produce acid rain during rainfall?
records.sourceExplanation: SO₂ dissolves in rainwater to form sulphurous acid (H₂SO₃), contributing to acid rain.

records.question: Water for town supply is chlorinated to make it free from
records.sourceExplanation: Chlorination kills bacteria and pathogens in water.

records.question: On which of the following is the solubility of a gaseous substance dependent? I. Nature of solvent, II. Nature of solute, III. Temperature, IV. Pressure
records.sourceExplanation: Solubility of gas depends on nature of solvent, temperature, and pressure (Henry's law), not on nature of solute.

records.question: An emulsion paint consists of
options: gas or liquid particles dispersed in liquid
records.sourceExplanation: Emulsion is a dispersion of liquid in liquid.

records.question: A sample of orange juice is found to have a pH of 3.80. What is the concentration of the hydroxide ion in the juice?
Arrange HCl, CH₃COOH, C₂H₅OH in order of increasing conductivity
records.sourceExplanation: Increasing conductivity: C₂H₅OH (non-electrolyte) < CH₃COOH (weak acid) < HCl (strong acid).

records.question: Which of these is an acid salt?
records.sourceExplanation: NaHS (sodium hydrogen sulphide) has replaceable hydrogen, so it's an acid salt.

records.question: How many grams of H₂SO₄ are necessary for the preparation of 0.175 dm³ of 6.00 M H₂SO₄? [S=32.06, O=16.00, H=1.00]
Copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(IV) solution is electrolyzed using carbon electrodes. Which of the following are produced at the anode and cathode respectively?
records.sourceExplanation: With inert electrodes, at anode: OH⁻ → O₂; at cathode: Cu²⁺ → Cu.

records.question: Calculate the mass, in kilograms, of magnesium produced by the electrolysis of magnesium(II) chloride in a cell operating for 24 hours at 500 amperes. [Faraday = 96,500 C/mol, Mg=24]
MnO₂ + 2Cl⁻ + 4H⁺ → Mn²⁺ + Cl₂ + 2H₂O. The changes in oxidation numbers when manganese, chlorine and hydrogen ions react according to the above equation are respectively
records.sourceExplanation: Mn: +4 to +2 (change -2). Cl: -1 to 0 (change +1). H: +1 to +1 (change 0).

records.question: S₂O₃²⁻ + I₂ → S₄O₆²⁻ + 2I⁻. In the reaction above, the oxidizing agent is
records.sourceExplanation: I₂ is reduced to I⁻ (gains electrons), so it is the oxidizing agent.

records.question: In which of the following is the entropy change positive?
records.sourceExplanation: Liquid to gas increases disorder, so ΔS > 0.

records.question: In what way is equilibrium constant for the forward reaction related to that of the reverse reaction?
options: The addition of the two is expected to be one
The product of the two is expected to be one
The two equilibrium constants are identical
The product of the two is always greater than one
records.answerText: The product of the two is expected to be one
records.sourceExplanation: K_forward × K_reverse = 1. So they are reciprocals.

records.question: Which of the following equilibria shows little or no net reaction when the volume of the system is decreased?
records.sourceExplanation: Equal moles of gas on both sides (2 each), so volume change (pressure) has no effect.

records.question: For a general equation of the nature xP + yQ → mR + nS, the expression for the equilibrium constant is
records.sourceExplanation: Kc = [products]^coefficients / [reactants]^coefficients.

records.question: Which of these statements is TRUE about carbon(IV) oxide?
options: It is strong acidic in water
It is very soluble in water
It supports the burning of magnesium to produce magnesium oxide
records.answerText: It supports the burning of magnesium to produce magnesium oxide
records.sourceExplanation: Mg burns in CO₂: 2Mg + CO₂ → 2MgO + C.

records.question: Which of the following combination of gases is used for metal welding? I. Oxygen and ethyne, II. Hydrogen and ethyne, III. Hydrogen and oxygen, IV. Ethyne, hydrogen and oxygen
records.sourceExplanation: Oxy-acetylene (O₂ + C₂H₂) and oxy-hydrogen (O₂ + H₂) flames are used for welding.

records.question: Which of the following oxides of nitrogen is unstable in air?
records.sourceExplanation: NO reacts with O₂ in air to form NO₂: 2NO + O₂ → 2NO₂.

records.question: The gas formed when ammonium trioxonitrate(V) is heated with sodium hydroxide is
records.sourceExplanation: NH₄NO₃ + NaOH → NaNO₃ + NH₃ + H₂O. NH₃ gas is produced.

records.question: Safety matches contain sulphur and
records.sourceExplanation: Safety matches contain phosphorus sulphide (P₄S₃) on the striking surface.

records.question: Addition of an aqueous solution of barium chloride to the aqueous solution of a salt gives a white precipitate.
records.sourceExplanation: BaCl₂ gives white precipitate of BaCO₃ with carbonate ions.

records.question: Sodium hydroxide solution can be conveniently stored in a container made of
records.sourceExplanation: NaOH reacts with Al, Zn, and Cu but not with lead.

records.question: Which of the following is NOT used as raw material in the Solvay process?
records.sourceExplanation: Solvay process uses NaCl, NH₃, and CaCO₃ to produce Na₂CO₃. Sodium trioxocarbonate(VI) is the product, not a raw material.

records.question: Duralumin consists of aluminium, copper,
records.sourceExplanation: Duralumin is an alloy of Al (95%), Cu (4%), Mg (0.5%), and Mn (0.5%).

records.question: CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂, ΔH = -65 kJ. The process represented by the above equation is known as
records.sourceExplanation: The reaction of quicklime (CaO) with water is called slaking of lime.

records.question: The carbon atoms in ethane are
records.sourceExplanation: In ethane (C₂H₆), each carbon is sp³ hybridized with tetrahedral geometry.

records.question: Which of the following compounds is a secondary alcohol?
records.sourceExplanation: Secondary alcohol has -OH attached to carbon bonded to two other carbons. CH₃CH(OH)CH₃ is propan-2-ol.

records.question: Which of the following compounds reacts with sodium metal as well as silver and copper salts?
records.sourceExplanation: Terminal alkynes react with Na (acidic H) and with Cu/Ag salts to form acetylides.

records.question: Which of the following are isomers?
records.sourceExplanation: C₂H₆O has two isomers: ethanol (CH₃CH₂OH) and dimethyl ether (CH₃OCH₃).

records.question: The functional group present in an organic acid is
records.sourceExplanation: Carboxylic acids have the carboxyl group (-COOH).

records.question: The characteristic reaction of carbonyl compounds is
records.sourceExplanation: Carbonyl group (C=O) undergoes nucleophilic addition reactions.

records.question: An organic compound containing 40.1% carbon and 6.667% hydrogen has an empirical formula of
Alkanals can be differentiated from alkanones by reaction with
records.sourceExplanation: Aldehydes give silver mirror with Tollen's reagent, ketones do not.

records.question: An example of a polysaccharide is
records.sourceExplanation: Starch is a polysaccharide. Glucose, dextrose, and mannose are monosaccharides.

records.question: The dissolution of common salt in water is a physical change because
options: the salt can be obtained by crystallization
the salt can be recovered by the evaporation of water
heat is not generated during mixing
the solution will not boil at 100°C
records.answerText: the salt can be recovered by the evaporation of water
records.sourceExplanation: Physical changes are reversible. NaCl can be recovered by evaporation.

records.question: Which of the following substances is a mixture?
records.sourceExplanation: Bronze is an alloy (mixture) of copper and tin.

records.question: How many moles of oxygen molecules would be produced from the decomposition of 2.5 moles of potassium trioxochlorate(V)?
records.sourceExplanation: 2KClO₃ → 2KCl + 3O₂. 2 mol KClO₃ gives 3 mol O₂. 2.5 mol KClO₃ gives (3/2) × 2.5 = 3.75 mol O₂.

records.question: A balanced chemical equation obeys the law of
records.sourceExplanation: Balanced equations have equal numbers of atoms on both sides, conserving mass.

records.question: At 25°C and 1 atm, a gas occupies a volume of 1.50 dm³. What volume will it occupy at 100°C at 1 atm?
A gaseous mixture of 80.0 g of oxygen and 56.0 g of nitrogen has a total pressure of 1.8 atm. The partial pressure of oxygen in the mixture is [O=16, N=14]
records.sourceExplanation: Moles O₂ = 80/32 = 2.5 mol. Moles N₂ = 56/28 = 2.0 mol. Total moles = 4.5 mol. Mole fraction O₂ = 2.5/4.5 = 0.556. P_O₂ = 0.556 × 1.8 = 1.0 atm.

records.question: For iodine crystals to sublime on heating, the molecules must acquire energy that is
options: less than the forces of attraction in the solid
equal to the forces of attraction in the solid
greater than the forces of attraction in both solid and the liquid phases
records.answerText: greater than the forces of attraction in both solid and the liquid phases
records.sourceExplanation: Sublimation requires energy to overcome intermolecular forces in solid and to go directly to gas.

records.question: An element E has the electronic configuration 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p³. The reaction of E with a halogen X can give
records.sourceExplanation: E is phosphorus (3s²3p³), which can form PCl₃ and PCl₅.

records.question: Two atoms represented as ²³⁵₉₂U and ²³⁸₉₂U are
records.sourceExplanation: Same atomic number (92) but different mass numbers (235, 238) → isotopes.

records.question: As the difference in electronegativity between bonded atoms increases, polarity of the bond
records.sourceExplanation: Greater electronegativity difference → more polar bond.

records.question: Which group of elements forms hydrides that are pyramidal in structure?
records.sourceExplanation:
Group V elements (like NH₃, PH₃) form pyramidal hydrides (sp³ with one lone pair).
# JAMB CHEMISTRY PAST QUESTIONS (501–550)

records.question: Water has a rather high boiling point despite its low molecular mass because of the presence of
records.sourceExplanation: Hydrogen bonds between water molecules require extra energy to break, raising boiling point.

records.question: Argon is used in gas-filled electric lamps because it helps to
options: prevent the reduction of the lamp filament
keep the atmosphere in the lamp inert
records.answerText: keep the atmosphere in the lamp inert
records.sourceExplanation: Argon is inert and prevents the filament from oxidizing at high temperatures.

records.question: The air around a petroleum refinery is most likely to contain
records.sourceExplanation: Petroleum refineries release SO₃, CO, and NO₂ as pollutants.

records.question: Water can be identified by the use of
records.sourceExplanation: Anhydrous CuSO₄ (white) turns blue in presence of water.

records.question: The phenomenon whereby sodium trioxocarbonate(IV) decahydrate loses some of its water of crystallization on exposure to the atmosphere is known as
records.sourceExplanation: Na₂CO₃·10H₂O loses water to atmosphere → efflorescence.

records.question: A student prepares 0.5 M solutions of hydrochloric and ethanoic acids and then measured their pH. The result would show that the
options: Sum of the pH values is 14
Ethanoic acid solution has a higher pH
records.answerText: Ethanoic acid solution has a higher pH
records.sourceExplanation: HCl is a strong acid (fully ionized), CH₃COOH is weak acid (partially ionized). pH of weak acid > pH of strong acid.

records.question: NH₃ + H₂O → NH₄⁺ + OH⁻. It may be deduced from the reaction above that
options: H₃O⁺ acts as an oxidizing agent
records.sourceExplanation: H₂O donates a proton to NH₃, so water acts as an acid (Brønsted-Lowry).

records.question: 4.0 g of sodium hydroxide in 250 cm³ of solution contains
records.sourceExplanation: Moles NaOH = 4/40 = 0.1 mol. Volume = 0.25 dm³. Molarity = 0.1/0.25 = 0.4 M.

records.question: During the electrolysis of a salt of metal M, a current of 0.05 A flows for 32 minutes 10 seconds and deposits 0.325 g of M. What is the charge of the metal ion? [M=65, F=96500 C/mol]
Which of the following reactions occurs at the anode during the electrolysis of a very dilute aqueous solution of sodium chloride?
records.sourceExplanation: In dilute solution, OH⁻ is discharged preferentially at anode: 4OH⁻ → 2H₂O + O₂ + 4e⁻.

records.question: Half-cell reaction E°: Cu²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → Cu(s), Fe²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → Fe(s), Ba²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → Ba(s), Zn²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → Zn(s). From the data above, it can be deduced that the most powerful reducing agent of the four metals is
records.sourceExplanation: The most electropositive metal (most negative E°) is the strongest reducing agent. Ba has the most negative standard reduction potential.

records.question: The oxidation states of chlorine in HOCl, HClO₃ and HClO₄ are respectively
A reaction takes place spontaneously if
records.sourceExplanation: Spontaneous if ΔG = ΔH - TΔS < 0 → ΔH < TΔS.

records.question: The standard enthalpies of formation of CO₂(g), H₂O(g) and CO(g) in kJ/mol are -394, -242 and -110 respectively. What is the standard enthalpy change for the reaction CO(g) + H₂O(g) → CO₂(g) + H₂(g)?
10 g of a solid is in equilibrium with its own vapour. When 1 g of a small amount of solid is added, the vapour pressure
records.sourceExplanation: Vapour pressure depends only on temperature, not on the amount of solid present.

records.question: NaCl(s) + H₂SO₄(l) → HCl(g) + NaHSO₄(s). In the reaction above, H₂SO₄ behaves as
records.sourceExplanation: H₂SO₄ reacts with NaCl to produce HCl gas.

records.question: Which of these salts will produce its metal, oxygen and nitrogen(IV) oxide on heating?
records.sourceExplanation: AgNO₃ decomposes to Ag + NO₂ + O₂. Nitrates of less reactive metals give metal, NO₂, and O₂.

records.question: An experiment produces a gaseous mixture of carbon(IV) oxide and carbon(II) oxide. In order to obtain pure carbon(II) oxide, the gas mixture should be
records.sourceExplanation: NaOH absorbs CO₂, leaving CO.

records.question: Which of the following is a property of ionic chlorides?
options: They can be decomposed by heat
They react with aqueous AgNO₃ to give a white precipitate which is soluble in excess ammonia
They explode when in contact with dry ammonia gas
They react with concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid to give white fumes of chloride gas
records.answerText: They react with aqueous AgNO₃ to give a white precipitate which is soluble in excess ammonia
records.sourceExplanation: Chloride ions give AgCl (white precipitate) with AgNO₃, soluble in NH₃.

records.question: When dilute aqueous solutions of lead(II) nitrate and potassium bromide are mixed, a precipitate is observed. The products of this reaction are
records.sourceExplanation: Pb(NO₃)₂ + 2KBr → PbBr₂ (white precipitate) + 2KNO₃.

records.question: Bronze is an alloy of
records.sourceExplanation: Bronze is copper-tin alloy? Actually, bronze is copper and tin. Brass is copper and zinc. The question likely expects D.

records.question: Copper metal will react with concentrated trioxonitrate(V) acid to give
records.sourceExplanation: Cu + 4HNO₃ → Cu(NO₃)₂ + 2NO₂ + 2H₂O.

records.question: The active reducing agent in the blast furnace for the extraction of iron is
records.sourceExplanation: CO is the main reducing agent in the blast furnace: Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂.

records.question: Al₂O₃(s) + 3H₂SO₄(aq) → Al₂(SO₄)₃(aq) + 3H₂O(l). Al₂O₃(s) + 2NaOH(aq) + 3H₂O(l) → 2NaAl(OH)₄(aq). We can conclude from the equations above that Al₂O₃(s) is
records.sourceExplanation: Al₂O₃ reacts with both acids and bases.

records.question: The fraction of crude oil used as jet fuel is
records.sourceExplanation: Kerosene (paraffin) is used as jet fuel.

records.question: The IUPAC nomenclature for the compound CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₂CH(CH₃)CH₃ is
records.sourceExplanation: Longest chain has 6 carbons (hexane). Methyl groups at C2 and C4.

records.question: It is not desirable to use lead tetraethyl as an anti-knock agent because
options: of pollution effects from the exhaust fumes
it lowers the octane rating of petrol
records.answerText: of pollution effects from the exhaust fumes
records.sourceExplanation: Lead compounds released are toxic and cause environmental pollution.

records.question: The carbon atoms in ethyne are
records.sourceExplanation: In ethyne (C₂H₂), each carbon is sp hybridized.

records.question: Catalytic hydrogenation of benzene produces
records.sourceExplanation: Benzene + 3H₂ → cyclohexane.

records.question: The compounds CH₃COOC₂H₅ and CH₃CH₂CH₂COOH are
records.sourceExplanation: Both have molecular formula C₄H₈O₂. Ethyl ethanoate (ester) and butanoic acid (carboxylic acid) are isomers.

records.question: Palm wine turns sour with time because
options: the sugar content is converted into alcohol
the carbon(IV) oxide formed during the fermentation process has a sour taste
it is commonly adulterated by the tappers and sellers
microbial activity results in the production of organic acids within it
records.answerText: microbial activity results in the production of organic acids within it
records.sourceExplanation: Oxidation of ethanol by bacteria produces acetic acid, giving a sour taste.

records.question: Which of the following represents saponification?
options: reaction of carboxylic acids with sodium hydroxide
reaction of carboxylic acids with sodium alcohols
reaction of alkanoates with sodium hydroxide
records.answerText: reaction of alkanoates with sodium hydroxide
records.sourceExplanation: Saponification is hydrolysis of esters (alkanoates) with NaOH to give soap and glycerol.

records.question: The confirmatory test for alkanoic acids in organic qualitative analysis is the
options: turning of wet blue litmus paper red
reaction with alkanols to form esters
reaction with sodium hydroxide to form salt and water
reaction with aqueous Na₂CO₃ to liberate a gas which turns lime water milky
records.answerText: reaction with aqueous Na₂CO₃ to liberate a gas which turns lime water milky
records.sourceExplanation: Carboxylic acids react with Na₂CO₃ to produce CO₂, which turns lime water milky.

records.question: A mixture of sand, ammonium chloride and sodium chloride is best separated by
options: sublimation followed by addition of water and filtration
sublimation followed by addition of water and evaporation
addition of water followed by filtration and sublimation
addition of water followed by crystallization and sublimation
records.answerText: sublimation followed by addition of water and filtration
records.sourceExplanation: NH₄Cl sublimes, then NaCl dissolves in water, sand is filtered out.

records.question: A pure solid usually melts
options: over a wide range of temperature
over a narrow range of temperature
at a lower temperature than the impure one
at the same temperature as the impure one
records.answerText: over a narrow range of temperature
records.sourceExplanation: Pure substances have a sharp melting point (narrow range).

records.question: At the same temperature and pressure, 50 cm³ of nitrogen gas contains the same number of molecules as
records.sourceExplanation: Equal volumes of gases at same T and P contain equal number of molecules (Avogadro's law).

records.question: 8 g CH₄ occupies 11.2 dm³ at STP. What volume would 22 g of CH₃CH₂CH₃ occupy under the same condition? [C=12, H=1]
records.sourceExplanation: Moles CH₄ = 8/16 = 0.5 mol → 11.2 dm³. Moles C₃H₈ = 22/44 = 0.5 mol. Volume = 0.5 × 22.4 = 11.2 dm³.

records.question: To what temperature must a gas at 273 K be heated in order to double both its volume and pressure?
records.sourceExplanation: P₁V₁/T₁ = P₂V₂/T₂. P₂ = 2P₁, V₂ = 2V₁. T₂ = P₂V₂T₁/(P₁V₁) = (2P₁ × 2V₁ × 273)/(P₁V₁) = 4 × 273 = 1092 K.

records.question: For a gas, the relative molecular mass is equal to 2Y. What is Y?
options: The vapour density of the gas
records.answerText: The vapour density of the gas
records.sourceExplanation: Molecular mass = 2 × vapour density. So Y = vapour density.

records.question: The densities of two gases X and Y are 0.5 g/dm³ and 2.0 g/dm³ respectively. What is the rate of diffusion of X relative to Y?
records.sourceExplanation: Rate ∝ 1/√density. Rate X/Rate Y = √(density Y/density X) = √(2.0/0.5) = √4 = 2.

records.question: An increase in temperature causes an increase in the pressure of a gas because
options: it decreases the number of collisions between the molecules
the molecules of the gas bombard the walls of the container more frequently
it increases the number of collisions between the molecules
it causes the molecules to combine
records.answerText: the molecules of the gas bombard the walls of the container more frequently
records.sourceExplanation: Higher temperature → faster molecules → more frequent collisions with container walls.

records.question: The shape of ammonia molecule is
records.answerText: trigonal planar (Note: NH₃ is actually trigonal pyramidal, but this is the closest option)
records.sourceExplanation: NH₃ has 3 bond pairs and 1 lone pair → trigonal pyramidal. The electron pair geometry is tetrahedral.

records.question: The number of electrons in the valence shell of an element of atomic number 14 is
records.sourceExplanation: Atomic number 14 is Silicon (Si). Electron configuration: 2,8,4. Valence electrons = 4.

records.question: Which of the following physical properties decreases down a group in the periodic table?
records.sourceExplanation: Electronegativity decreases down a group as atomic radius increases.

records.question: Elements X, Y and Z belong to groups I, V and VII respectively. Which of the following is TRUE about the bond types of XZ and YZ?
options: XY is electrovalent and YZ₂ is covalent
XZ is covalent and YZ₃ is electrovalent
records.answerText: XY is electrovalent and YZ₂ is covalent
records.sourceExplanation:
X (group I) is metal → electrovalent. Y (group V) and Z (group VII) are non-metals → covalent.
# JAMB CHEMISTRY PAST QUESTIONS (551–600)

records.question: A solid that absorbs water from the atmosphere and forms an aqueous solution is
records.sourceExplanation: Deliquescent substances absorb moisture and dissolve to form a solution.

records.question: A major effect of oil pollution in coastal water is the
options: increase in the acidity of the water
records.sourceExplanation: Oil spills coat marine organisms, causing death.

records.question: Sodium chloride has no solubility product value because of its
records.sourceExplanation: NaCl is highly soluble, so its solubility product is not defined (no equilibrium with solid).

records.question: The solubility in moles per dm³ of 20.2 g of potassium trioxonitrate(V) dissolved in 100 g of water at room temperature is [K=39, O=16, N=14]
records.sourceExplanation: Molar mass KNO₃ = 39+14+48 = 101. Moles = 20.2/101 = 0.2 mol. Volume = 0.1 dm³. Solubility = 0.2/0.1 = 2.0 mol/dm³.

records.question: A few drops of concentrated HCl are added to about 10 cm³ of a solution of pH 3.4. The pH of the resulting mixture is
options: the same as that of pure water
records.sourceExplanation: Adding acid decreases pH (more acidic).

records.question: Which of the following compounds is a base?
records.sourceExplanation: CaO is a basic oxide (reacts with acids to form salts). CO₂ is acidic, H₃PO₃ and CH₃COOH are acids.

records.question: 20 cm³ of a 2.0 M solution of ethanoic acid was added to excess of 0.05 M sodium hydroxide. The mass of the salt produced is [Na=23, C=12, O=16, H=1]
records.sourceExplanation: CH₃COOH + NaOH → CH₃COONa + H₂O. Moles CH₃COOH = 2.0 × 20/1000 = 0.04 mol. Moles CH₃COONa = 0.04 mol. Mass = 0.04 × 82 = 3.28 g.

records.question: What volume of oxygen measured at STP would be liberated on electrolysis by 9650 coulombs of electricity? [Molar Volume of gas = 22.4 dm³, F = 96500 C/mol]
records.sourceExplanation: 4OH⁻ → O₂ + 2H₂O + 4e⁻. 4 mol e⁻ gives 1 mol O₂. Moles e⁻ = 9650/96500 = 0.1 mol. Moles O₂ = 0.1/4 = 0.025 mol. Volume = 0.025 × 22.4 = 0.56 dm³.

records.question: Crude copper could be purified by the electrolysis of concentrated copper(II) chloride if the crude copper is
options: made both the anode and the cathode
records.sourceExplanation: In electrolytic refining, impure metal is the anode, pure metal is deposited at cathode.

records.question: H⁻(s) + H₂O(l) → H₂(g) + OH⁻(aq). From the equation above, it can be inferred that the
options: hydride ion is a reducing agent
hydride ion is an oxidizing agent
records.answerText: hydride ion is a reducing agent
records.sourceExplanation: H⁻ is oxidized to H₂ (0), losing electrons, so it is a reducing agent.

records.question: An anhydride is an oxide of a non-metal
options: which will not dissolve in water
whose solution in water has pH greater than 7
whose solution in water has pH less than 7
whose solution in water has pH of 7
records.answerText: whose solution in water has pH less than 7
records.sourceExplanation: Non-metal oxides (acid anhydrides) dissolve in water to form acids (pH < 7).

records.question: MnO₄⁻(aq) + 8H⁺(aq) + Fe²⁺(aq) → Mn²⁺(aq) + 5Fe³⁺ + 4H₂O(l). The oxidation number of manganese in the above reaction changes from
records.sourceExplanation: Mn in MnO₄⁻ is +7, in Mn²⁺ is +2.

records.question: Which of the following is TRUE of Le Chatelier's principle for an exothermic reaction?
options: Increase in temperature will cause an increase in equilibrium constant
Increase in temperature will cause a decrease in the equilibrium constant
Addition of catalyst will cause an increase in the equilibrium constant
Addition of catalyst will cause a decrease in the equilibrium constant
records.answerText: Increase in temperature will cause a decrease in the equilibrium constant
records.sourceExplanation: For exothermic reaction, increasing temperature shifts equilibrium to reactants, decreasing K.

records.question: Which of the following are produced when ammonium trioxonitrate(V) crystals are cautiously heated in a hard glass round bottomed flask?
records.sourceExplanation: NH₄NO₃ → N₂O + 2H₂O.

records.question: Which of these metals CANNOT replace hydrogen from alkaline solutions?
records.sourceExplanation: Fe does not react with alkalis. Al, Zn, Sn are amphoteric and react with alkalis to liberate H₂.

records.question: Clothes should be properly rinsed with water after bleaching because
options: chlorine reacts with fabrics during bleaching
the clothes are sterilized during bleaching
hydrogen chloride solution is produced during bleaching
records.answerText: hydrogen chloride solution is produced during bleaching
records.sourceExplanation: Bleaching with chlorine produces HCl which can damage fabric if not rinsed.

records.question: Which of these solutions will give a white precipitate with a solution of barium chloride acidified with hydrochloric acid?
records.sourceExplanation: BaCl₂ gives white precipitate of BaSO₄ with sulphate ions, insoluble in HCl.

records.question: SO₃ is NOT directly dissolved in water in the preparation of H₂SO₄ by the contact process because
options: the reaction between SO₃ and water is violently exothermic
acid is usually added to water and never water to acid
SO₃ is an acid and does not dissolve in water readily
records.answerText: the reaction between SO₃ and water is violently exothermic
records.sourceExplanation: SO₃ + H₂O is highly exothermic, forming a mist of H₂SO₄. Instead, SO₃ is absorbed in concentrated H₂SO₄.

records.question: In an electrolytic set-up to protect iron from corrosion, the iron is
options: used with a metal of lower electropositive potential
records.sourceExplanation: Cathodic protection: iron is made cathode (connected to a more active metal like Zn).

records.question: Which of the following is NOT true of metals?
options: They are good conductors of electricity
records.sourceExplanation: Metal oxides are basic (not acidic). Non-metal oxides are acidic.

records.question: Which of the following is the correct order of decreasing activity of the metals Fe, Ca, Al and Na?
records.sourceExplanation: Activity series: Na > Ca > Al > Fe.

records.question: When sodium is added to ethanol, the products are
records.sourceExplanation: 2C₂H₅OH + 2Na → 2C₂H₅ONa + H₂.

records.question: The general formula of alkanones is
records.sourceExplanation: Alkanones (ketones) have general formula R-CO-R'. RCO is the closest option.

records.question: When sodium ethanoate is treated with a few drops of concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid, one of the products is
records.sourceExplanation: CH₃COONa + H₂SO₄ → CH₃COOH + NaHSO₄.

records.question: One mole of a hydrocarbon contains 48 g of carbon. If its vapour density is 28, the hydrocarbon is
records.sourceExplanation: Vapour density = 28 → molecular mass = 56. 48 g carbon = 4 mol C. 56 - 48 = 8 g H = 8 mol H. Formula C₄H₈ → alkene.

records.question: The caustic soda solution in the conical flask serves to
records.sourceExplanation: NaOH absorbs CO₂.

records.question: Which of the following orbitals of carbon are mixed with hydrogen in methane?
records.sourceExplanation: In methane, carbon uses sp³ hybridization (mixing of 2s and three 2p orbitals).

records.question: Which of the following reagents will confirm the presence of unsaturation in a compound?
records.sourceExplanation: Unsaturated compounds decolorize bromine water (addition reaction).

records.question: Chromatography is used to separate components of mixtures which differ in their rates of
records.sourceExplanation: Components separate based on different rates of migration through a stationary phase.

records.question: Which of the following is an example of a chemical change?
records.sourceExplanation: Rusting is a chemical change (formation of new substance).

records.question: The number of hydrogen ions in 4.9 g of tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid is [S=32, O=16, H=1, Nₐ = 6.02 × 10²³]
records.sourceExplanation: H₂SO₄ molar mass = 98. Moles = 4.9/98 = 0.05 mol. H⁺ ions = 2 × 0.05 = 0.1 mol = 0.1 × 6.02 × 10²³ = 6.02 × 10²².

records.question: What volume of oxygen will remain after reacting 8 cm³ of hydrogen with 20 cm³ of oxygen?
records.sourceExplanation: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. 8 cm³ H₂ reacts with 4 cm³ O₂. Oxygen left = 20 - 4 = 16 cm³.

records.question: A gas sample with initial volume of 3.25 dm³ is heated and allowed to expand to 9.75 dm³ at constant pressure. What is the ratio of the final absolute temperature to the initial absolute temperature?
records.sourceExplanation: V₁/T₁ = V₂/T₂ → T₂/T₁ = V₂/V₁ = 9.75/3.25 = 3.

records.question: Two cylinders A and B each contains 30 cm³ of oxygen and nitrogen respectively at the same temperature and pressure. If there are 5.0 moles of nitrogen, then the mass of oxygen is [O=16]
records.sourceExplanation: Equal volumes contain equal moles. Moles O₂ = 5.0 mol. Mass O₂ = 5 × 32 = 160 g.

records.question: A liquid begins to boil when
options: its vapour pressure is equal to vapour pressure of its solid at the given temperature
molecules start escaping from its surface
its vapour pressure equals the atmospheric pressure
records.answerText: its vapour pressure equals the atmospheric pressure
records.sourceExplanation: Boiling occurs when vapour pressure equals external (atmospheric) pressure.

records.question: A particle that contains 8 protons, 9 neutrons and 7 electrons could be written as
records.sourceExplanation: 8 protons = oxygen. 9 neutrons → mass number 17. 7 electrons → +1 charge (lost 1 electron). So ¹⁷₈O⁺.

records.question: In the oil drop experiment, Millikan determined the
options: charge to mass ratio of the electron
records.sourceExplanation: Millikan's oil drop experiment determined the charge of an electron.

records.question: The stability of ionic solids is generally due to the
options: negative electron affinity of most atoms
records.sourceExplanation: Ionic solids are held together by strong electrostatic forces (lattice energy).

records.question: Which of the following statements is FALSE about isotopes of the same element?
options: They have the same number of electrons in their outermost shells
They have the same atomic number and the same number of electrons
They have the same atomic number but different number of electrons
records.answerText: They have the same atomic number but different number of electrons
records.sourceExplanation: Isotopes have the same atomic number and same number of electrons (neutral atoms). They have different mass numbers.

records.question: Helium is often used in observation balloons because it is
records.sourceExplanation:
Helium is lighter than air and inert (non-combustible), making it safe for balloons.
# JAMB CHEMISTRY PAST QUESTIONS (601–650)

records.question: When plastic and packaging materials made from chloromethane are burnt in the open, the mixture of gases released into the atmosphere is most likely to contain
records.sourceExplanation: Chlorinated hydrocarbons release HCl gas when burned.

records.question: Deliquescent substances are also
records.sourceExplanation: Deliquescent substances are hygroscopic (absorb moisture) and dissolve to form solutions.

records.question: The difference between colloids and suspensions is brought out clearly by the fact that while colloids
options: do not scatter light, suspensions cannot be so separated
can be separated by filtration, suspensions cannot be separated
can be separated by a membrane, suspensions cannot
do not settle out on standing, suspensions do
records.answerText: do not settle out on standing, suspensions do
records.sourceExplanation: Colloidal particles do not settle due to Brownian motion; suspensions settle due to gravity.

records.question: In general, an increase in temperature increases the solubility of a solute in water because
options: more solute molecules collide with each other
most solutes dissolve with the evolution of heat
more solute molecules dissociate at higher temperatures
most solutes dissolve with absorption of heat
records.answerText: most solutes dissolve with absorption of heat
records.sourceExplanation: Most solutes have endothermic dissolution, so higher temperature favours dissolution.

records.question: Neutralization involves a reaction between H₃O⁺ and
records.sourceExplanation: Neutralization: H₃O⁺ + OH⁻ → 2H₂O.

records.question: Which of the following solutions will have a pH < 7?
records.sourceExplanation: NH₄Cl is salt of weak base and strong acid, giving acidic solution (pH < 7).

records.question: 56.00 cm³ of a gas at STP weighed 0.11 g. What is the vapour density of the gas? [Molar volume of gas at STP = 22.4 dm³]
records.sourceExplanation: Moles = 56/22400 = 0.0025 mol. Molar mass = 0.11/0.0025 = 44 g/mol. Vapour density = molar mass/2 = 22.

records.question: Which of the following gases will diffuse fastest when passed through a porous plug? [H=1, C=12, N=14, O=16]

records.question: Which of the following will have its mass increased when heated in air?

records.question: What is the temperature of a given mass of a gas initially at 0°C and 9 atm, if the pressure is reduced to 3 atm at constant volume?

records.question: A gaseous metallic chloride MClₓ consists of 20.22% of M by mass. The formula of the chloride is [M=27, Cl=35.5]

records.question: In order to remove one electron from 3s-orbital of gaseous sodium atom, about 496 kJ/mol of energy is required. This energy is referred to as

records.question: The method that can be used to convert hard water to soft water is

records.question: Given that electronegativity increases across a period and decreases down a group in the periodic table, in which of the following compounds will the molecules be held together by the strongest hydrogen bond?

records.question: 0.25 mol of hydrogen chloride was dissolved in distilled water and the volume made up to 0.50 dm³. If 15.00 cm³ of the solution requires 12.50 cm³ of aqueous sodium trioxocarbonate(IV) for neutralization, calculate the concentration of the alkaline solution.
records.sourceExplanation: HCl concentration = 0.25/0.50 = 0.5 M. Moles HCl in 15 cm³ = 0.5 × 15/1000 = 0.0075 mol. 2HCl + Na₂CO₃ → 2NaCl + CO₂ + H₂O. Moles Na₂CO₃ = 0.0075/2 = 0.00375 mol. Molarity Na₂CO₃ = 0.00375/(12.5/1000) = 0.30 M.

records.question: The correct order of increasing oxidation number of the transition metal ions for the compounds K₂Cr₂O₇, V₂O₅ and KMnO₄ is
records.sourceExplanation: Oxidation states: V in V₂O₅ = +5, Cr in K₂Cr₂O₇ = +6, Mn in KMnO₄ = +7.

records.question: The set of pollutants that is most likely to be produced when petrol is accidentally spilled on plastic materials and ignited is
records.sourceExplanation: Burning plastic (chlorinated) produces HCl, CO, CO₂.

records.question: What is observed when aqueous solution of tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid, potassium trioxonitrate(V) and potassium iodide are mixed together?

records.question: The solution with the lowest pH value is
records.sourceExplanation: M/5 = 0.2 M. Higher concentration of HCl gives lower pH.

records.question: The solubility product of Cu(IO₃)₂ is 1.08 × 10⁻⁷. Assuming that neither ions react appreciably with water to form H⁺ and OH⁻, what is the solubility of this salt?
records.sourceExplanation: Cu(IO₃)₂ ⇌ Cu²⁺ + 2IO₃⁻. Ksp = s × (2s)² = 4s³. 4s³ = 1.08 × 10⁻⁷ → s³ = 2.7 × 10⁻⁸ → s = 3.0 × 10⁻³ mol/dm³. Not in options. I'll go with C.

records.question: The entropy and enthalpy of a system are a measure of

heat content of a system only
records.answerText: degree of disorderliness and heat content respectively
records.sourceExplanation: Entropy = disorder, Enthalpy = heat content.

records.question: 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g). In the chemical reaction above, the substance that will increase the rate of production of sulphur(VI) oxide is
records.sourceExplanation: V₂O₅ is the catalyst in Contact process.

records.question: N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g). Increases in total pressure of the equilibrium reaction above will

Convert all of N₂O₄(g) to NO₂(g)

records.question: What quantity of electricity will liberate 0.125 mole of oxygen molecules during the electrolysis of dilute sodium chloride solution? [F = 96500 C/mol]
records.sourceExplanation: 4OH⁻ → O₂ + 2H₂O + 4e⁻. 1 mol O₂ requires 4 mol e⁻. 0.125 mol O₂ requires 0.5 mol e⁻. Charge = 0.5 × 96500 = 48,250 C.

records.question: X + Y → Z. The rate equation for the chemical reaction above is Δ[X]/Δt = [X]²[Y]. The overall order of the reaction is
records.sourceExplanation: Overall order = sum of exponents = 2 + 1 = 3.

records.question: When a current I was passed through an electrolyte solution for 40 minutes, a mass X g of a univalent metal was deposited at the cathode. What mass of the metal will be deposited when a current 2I is passed through the solution for 10 minutes?
records.sourceExplanation: Mass ∝ current × time. New mass = X × (2I × 10)/(I × 40) = X × 20/40 = X/2.

records.question: RS(aq) + HF(aq) ⇌ RF(s) + HS(aq), ΔH = -65.7 kJ/mol. From the equation above, it can be deduced that

the heat content of the reactants is higher than that of the products
a large amount of heat is absorbed
records.answerText: the heat content of the reactants is higher than that of the products
records.sourceExplanation: ΔH negative → exothermic → reactants have higher energy.

records.question: Which of the following statements is true of the electrochemical series?

Electropositivity of non-metals decrease down the series
Electronegativity of non-metals increase down the series
Electropositivity of metals decreases down the series
records.answerText: Electropositivity of metals increase down the series
records.sourceExplanation: Metals at the top are more electropositive (easily lose electrons).

records.question: Chlorine, bromine and iodine resemble one another in that they

records.question: Which of the following is an example of a mixture?
records.sourceExplanation:
Blood is a complex heterogeneous mixture consisting of red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets, and plasma.
Unlike pure chemical compounds, the components of blood are not chemically combined in fixed stoichiometric proportions.
They can be separated into distinct physical components using mechanical separation methods like centrifugation.
Options A, C (pure chemical sand component), and D represent specific chemical substances with fixed chemical formulas.

records.question: Calculate the percentage by mass of nitrogen in calcium trioxonitrate (V) [Ca = 40, N = 14, O = 16]
records.sourceExplanation:
The molar mass of calcium trioxonitrate (V), Ca(NO3)2, is 40 + 2[14 + (16 x 3)] = 164 g/mol.
The total mass contributed by the two nitrogen atoms in one mole of Ca(NO3)2 is 2 x 14 = 28 g/mol.
The percentage by mass of nitrogen is calculated as (28 / 164) x 100%, which equals 17.07%.
Rounding off this calculated value to one decimal place yields 17.1%, matching option C.

records.question: The droplets of water observed around a bottle of milk taken out of the refrigerator is due to the fact that the
options: water vapour in the air around the bottle gains some energy from the bottle
temperature of the milk drops as it loses heat into the surroundings
saturated vapour pressure of the milk is equal to the atmospheric pressure
water vapour in the air around the bottle loses some of its energy to the bottle
records.answerText: water vapour in the air around the bottle loses some of its energy to the bottle
records.sourceExplanation:
When a cold bottle is exposed to room air, water vapor present in surrounding air contacts the cold surface.
The warm water vapor transfers heat energy to the colder bottle, causing the vapor's kinetic energy to drop.
As the gas molecules lose energy, their temperature falls below the local dew point, causing condensation.
This physical phase change from gas to liquid deposits visible water droplets on the outer wall of the bottle.

records.question: The volume of a given gas is V cm³ at P mm Hg. What is the new volume of the gas if the pressure is reduced to half at constant temperature?
records.sourceExplanation:
According to Boyle's law, the volume of a given mass of gas is inversely proportional to its pressure at constant temperature.
Mathematically, this relationship is expressed by the ideal gas formula P1 V1 = P2 V2.
Given initial state P1 = P, V1 = V, and final pressure P2 = P/2, we substitute into the equation: P V = (P/2) V2.
Solving for V2 yields V2 = (2 P V) / P = 2V cm³, showing that halving the pressure doubles the volume.

records.question: Moving from left to right across a period, the general rise in the first ionization energy can be attributed to the
records.sourceExplanation:
Moving across a period from left to right, protons are added to the nucleus, increasing the nuclear charge.
Electrons are simultaneously added to the same outermost energy level, so shielding/screening remains nearly constant.
The stronger effective nuclear charge exerts a tighter electrostatic pull on the valence electrons.
Consequently, more energy is required to remove the outermost electron, causing ionization energy to rise.

records.question: How many unpaired electron(s) are there in the nitrogen sub-levels?
records.sourceExplanation:
Nitrogen has an atomic number of 7, with a ground-state electron configuration of 1s² 2s² 2p³.
According to Hund's rule of maximum multiplicity, electrons occupy degenerate orbitals singly before pairing up.
The three p-orbitals (2px, 2py, 2pz) each receive one electron with parallel spins.
Therefore, there are exactly 3 unpaired electrons in the 2p sub-level of a nitrogen atom.

records.question: The stability of the noble gases is due to the fact that they
options: have no electron in their outermost shells
have duplet or octet electron configurations
belong to group zero of the periodic table
records.answerText: have duplet or octet electron configurations
records.sourceExplanation:
Noble gases possess completely filled valence energy levels, achieving a stable duplet (Helium) or octet configuration.
Having eight valence electrons (or two for Helium) creates an exceptionally stable electronic arrangement.
Because their valence shells are full, they have minimal tendency to gain, lose, or share electrons with other atoms.
This chemical unreactivity and high stability is a direct consequence of their duplet or octet electronic structures.

records.question: The maximum number of electrons in the L shell of an atom is
records.sourceExplanation:
The maximum number of electrons that can occupy a given principal electron shell is determined by the formula 2n².
The L shell corresponds to the second principal quantum energy level, where the shell number n = 2.
Substituting n = 2 into the formula gives 2 (2)² = 2 4 = 8 electrons.
These 8 electrons are distributed between the 2s subshell (2 electrons) and 2p subshell (6 electrons).

records.question: Elements in the same period in the periodic table have the same
records.sourceExplanation:
Horizontal rows in the periodic table are known as periods, which correspond to principal energy levels.
All elements belonging to the same period have their valence electrons located in the same main energy shell.
Thus, they share the same total number of occupied electron shells.
Atomic numbers, chemical properties, and physical properties vary across a period as valence electrons change.

records.question: ²₁D + ³₁T → ⁴₂He + ¹₀n + energy The reaction above illustrates
records.sourceExplanation:
The nuclear reaction shows deuterium (²₁D) combining with tritium (³₁T) to form a helium nucleus (⁴₂He) and a neutron.
Nuclear fusion is defined as the combining of two light atomic nuclei to form a heavier nucleus with release of energy.
Since light isotopes of hydrogen unite to yield a heavier helium atom, this represents a classic fusion reaction.
It differs from nuclear fission, which involves splitting a heavy nucleus into smaller fragments.

records.question: A noble gas with a high power of fog penetration used in aerodrome beacons is
records.sourceExplanation:
Krypton and neon produce bright reddish-orange light that easily penetrates dense fog when electric discharge passes through them.
Krypton-filled lamps and high-intensity beacons provide essential visual guidance for aircraft landing in poor visibility.
Its long wavelength emission suffers minimal scattering by tiny water droplets suspended in fog.
Hence, it is widely utilized in specialized aerodrome beacon lighting systems.

records.question: Permanent hardness of water can be removed by
records.sourceExplanation:
Permanent hardness is caused by dissolved calcium and magnesium tetraoxosulphates(VI) or chlorides.
Adding caustic soda (NaOH) precipitates calcium and magnesium ions as insoluble hydroxides.
Chemical equation: Ca²⁺(aq) + 2OH⁻(aq) → Ca(OH)₂(s), removing the soluble ions responsible for hardness.
Boiling only removes temporary hardness (bicarbonates) and cannot precipitate permanent hardness ions.

records.question: Substances employed as drying agents are usually
records.sourceExplanation:
Drying agents are substances that readily absorb moisture or water vapor from their surroundings or gases.
Substances with a strong affinity for absorbing water from the atmosphere without necessarily dissolving are hygroscopic.
Examples include concentrated H2SO4, silica gel, and anhydrous calcium chloride.
Efflorescent substances lose water, whereas amphoteric substances react with both acids and bases.

records.question: Calculate the solubility in mol dm⁻³ of 40g of CuSO4 dissolved in 100g of water at 120⁰C. [Cu = 64, S = 32, O = 16]
records.sourceExplanation:
Molar mass of CuSO4 = 64 + 32 + (16 x 4) = 160 g/mol; moles of CuSO4 = 40 / 160 = 0.25 mol.
100g of water equals 100 cm³ (or 0.1 dm³) assuming a standard water density of 1 g/cm³.
Solubility in mol dm⁻³ is calculated as Moles of Solute / Volume of Solvent in dm³.
Substituting values yields 0.25 mol / 0.1 dm³ = 2.50 mol dm⁻³, matching Option B.

records.question: Coffee stains can best be removed by
options: a solution of borax in water
records.sourceExplanation:
Coffee stains contain organic tannins and acidic compounds that adhere strongly to fabric fibers.
An aqueous solution of ammonia is mildly alkaline and acts as an effective solvent/cleaning agent.
The alkaline ammonia neutralizes acidic stain components and breaks down organic chromophores.
This allows the coffee pigments to be emulsified and washed away easily without damaging fabrics.

records.question: Carbon (II) oxide is considered dangerous if inhaled mainly because it
options: can cause injury to the nervous system
competes with oxygen in the blood
competes with carbon (IV) oxide in the blood
records.answerText: competes with oxygen in the blood
records.sourceExplanation:
Carbon (II) oxide (CO) has an affinity for hemoglobin that is roughly 200 times higher than that of oxygen.
Upon inhalation, CO preferentially binds with hemoglobin to form stable carboxyhemoglobin.
This competes with and blocks oxygen binding, severely reducing the blood's oxygen-carrying capacity.
The resulting cellular oxygen deprivation can quickly lead to asphyxiation and death.

records.question: The acid that is used to remove rust is
records.sourceExplanation:
Rust consists primarily of hydrated iron (III) oxide, Fe2O3·xH2O.
Hydrochloric acid (HCl) reacts with insoluble rust to produce soluble iron chlorides and water.
Equation: Fe2O3 + 6HCl → 2FeCl3 + 3H2O, effectively dissolving rust scale from metal surfaces.
Because of this property, dilute HCl (pickling liquor) is widely used commercially for rust removal.

records.question: Calculate the volume of 0.5 mol dm⁻³ H2SO4 that is neutralized by 25 cm³ of 0.1 mol dm⁻³ NaOH
records.sourceExplanation:
The balanced neutralization equation is H2SO4 + 2NaOH → Na2SO4 + 2H2O, giving mole ratio na/nb = 1/2.
Using the titration relationship equation: (Ca Va) / (Cb Vb) = na / nb.
Substitute known values: (0.5 Va) / (0.1 25) = 1 / 2, which simplifies to 0.5 Va / 2.5 = 0.5.
Solving for Va yields Va = (0.5 2.5) / 0.5 = 2.5 cm³, matching option B.

records.question: The colour of methyl orange in alkaline medium is
records.sourceExplanation:
Methyl orange is a common acid-base indicator that changes color depending on solution pH.
In acidic solutions (pH < 3.1), methyl orange exists in a protonated form that appears red.
In neutral to alkaline media (pH > 4.4), it deprotonates to assume a distinct yellow color.
Thus, in an alkaline medium, methyl orange reliably displays a yellow color.

records.question: Which of the following salts is slightly soluble in water?
records.sourceExplanation:
Calcium tetraoxosulphate (VI), CaSO4, is classified as a sparingly or slightly soluble salt in water.
Most alkali metal salts like Na2CO3 are completely soluble, whereas AgCl and PbCl2 (cold) are virtually insoluble.
CaSO4 has a low solubility product, dissolving only to a limited extent at ambient temperatures.
Therefore, CaSO4 fits the description of being slightly soluble compared to the options provided.

records.question: 6AgNO3(aq) + PH3(g) + 3H2O(l) → 6Ag(s) + H3PO3(g) + 6HNO3(aq) In the above reaction, the reducing agent is
records.sourceExplanation:
A reducing agent undergoes oxidation by donating electrons and increasing its oxidation state.
In phosphine (PH3), the oxidation state of phosphorus increases from -3 to +3 in H3PO3.
Simultaneously, silver ions (Ag⁺) in AgNO3 are reduced from oxidation state +1 to 0 (metallic Ag).
Because PH3 causes the reduction of AgNO3 while being oxidized itself, PH3 is the reducing agent.

records.question: The IUPAC nomenclature of the compound LiAlH4 is
records.sourceExplanation:
LiAlH4 consists of a lithium cation (Li⁺) and a complex tetrahydridoaluminate anion ([AlH4]⁻).
According to IUPAC naming rules for complex hydrides, the metal cation is named first as lithium.
The anionic ligand is four hydrides ('tetrahydrido') attached to central aluminum ('aluminate').
Aluminum has an oxidation state of +3 here, giving the complete name lithium tetrahydridoaluminate (III).

JAMB Chemistry Past Questions & Detailed Explanations (24 - 50)

records.question: Iron can be protected from corrosion by coating the surface with
records.sourceExplanation:
Coating iron with zinc is a process known as galvanization.
Zinc is more electropositive (more reactive) than iron in the electrochemical series.
It provides both a protective barrier and sacrificial protection; zinc oxidizes preferentially over iron.
Even if the zinc coating is scratched, the underlying iron remains protected against rusting.

records.question: What quantity of aluminium is deposited when a current of 10A is passed through a solution of an aluminium salt for 1930s? [Al = 27, F = 96500 C mol⁻¹]
records.sourceExplanation:
Total charge passed Q = I \times t = 10\text{ A} \times 1930\text{ s} = 19300\text{ C}.
Reduction equation: \text{Al}^{3+} + 3e^- \rightarrow \text{Al}, showing that 3 moles of electrons (3 Faraday) deposit 1 mole (27 g) of Al.
Charge required for 27 g of Al = 3 \times 96500\text{ C} = 289500\text{ C}.
Mass deposited = (19300\text{ C} / 289500\text{ C}) \times 27\text{ g} = 1.8\text{ g}, corresponding to option B.

records.question: In which of the following is the entropy change positive?
options: Reaction between an acid and a base
Addition of concentrated acid to water
Dissolution of sodium metal in water
records.sourceExplanation:
Entropy (S) is a measure of molecular randomness or degree of disorder in a chemical system.
Thermal dissociation of \text{NH}_4\text{Cl} is given by \text{NH}_4\text{Cl}(s) \rightarrow \text{NH}_3(g) + \text{HCl}(g).
One mole of solid reactant decomposes to form two moles of gaseous products.
Since gases have vastly higher entropy than solids, this transition results in a positive entropy change (\Delta S > 0).

records.question: If a reaction is exothermic and there is a great disorder, it means that
options: the reaction is in a state of equilibrium
there will be a large increase in free energy
there will be a large decrease in free energy
records.answerText: there will be a large increase in free energy
records.sourceExplanation:
Gibbs free energy change equation is \Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S, where exothermic means \Delta H is negative.
Great disorder implies a large positive entropy change (\Delta S > 0), making the -T\Delta S term negative.
Both terms (-\Delta H and -T\Delta S) contribute negatively to \Delta G, resulting in a large negative value for \Delta G.
A large negative \Delta G corresponds to a significant decrease in free energy, driving spontaneous reaction.

records.question: In the preparation of oxygen by heating \text{KClO}_3 in the presence of \text{MnO}_2, only moderate heat is needed because the catalyst acts by
options: lowering the pressure of the reaction
increasing the surface area of the reactant
increase the rate of the reaction
lowering the energy barrier of the reaction
records.answerText: lowering the energy barrier of the reaction
records.sourceExplanation:
Manganese (IV) oxide (\text{MnO}_2) serves as a positive catalyst in the thermal decomposition of \text{KClO}_3.
Catalysts speed up chemical reactions by providing an alternative reaction pathway with lower activation energy.
By lowering the energy barrier, a larger fraction of molecules possess sufficient energy to react at lower temperatures.
Consequently, the reaction proceeds rapidly with only moderate heat input required.

records.question: The graph above demonstrates the effect of
options: surface area on the rate of reaction
catalyst on the rate of reaction
concentration on the rate of reaction
records.answerText: surface area on the rate of reaction
records.sourceExplanation:
Reaction rate curves comparing powdered vs chunk/lump reactants demonstrate the impact of surface area.
Breaking a solid reactant into smaller particles increases the exposed total surface area.
A greater surface area increases the frequency of effective collisions between reacting particles.
This accelerates the initial reaction rate, as clearly illustrated by the kinetic curves.

records.question: 2\text{H}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(g)\ \Delta H = \text{-ve}. What happens to the equilibrium constant of the reaction above if the temperature is increased?
records.sourceExplanation:
The forward reaction is exothermic (\Delta H = \text{-ve}), releasing heat to the surroundings.
According to Le Chatelier's principle, increasing temperature shifts equilibrium in the endothermic (reverse) direction.
The shift favors reactants over products, reducing product concentration relative to reactants.
Since K_c = \frac{[\text{Products}]}{[\text{Reactants}]}, a shift toward reactants causes the equilibrium constant K_c to decrease.

records.question: To a solution of an unknown compound, a little dilute tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid was added with some freshly prepared iron (II) tetraoxosulphate (VI) solution. The brown ring observed after the addition of a stream of concentrated tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid confirmed the presence of
records.sourceExplanation:
The test described is the classical brown ring test used specifically to identify trioxonitrate (V) ions, \text{NO}_3^-.
Concentrated \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 reacts with \text{NO}_3^- to liberate nitric oxide (\text{NO}) gas in solution.
\text{NO} coordinates with excess \text{FeSO}_4 to form the complex dark brown compound [\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_5(\text{NO})]\text{SO}_4.
This complex appears as a distinct brown ring at the junction of the two liquid layers, confirming \text{NO}_3^-.

records.question: In the diagram above, the gas produced is
records.sourceExplanation:
Action of moderately dilute \text{HNO}_3 on copper turnings produces nitrogen (II) oxide gas, \text{NO}.
Chemical equation: 3\text{Cu} + 8\text{HNO}_3 \rightarrow 3\text{Cu}(\text{NO}_3)_2 + 2\text{NO} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}.
\text{NO} is a colorless, insoluble gas that turns brown (\text{NO}_2) upon coming into contact with air/oxygen.
Thus, the primary gaseous product collected over water in this standard lab set-up is \text{NO}.

records.question: Which of the following is used in rocket fuels?
records.sourceExplanation:
Concentrated nitric acid (\text{HNO}_3) acts as a powerful oxidizing agent in rocket propulsion systems.
It supplies concentrated oxygen to burn liquid rocket fuels (like hydrazine) rapidly and violently.
This hypergolic combustion generates high-pressure gases that propel the rocket forward.
Therefore, \text{HNO}_3 is widely applied as a liquid oxidizer component in rocket fuels.

records.question: In the diagram below, the purpose of the asbestos is to
records.sourceExplanation:
Platinized asbestos is commonly employed in industrial gas preparation apparatus like the Contact Process.
It acts as a heterogeneous catalyst providing an active surface for gas-phase reactions.
The asbestos fiber holds the dispersed catalyst material, maximizing contact area with reactant gases.
Hence, its core purpose in the reaction pathway is to catalyze the chemical reaction.

records.question: A constituent common to bronze and solder is
records.sourceExplanation:
Bronze is an alloy primarily composed of copper (\text{Cu}) and tin (\text{Sn}).
Solder is an alloy primarily composed of lead (\text{Pb}) and tin (\text{Sn}).
Comparing the elemental composition of both alloys shows that tin (\text{Sn}) is present in both.
Therefore, tin is the constituent element common to both bronze and solder.

records.question: When iron is exposed to moist air, it gradually rusts. This is due to the formation of
records.sourceExplanation:
Rusting requires atmospheric oxygen and liquid water/moisture acting together on iron metal.
Electrochemical oxidation converts metallic iron into iron (III) ions.
These ions precipitate out as reddish-brown hydrated iron (III) oxide, \text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3 \cdot x\text{H}_2\text{O}.
Anhydrous forms do not represent rust, making hydrated iron (III) oxide the correct composition.

records.question: A compound gives an orange-red colour to non-luminous flame. This compound is likely to contain
records.sourceExplanation:
Flame tests identify characteristic atomic emission spectra of metal cations when heated in a flame.
Calcium ions (\text{Ca}^{2+}) impart a distinctive brick-red or orange-red color to a non-luminous Bunsen flame.
Sodium gives persistent golden yellow, whereas iron cations do not impart characteristic bright flame colors.
Thus, an orange-red flame indicates the presence of calcium ions (\text{Ca}^{2+}).

records.question: Stainless steel is used for making
records.sourceExplanation:
Stainless steel is an alloy of iron, chromium, nickel, and carbon highly resistant to corrosion.
It exhibits high luster, durability, mechanical strength, and chemical inertness.
Due to its durability and resistance to tarnishing, it is extensively used to manufacture cutlery, surgical tools, coins, and medals.
Out of the given options, coins and medals are prominent applications of stainless steel.

records.question: The residual solids from the fractional distillation of petroleum are used as
options: raw materials for the cracking process
records.sourceExplanation:
Fractional distillation leaves behind heavy non-volatile residue known as bitumen or asphalt.
This thick carbonaceous residue is highly water-resistant and durable.
It is widely utilized for road surfacing, waterproofing roofs, and protective coatings for underground pipes.
Hence, pipe coating represents a major practical application for petroleum distillation residues.

records.question: The IUPAC nomenclature of the compound above is
records.sourceExplanation:
To name the alkane, identify the longest continuous carbon chain containing seven carbon atoms (heptane).
Number the carbon chain from the end that gives the substituent the lowest possible locant number.
A propyl group substituent (-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3) is attached at carbon-3 along the main heptane chain.
Combining locant and substituent name yields 3-propylheptane.

records.question: Which of the following is used as fuel in miners' lamp?
records.sourceExplanation:
Ethyne (acetylene, \text{C}_2\text{H}_2) gas burns in oxygen to produce a very bright, luminous flame.
It is generated by reacting calcium carbide with water in portable carbide lamps.
Historically, miners relied on these acetylene lamps attached to helmets for underground illumination.
Therefore, ethyne is the hydrocarbon traditional utilized in miners' safety lamps.

records.question: Which of the following organic compounds is very soluble in water?
records.sourceExplanation:
Ethanoic acid (\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}) contains a polar carboxylic acid functional group (-\text{COOH}).
It forms strong hydrogen bonds with water molecules due to its hydroxyl and carbonyl groups.
Lower alkanoic acids like \text{CH}_3\text{COOH} are completely miscible with water in all proportions.
Non-polar or weakly polar compounds like ethene, ethyne, or esters have very limited water solubility.

records.question: Benzene reacts with hydrogen in the presence of nickel catalyst at 180⁰C to give
records.sourceExplanation:
Benzene undergoes catalytic hydrogenation when heated with hydrogen gas and nickel catalyst at 180°C.
The aromatic ring breaks down as three molecules of \text{H}_2 add across the delocalized double bonds.
Reaction equation: \text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + 3\text{H}_2 \rightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}.
The complete saturation of the aromatic nucleus yields the cyclic alkane cyclohexane.

records.question: Which of the following is used to hasten the ripening of fruit?
records.sourceExplanation:
Ethene (ethylene, \text{C}_2\text{H}_4) is a naturally occurring plant hormone that controls fruit maturation.
It triggers biochemical pathways responsible for softening, color change, and sugar accumulation.
Agriculture industries artificially introduce ethene gas into storage chambers to speed up ripening.
Thus, ethene is commercially applied as an effective fruit ripening agent.

records.question: The final products of the reaction between methane and chlorine in the presence of ultraviolet light are hydrogen chloride and
records.sourceExplanation:
Methane undergoes free-radical substitution with chlorine gas under ultraviolet light irradiation.
Hydrogen atoms are sequentially replaced by chlorine: \text{CH}_4 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{Cl} \rightarrow \text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{CHCl}_3 \rightarrow \text{CCl}_4.
When excess chlorine is present, substitution proceeds until all four hydrogen atoms are replaced.
The fully substituted final organic product is tetrachloromethane (\text{CCl}_4), along with \text{HCl}.

records.question: The correct order of increasing boiling points of the following compounds \text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{OH}, \text{C}_7\text{H}_{16} and \text{C}_4\text{H}_{10} is
records.sourceExplanation:
\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10} (butane) is a short non-polar alkane with weak van der Waals forces, giving it the lowest boiling point.
\text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{OH} (propanol) contains an -\text{OH} group capable of strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding, raising its boiling point.
\text{C}_7\text{H}_{16} (heptane) is a much larger hydrocarbon with a significantly higher molar mass and extensive dispersion forces.
Ordering by strength of intermolecular forces gives \text{C}_4\text{H}_{10} < \text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{OH} < \text{C}_7\text{H}_{16}, matching option D.

records.question: One of the major uses of alkane is
records.sourceExplanation:
Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons that undergo clean combustion in excess oxygen.
They burn exothermically to yield carbon dioxide, water vapor, and large amounts of heat energy.
Examples like methane (natural gas), propane, butane (LPG), and petrol drive domestic heating and transport.
