Hence, their primary economic and industrial application is serving as domestic and industrial fuels.

records.question: The haloalkanes used in dry-cleaning industries are
records.sourceExplanation:
Trichloromethane (\text{CHCl}_3) and tetrachloromethane (\text{CCl}_4) are effective non-polar organic solvents.
They readily dissolve non-polar organic substances like grease, oils, and fats without swelling textile fibers.
Their volatile nature allows them to evaporate cleanly from fabrics post-cleaning.
Due to these solvent properties, they have historically been widely used in dry-cleaning processes.

records.question: Two hydrocarbons X and Y were treated with bromine water. X decolorized the solution and Y did not. Which class of compound does Y belong?
records.sourceExplanation:
Bromine water test differentiates saturated hydrocarbons from unsaturated hydrocarbons.
Unsaturated compounds (alkenes/alkynes) rapidly undergo addition reactions, decolorizing bromine water.
Hydrocarbon Y failed to decolorize bromine water, indicating that it lacks double or triple C=C bonds.
Since Y is a saturated hydrocarbon incapable of addition under standard conditions, Y belongs to alkanes.

records.question: The compound that is used as an anaesthetic is
records.sourceExplanation:
Trichloromethane (\text{CHCl}_3), commonly known as chloroform, depresses the central nervous system.
Inhaling its vapors induces reversible loss of consciousness and pain sensation.
It was historically widely used as an inhalation anesthetic in surgical procedures.
Therefore, \text{CHCl}_3 corresponds to the organohalogen compound used as an anesthetic agent.
JAMB Chemistry Past Questions & Detailed Explanations (51 - 100)

records.question: In which of the following are water molecules in the most disorderly arrangement?
records.sourceExplanation:
Entropy represents the degree of disorder or randomness in a chemical system.
The gaseous state (steam) has significantly higher kinetic energy and freedom of molecular motion than solid (ice) or liquid water.
At 100°C, steam molecules move rapidly and randomly in three dimensions with negligible intermolecular forces.
Thus, steam at 100°C exhibits the highest molecular disorder.

records.question: Alloys are best prepared by
options: reducing a mixture of their metallic oxides
cooling a molten mixture of the metals
records.answerText: cooling a molten mixture of the metals
records.sourceExplanation:
An alloy is a homogeneous solid solution or mixture composed of two or more metals (or a metal and a non-metal).
Alloys are manufactured by melting the constituent metals together in precise proportions.
Upon thorough mixing and gradual cooling, the liquid mixture solidifies into a uniform alloy structure.
Therefore, cooling a molten mixture of metals is the primary technique.

records.question: In cold countries where the temperature falls below 0°C, salt is often sprinkled on icy roads in order to
options: raise the melting point of the ice
lower the melting point of the ice
increase the density of the ice
records.answerText: lower the melting point of the ice
records.sourceExplanation:
Dissolving a non-volatile solute like sodium chloride (\text{NaCl}) in water causes freezing point depression.
The presence of salt ions disrupts the formation of the rigid ice crystal lattice.
This causes ice on roads to melt at temperatures well below 0°C, clearing frozen roadways.
Thus, salt acts by lowering the melting point of ice.

records.question: Nitrogen obtained from the liquefaction of air has a higher density than nitrogen obtained from nitrogen compounds because the former contains
records.sourceExplanation:
Atmospheric air contains about 1% noble gases, predominantly argon (\text{Ar}, molar mass 40 g/mol).
Fractional distillation of liquid air leaves dense noble gases mixed with atmospheric nitrogen (\text{N}_2, molar mass 28 g/mol).
Chemical nitrogen prepared from pure compounds (e.g., thermal decomposition of \text{NH}_4\text{NO}_2) is pure \text{N}_2.
The inclusion of heavier argon increases the average density of atmospheric nitrogen.

records.question: The method that can be used to convert hard water to soft water by removing both temporary and permanent hardness is
options: the use of an ion-exchange resin
records.answerText: the use of an ion-exchange resin
records.sourceExplanation:
Permanent hardness is caused by dissolved \text{Ca}^{2+} and \text{Mg}^{2+} sulfates or chlorides, while temporary hardness is due to hydrogen carbonates.
Ion-exchange resins (Permutit process) replace \text{Ca}^{2+} and \text{Mg}^{2+} cations with non-hardening ions like \text{Na}^+ or \text{H}^+.
This process effectively removes both types of hardness completely.
Hence, an ion-exchange resin acts as a universal water softening system.

records.question: An element with the electronic configuration 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 3d^7 4s^2 is classified as a
records.sourceExplanation:
Elements filling the 3d subshell progressively (atomic numbers 21 to 30) are d-block elements.
The presence of partially filled d-orbitals (3d^7) defines transition metals.
Cobalt (\text{Co}, Z = 27) possesses this exact electronic configuration.
Therefore, it belongs to the transition elements series.

records.question: Which of the following compounds can be represented by the general molecular formula \text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n+2}\text{O}?
records.sourceExplanation:
The general formula \text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n+2}\text{O} corresponds to saturated monohydric alcohols and ethers.
For ethanol (\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} or \text{C}_2\text{H}_6\text{O}), substituting n = 2 yields \text{C}_2\text{H}_{2(2)+2}\text{O} = \text{C}_2\text{H}_6\text{O}.
Carbonyl compounds like ethanal (\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}) fit \text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n}\text{O}.
Thus, ethanol matches this general molecular formula.

records.question: The catalyst used in the Contact Process for the industrial manufacture of tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid is
records.sourceExplanation:
In the Contact Process, sulfur dioxide (\text{SO}_2) is oxidized to sulfur trioxide (\text{SO}_3).
Oxidation equation: 2\text{SO}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3(g).
Vanadium (V) oxide (\text{V}_2\text{O}_5) is preferred commercially over platinum due to lower cost and high resistance to catalytic poisoning by impurities like arsenic.
Hence, \text{V}_2\text{O}_5 is the primary catalyst used.

records.question: Which of the following gases will bleach moist litmus paper?
records.sourceExplanation:
Chlorine gas (\text{Cl}_2) reacts with water to form hypochlorous acid (\text{HClO}).
\text{HClO} acts as a powerful oxidizing agent, liberating atomic oxygen that oxidizes organic dyes.
This reaction permanently bleaches damp blue or red litmus paper white.
Therefore, chlorine is a strong chemical bleaching agent.

records.question: The oxidation state of chromium in potassium dichromate (VI), \text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7, is
records.sourceExplanation:
Potassium (\text{K}) has an oxidation state of +1 and oxygen (\text{O}) is -2.
Overall sum for neutral molecule: 2(+1) + 2(x) + 7(-2) = 0.
2 + 2x - 14 = 0 \implies 2x = 12 \implies x = +6.
So, the oxidation state of chromium (\text{Cr}) is +6.

records.question: What volume of 0.5\text{ mol/dm}^3 \text{HCl} is required to neutralize 25\text{ cm}^3 of 0.2\text{ mol/dm}^3 \text{NaOH}?
records.sourceExplanation:
Neutralization formula: \frac{C_a V_a}{C_b V_b} = \frac{n_a}{n_b}.
For \text{HCl} + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{NaCl} + \text{H}_2\text{O}, n_a = 1 and n_b = 1.
Substituting values: \frac{0.5 \times V_a}{0.2 \times 25} = 1 \implies 0.5 V_a = 5 \implies V_a = 10\text{ cm}^3.
Thus, 10\text{ cm}^3 of acid is required.

records.question: Which of the following processes is endothermic?
options: Dissolution of ammonium chloride in water
records.answerText: Dissolution of ammonium chloride in water
records.sourceExplanation:
An endothermic process absorbs heat energy from its surroundings (\Delta H > 0).
Dissolving \text{NH}_4\text{Cl} in water breaks crystal lattice bonds, absorbing thermal energy and cooling the solution.
Freezing, condensation, and combustion all liberate thermal energy (exothermic).
Therefore, the dissolution of \text{NH}_4\text{Cl} is an endothermic process.

records.question: The phenomenon whereby a salt absorbs moisture from the atmosphere to form a solution is called
records.sourceExplanation:
Deliquescence is the property of certain soluble solids absorbing sufficient atmospheric water vapor to dissolve completely into a liquid solution.
Examples include \text{CaCl}_2, \text{NaOH}, and \text{FeCl}_3.
Hygroscopic substances absorb moisture without forming a solution.
Efflorescence is the loss of water of crystallization to the atmosphere.

records.question: According to Graham's law of diffusion, the rate of diffusion of a gas is inversely proportional to the
records.sourceExplanation:
Graham's Law states r \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{\rho}} or r \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{M}} at constant temperature and pressure.
The rate of gas diffusion (r) is inversely proportional to the square root of its density (\rho) or molar mass (M).
Heavier, denser gases diffuse more slowly than lighter gases.
Thus, option A correctly expresses Graham's law.

records.question: Which of the following elements has the highest electronegativity?
records.sourceExplanation:
Electronegativity measures an atom's tendency to attract shared bonding electrons.
Electronegativity increases across a period and decreases down a group in the periodic table.
Fluorine (\text{F}) sits at the top right of Group 17 with an electronegativity value of 4.0 on the Pauling scale.
Hence, fluorine is the most electronegative element in the periodic table.

records.question: The empirical formula of a hydrocarbon containing 85.7% carbon and 14.3% hydrogen by mass is [C = 12, H = 1]
records.sourceExplanation:
Calculate mole ratios: Carbon = 85.7 / 12 = 7.14, Hydrogen = 14.3 / 1 = 14.3.
Divide by the smallest mole value (7.14): \text{C} = 7.14 / 7.14 = 1, \text{H} = 14.3 / 7.14 \approx 2.
The simple mole ratio is 1 : 2.
The empirical formula is \text{CH}_2.

records.question: In the electrolysis of aqueous copper (II) tetraoxosulphate (VI) using platinum electrodes, the product formed at the anode is
records.sourceExplanation:
Ions present in solution: \text{Cu}^{2+}, \text{H}^+ at cathode; \text{SO}_4^{2-}, \text{OH}^- at anode.
At the inert platinum anode, \text{OH}^- ions are discharged preferentially over \text{SO}_4^{2-} because \text{OH}^- has a lower discharge potential.
Reaction equation: 4\text{OH}^- - 4e^- \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{O}_2(g).
Thus, oxygen gas is evolved at the anode.

records.question: Which of the following oxides is amphoteric?
records.sourceExplanation:
Amphoteric oxides react with both acids and strong bases to form salt and water.
Zinc oxide (\text{ZnO}) reacts with \text{HCl} to form \text{ZnCl}_2 and with \text{NaOH} to form sodium zincate (\text{Na}_2\text{Zn(OH)}_4).
Other common amphoteric oxides include \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3 and \text{PbO}.
Therefore, \text{ZnO} is an amphoteric oxide.

records.question: What is the concentration of hydrogen ions [\text{H}^+] in a solution whose \text{pH} is 3?
records.sourceExplanation:
By definition, \text{pH} = -\log_{10}[\text{H}^+].
Expressing in exponential form: [\text{H}^+] = 10^{-\text{pH}}.
Substituting \text{pH} = 3 gives [\text{H}^+] = 10^{-3} = 1 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol/dm}^3.
Thus, option A is correct.

records.question: Which gas is primarily responsible for global warming (greenhouse effect)?
records.sourceExplanation:
Carbon (IV) oxide (\text{CO}_2) traps longwave infrared thermal radiation emitted from Earth's surface.
This thermal retention prevents heat from escaping into space, raising global atmospheric temperatures.
Increased combustion of fossil fuels elevates atmospheric \text{CO}_2 concentration.
Hence, \text{CO}_2 is a primary greenhouse gas driving global warming.

records.question: The main raw materials used in the Solvay process for manufacturing sodium trioxocarbonate (IV) are
records.sourceExplanation:
The Solvay process synthesizes \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 from brine (\text{NaCl} solution), ammonia (\text{NH}_3), and limestone (\text{CaCO}_3).
\text{CaCO}_3 provides \text{CO}_2 upon thermal decomposition.
Reaction of brine, \text{NH}_3, and \text{CO}_2 precipitates \text{NaHCO}_3, which is calcined to \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3.
Thus, \text{NaCl}, \text{NH}_3, and \text{CaCO}_3 are the essential raw materials.

records.question: Which of the following organic functional groups characterizes alkanols?
records.sourceExplanation:
Alkanols (alcohols) contain the hydroxyl functional group (-\text{OH}) attached to a saturated carbon atom.
\text{COOH} represents carboxylic acids, -\text{CHO} aldehydes, and -\text{COO}- esters.
Therefore, the hydroxyl group (-\text{OH}) identifies alkanols.

records.question: Saponification is the alkaline hydrolysis of fats and oils using
records.sourceExplanation:
Fats and oils are triesters composed of glycerol and long-chain fatty acids.
Alkaline hydrolysis using sodium hydroxide (\text{NaOH}) or potassium hydroxide (\text{KOH}) cleaves ester bonds.
Products formed are propane-1,2,3-triol (glycerol) and sodium salts of fatty acids (soaps).
Hence, saponification relies on strong concentrated alkali.

records.question: The molecular shape of a methane (\text{CH}_4) molecule is
records.sourceExplanation:
The central carbon atom in \text{CH}_4 undergoes sp^3 hybridization with four bonding electron pairs and zero lone pairs.
According to VSEPR theory, four bonding electron pairs arrange as far apart as possible in 3D space.
This minimizes electrostatic repulsion, yielding a symmetrical tetrahedral geometry with bond angles of 109.5^\circ.
Thus, methane has a tetrahedral shape.

records.question: Which particle is emitted when an atom of ^{238}_{92}\text{U} decays to ^{234}_{90}\text{Th}?
records.sourceExplanation:
Mass number change = 238 - 234 = 4.
Atomic number change = 92 - 90 = 2.
The emitted particle carries 4 units of atomic mass and 2 units of atomic number (^{4}_{2}\text{He} or \alpha).
An alpha particle is a helium nucleus (^4_2\text{He}).
Therefore, an alpha particle was emitted during decay.

records.question: What is the number of unpaired electrons in a neutral chlorine atom (Z = 17)?
records.sourceExplanation:
Electronic configuration of Cl (Z=17): 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^5.
Outer 3p subshell holds 5 electrons distributed across 3 degenerate orbitals (3p_x^2, 3p_y^2, 3p_z^1).
Two orbitals contain paired electrons and one orbital contains a single unpaired electron.
Hence, chlorine has exactly 1 unpaired electron.

records.question: Which of the following compounds exhibits functional group isomerism with ethanoic acid (\text{CH}_3\text{COOH})?
records.sourceExplanation:
Ethanoic acid (\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}_2) is a carboxylic acid.
Methyl methanoate (\text{HCOOCH}_3) is an ester with the same molecular formula \text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}_2.
Both share identical molecular formulas but belong to different organic functional classes.
Therefore, methyl methanoate is a functional group isomer of ethanoic acid.

records.question: The property of carbon that enables it to form long chains and ring structures is
records.sourceExplanation:
Catenation is the ability of an element to form covalent bonds with other atoms of the same element to build open chains or cyclic structures.
Carbon exhibits exceptional catenation due to the high stability of carbon-carbon (\text{C}-\text{C}) bonds.
This forms the structural foundation of millions of organic compounds.
Thus, catenation is the defining property.

records.question: Which of the following elements is purified commercially by zone refining?
records.sourceExplanation:
Zone refining is a fractional crystallization technique based on solubility differences of impurities in molten vs solid states.
It produces ultra-pure metals and semiconductors (purity >99.999\%).
High-purity silicon (\text{Si}) and germanium (\text{Ge}) required for microelectronics and semiconductors are purified using zone refining.
Hence, silicon is purified by zone refining.

records.question: A solution with a \text{pH} greater than 7 turns red litmus paper
records.sourceExplanation:
\text{pH} > 7 indicates an alkaline (basic) solution containing excess hydroxide ions (\text{OH}^-).
Basic solutions turn red litmus paper blue.
Acidic solutions (\text{pH} < 7) turn blue litmus red.
Therefore, the paper turns blue.

records.question: The functional group present in alkenes is
records.sourceExplanation:
Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons containing at least one carbon-carbon double bond (\text{C}=\text{C}).
Alkanes contain carbon-carbon single bonds (\text{C}-\text{C}).
Alkynes contain carbon-carbon triple bonds (\text{C}\equiv\text{C}).
Therefore, \text{C}=\text{C} is the signature functional group of alkenes.

records.question: Which metal is extracted commercially from bauxite ore?
records.sourceExplanation:
Bauxite is hydrated aluminium oxide (\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3 \cdot x\text{H}_2\text{O}).
It is purified to alumina via the Bayer process and electrolyzed in molten cryolite via the Hall-Héroult process.
This yields pure metallic aluminium.
Thus, aluminium is extracted from bauxite.

records.question: The standard condition for temperature and pressure (STP) defines temperature and pressure as
records.sourceExplanation:
Standard Temperature and Pressure (STP) is defined as 0^\circ\text{C} (273.15\text{ K}) and 1\text{ atm} (760\text{ mmHg} / 101.3\text{ kPa}).
Under STP conditions, 1 mole of an ideal gas occupies a molar volume of 22.4\text{ dm}^3.
Thus, option B states the correct STP parameters.

records.question: Which of the following compounds is an alkyne?
records.sourceExplanation:
Alkynes follow the general molecular formula \text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n-2}.
For ethyne (n = 2), molecular formula is \text{C}_2\text{H}_{2(2)-2} = \text{C}_2\text{H}_2.
\text{C}_2\text{H}_6 and \text{C}_3\text{H}_8 are alkanes (\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n+2}), and \text{C}_2\text{H}_4 is an alkene (\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n}).
Therefore, \text{C}_2\text{H}_2 is an alkyne.

records.question: When temporary hard water is boiled, the insoluble precipitate formed is
records.sourceExplanation:
Temporary water hardness is caused by dissolved calcium hydrogen carbonate, \text{Ca(HCO}_3)_2.
Heating decomposes it: \text{Ca(HCO}_3)_2(aq) \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{CaCO}_3(s) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(l) + \text{CO}_2(g).
Insoluble calcium carbonate (\text{CaCO}_3) precipitates out as boiler scale/limescale.
Thus, \text{CaCO}_3 forms the insoluble precipitate.
JAMB Chemistry Past Questions & Detailed Explanations (86 - 100)

records.question: Which bond type involves equal sharing of electron pairs between two non-metal atoms?
records.sourceExplanation:
In a non-polar covalent bond, electron pairs are shared equally between atoms with identical or nearly identical electronegativities (e.g., \text{H}_2, \text{O}_2, \text{Cl}_2).
Polar covalent bonds involve unequal electron sharing due to significant electronegativity differences.
Ionic bonds involve complete electron transfer from a metal to a non-metal.
Hence, non-polar covalent bonding involves equal sharing of bonding electrons.

records.question: The principal gas responsible for acid rain is
records.sourceExplanation:
Industrial combustion of fossil fuels containing sulfur impurities releases sulfur dioxide (\text{SO}_2).
Atmospheric oxidation converts \text{SO}_2 to \text{SO}_3, which reacts with rainwater: \text{SO}_3(g) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4(aq).
Sulfuric and sulfurous acids lower rainwater \text{pH} below 5.6, forming acid rain.
Therefore, \text{SO}_2 is the primary culprit gas.

records.question: The atomic number of an element is defined as the number of
records.sourceExplanation:
The atomic number (Z) uniquely identifies a chemical element.
It equals the total number of protons present in the nucleus of an atom.
The mass number (A) represents the total sum of protons and neutrons.
Thus, the atomic number is defined by the proton count.

records.question: Which gas is produced when dilute hydrochloric acid reacts with zinc metal?
records.sourceExplanation:
Metals above hydrogen in the electrochemical series displace hydrogen from dilute acids.
Chemical equation: \text{Zn}(s) + 2\text{HCl}(aq) \rightarrow \text{ZnCl}_2(aq) + \text{H}_2(g).
Hydrogen gas (\text{H}_2) is evolved with effervescence and burns with a characteristic "pop" sound.
Thus, hydrogen gas is produced.

records.question: Which of the following organic compounds decolorizes bromine water?
records.sourceExplanation:
Propene (\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2) contains an unsaturated carbon-carbon double bond (\text{C}=\text{C}).
Unsaturated hydrocarbons rapidly undergo electrophilic addition with bromine water, yielding 1,2-dibromopropane.
This reaction discharges the reddish-brown color of bromine water to form a colorless solution.
Saturated alkanes (ethane, methane, propane) do not react with bromine water under normal conditions.

records.question: The process of separating petroleum into its various fractions based on differences in boiling points is
records.sourceExplanation:
Crude oil (petroleum) is a complex mixture of liquid hydrocarbons with relatively close boiling points.
Fractional distillation in a tall fractionating column separates fractions (petrol, kerosene, diesel, bitumen) according to their specific boiling point ranges.
Vapors condense at different column heights corresponding to their condensation temperatures.
Thus, fractional distillation is the appropriate separation method.

records.question: The catalyst used in the Haber process for the industrial synthesis of ammonia is
records.sourceExplanation:
The Haber process synthesizes ammonia: \text{N}_2(g) + 3\text{H}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3(g).
Finely divided iron promoted with metal oxides (like \text{K}_2\text{O} or \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3) serves as the catalyst.
It lowers the activation energy under optimal operational conditions (450^\circ\text{C} and 200\text{ atm}).
Hence, finely divided iron is the industrial catalyst used.

records.question: Which of the following elements belongs to Group 17 (Halogens) of the periodic table?
records.sourceExplanation:
Group 17 (VIIA) elements are known as halogens and have 7 valence electrons (ns^2 np^5).
The group consists of fluorine (\text{F}), chlorine (\text{Cl}), bromine (\text{Br}), iodine (\text{I}), and astatine (\text{At}).
Sodium is in Group 1, calcium is in Group 2, and argon is in Group 18.
Therefore, chlorine is a halogen.

records.question: What mass of sodium hydroxide (\text{NaOH}) is required to prepare 250\text{ cm}^3 of a 0.1\text{ mol/dm}^3 solution? [\text{Na} = 23, \text{O} = 16, \text{H} = 1]
records.sourceExplanation:
Molar mass of \text{NaOH} = 23 + 16 + 1 = 40\text{ g/mol}.
Moles required (n) = \text{Concentration} \times \text{Volume in dm}^3 = 0.1\text{ mol/dm}^3 \times \frac{250}{1000}\text{ dm}^3 = 0.025\text{ mol}.
Mass = \text{Moles} \times \text{Molar Mass} = 0.025\text{ mol} \times 40\text{ g/mol} = 1.0\text{ g}.
Thus, 1.0\text{ g} of \text{NaOH} is required.

records.question: Which gas is collected by downward displacement of air because it is denser than air and soluble in water?
records.sourceExplanation:
Carbon (IV) oxide (\text{CO}_2) has a molar mass of 44\text{ g/mol}, making it significantly denser than dry air (\approx 29\text{ g/mol}).
Because it is denser than air, it displaces air upward in a gas jar (upward delivery / downward displacement of air).
Ammonia and hydrogen are lighter than air and are collected by downward delivery.
Hence, \text{CO}_2 is collected by downward displacement of air.

records.question: In an electrochemical cell, oxidation always takes place at the
records.sourceExplanation:
By standard definition, oxidation (loss of electrons) occurs at the anode electrode in both galvanic and electrolytic cells.
Reduction (gain of electrons) always takes place at the cathode electrode.
A standard memory aid is AN OX (Anode = Oxidation) and RED CAT (Reduction = Cathode).
Thus, oxidation takes place at the anode.

records.question: Which of the following is an example of a physical change?
records.sourceExplanation:
A physical change alters physical form without creating new chemical substances and is easily reversible.
Magnetizing an iron rod aligns its internal magnetic domains without altering the chemical identity of iron (\text{Fe}).
Burning, rusting, and fermentation break and form chemical bonds, producing entirely new substances.
Therefore, magnetization is a physical change.

records.question: The functional group of an ester is represented as
records.sourceExplanation:
Esters are produced from the reaction between carboxylic acids and alkanols, containing the ester link (-\text{COO}-).
Carboxylic acids contain the carboxyl group (-\text{COOH}), alkanols contain the hydroxyl group (-\text{OH}), and aldehydes contain the formyl group (-\text{CHO}).
Therefore, -\text{COO}- represents the ester functional group.

records.question: Which of the following laws states that equal volumes of all gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules?
records.sourceExplanation:
Avogadro's Law states that V \propto n at constant temperature and pressure.
Equal volumes (V) of any ideal gases under identical conditions contain the exact same number of moles or molecules (n).
Boyle's law relates pressure and volume; Charles's law relates volume and temperature.
Hence, Avogadro's Law is the correct choice.

records.question: In the Periodic Table, elements in the same vertical column (group) have the same number of
records.sourceExplanation:
Elements arranged in the same vertical column (group) share identical valence-shell electron configurations.
As a result, they possess the exact same number of valence (outermost) electrons.
This identical valence electron count gives elements in the same group similar chemical properties and reactivity patterns.
Thus, valence electrons remain constant down a group.
JAMB CHEMISTRY PAST QUESTIONS & DETAILED EXPLANATIONS (101 - 150)

records.question: The reaction between an alkanoic acid and an alkanol in the presence of concentrated H2SO4 is known as
records.sourceExplanation:
The reaction of a carboxylic acid (alkanoic acid) with an alcohol (alkanol) yields an ester and water.
Concentrated H2SO4 acts as both a catalyst and a dehydrating agent to shift equilibrium toward product formation.
This process is termed esterification.

records.question: What mass of aluminium is contained in 2.5 moles of pure aluminium metal? [Al = 27]
records.sourceExplanation:
Mass = Moles × Molar Mass
Mass = 2.5 mol × 27 g/mol = 67.5 g.
Therefore, 2.5 moles of aluminium weighs 67.5 g.

records.question: Which of the following drying agents is most suitable for drying ammonia gas?
records.sourceExplanation:
Ammonia (NH3) is a basic gas.
It reacts chemically with acidic drying agents like H2SO4 and P4O10, forming salts.
It also reacts with CaCl2 to form a complex compound, CaCl2·8NH3.
Quicklime (CaO) is basic, so it dries ammonia gas without reacting with it.

records.question: Which allotrope of sulfur is stable above 96°C?
records.sourceExplanation:
Rhombic sulfur (alpha-sulfur) is stable below 96°C.
At 96°C (transition temperature), rhombic sulfur slowly converts into monoclinic sulfur (beta-sulfur).
Monoclinic sulfur remains the stable crystalline allotrope between 96°C and its melting point (119°C).

records.question: Temporary hardness of water can be removed by
records.sourceExplanation:
Temporary hardness is caused by dissolved calcium or magnesium hydrogen trioxocarbonate (IV), Ca(HCO3)2 or Mg(HCO3)2.
Boiling decomposes the soluble hydrogen carbonate into insoluble calcium carbonate (CaCO3), water, and carbon (IV) oxide.
The precipitated CaCO3 can then be filtered out, softening the water.

records.question: During the electrolysis of concentrated sodium chloride solution (brine) using carbon electrodes, the main gas evolved at the anode is
records.sourceExplanation:
Ions present: Na+ and H+ at the cathode; Cl- and OH- at the anode.
At the anode, although OH- has a lower discharge potential, the high concentration of Cl- ions (concentration effect) causes Cl- to be discharged preferentially.
Chlorine gas (Cl2) is liberated at the anode.

records.question: A radioactive isotope has a half-life of 10 days. If the initial mass is 80 g, what mass remains after 30 days?
records.sourceExplanation:
Number of half-lives (n) = Total time / Half-life = 30 days / 10 days = 3 half-lives.
Remaining mass = Initial mass / (2^n) = 80 g / (2^3) = 80 g / 8 = 10 g.

records.question: For the reversible reaction: N2(g) + 3H2(g) ⇌ 2NH3(g) ΔH = -92 kJ, an increase in total pressure will
options: have no effect on the equilibrium position
records.sourceExplanation:
According to Le Chatelier's principle, an increase in pressure shifts the equilibrium in the direction of fewer moles of gas.
Reactant side has 1 + 3 = 4 moles of gas; product side has 2 moles of gas.
Increasing pressure shifts the position of equilibrium to the right (forward reaction), increasing ammonia yield.

records.question: Which of the following periodic properties generally decreases across a period from left to right?
records.sourceExplanation:
Across a period from left to right, nuclear charge increases while the number of electron shells remains constant.
The stronger electrostatic attraction pulls outer electrons closer to the nucleus, causing atomic radius to decrease.
Ionization energy, electronegativity, and electron affinity generally increase across a period.

records.question: A green flame test color indicates the presence of which cation?
records.sourceExplanation:
Sodium (Na+) gives a persistent golden-yellow flame.
Potassium (K+) gives a lilac/violet flame.
Calcium (Ca2+) gives a brick-red/orange-red flame.
Copper (Cu2+) gives a characteristic bluish-green flame.

records.question: Which indicator is most suitable for titrating a strong acid against a weak base?
records.sourceExplanation:
Titrating a strong acid against a weak base yields an acidic equivalence point (pH < 7).
Methyl orange changes color in the acidic pH range (3.1 to 4.4), matching the sharp pH jump at equivalence.
Phenolphthalein is suitable for weak acid-strong base titrations (pH > 7).

records.question: What is the oxidation number of sulfur in H2SO4?
records.sourceExplanation:
In H2SO4, Hydrogen = +1 and Oxygen = -2.
Net charge of neutral compound = 0.
2(+1) + S + 4(-2) = 0 => 2 + S - 8 = 0 => S - 6 = 0 => S = +6.

records.question: The empirical formula of an organic compound containing 40% Carbon, 6.7% Hydrogen, and 53.3% Oxygen by mass is [C = 12, H = 1, O = 16]
records.sourceExplanation:
Moles: C = 40 / 12 = 3.33; H = 6.7 / 1 = 6.70; O = 53.3 / 16 = 3.33.
Divide by smallest (3.33): C = 1, H = 2, O = 1.
Empirical formula = CH2O.

records.question: At constant temperature, the volume of a fixed mass of gas is inversely proportional to its pressure. This statement represents
records.sourceExplanation:
Boyle's Law states that for a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature, P ∝ 1/V or P1V1 = P2V2.
Charles's Law relates volume and absolute temperature at constant pressure.

records.question: Which fraction of crude oil is collected at the top of a fractionating column?
records.sourceExplanation:
In fractional distillation of petroleum, fractions with lower boiling points volatilize easily and rise to the top.
Petroleum gases (methane, ethane, propane, butane) have the lowest boiling points (< 20°C) and emerge at the top.
Heavy residues like bitumen condense at the bottom.

records.question: The catalytic dehydration of ethanol with excess concentrated H2SO4 at 170°C yields
records.sourceExplanation:
Heating ethanol with excess concentrated H2SO4 at 170°C causes intramolecular dehydration to yield ethene:
C2H5OH -> C2H4 + H2O.
At lower temperature (140°C with excess ethanol), intermolecular dehydration yields ethoxyethane (diethyl ether).

records.question: If 20 g of a salt dissolves completely in 50 g of water at 25°C to form a saturated solution, the solubility of the salt in g/100g water is
records.sourceExplanation:
Solubility = (Mass of solute / Mass of solvent) × 100
Solubility = (20 g / 50 g) × 100 = 40 g per 100 g of water.

records.question: A reaction in which heat is absorbed from the surroundings is characterized by
records.sourceExplanation:
Endothermic reactions absorb thermal energy from their surroundings, raising the enthalpy of products above reactants.
Consequently, the enthalpy change ΔH = H_products - H_reactants is positive (+ΔH).

records.question: In terms of electron transfer, oxidation is defined as the
records.sourceExplanation:
Oxidation is the loss of electrons, leading to an increase in oxidation state.
Reduction is the gain of electrons, leading to a decrease in oxidation state.
Memory aid: OIL RIG (Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain).

records.question: What is the IUPAC name of the compound CH3-CH(OH)-CH3?
records.sourceExplanation:
The longest carbon chain has 3 carbon atoms (propane derivative).
The hydroxyl functional group (-OH) is located on carbon-2.
Systematic IUPAC name = Propan-2-ol (or 2-propanol).

records.question: Noble gases are chemically unreactive primarily because
options: they possess stable completely filled valence electron shells
records.answerText: they possess stable completely filled valence electron shells
records.sourceExplanation:
Noble gases (Group 18) have octet valence shell configurations (ns2 np6, or 1s2 for Helium).
This completely filled valence shell configuration imparts extreme chemical stability, preventing electron sharing, loss, or gain.

records.question: Which of the following actions increases the rate of a chemical reaction between solid zinc and hydrochloric acid?
options: Using zinc lumps instead of zinc powder
Lowering the temperature of the acid
Increasing the concentration of hydrochloric acid
records.answerText: Increasing the concentration of hydrochloric acid
records.sourceExplanation:
Increasing reactant concentration increases particle collision frequency per unit time.
Higher collision frequency accelerates the rate of chemical reaction.
Using powder (not lumps) and increasing temperature also increase reaction rate.

records.question: Vegetable oils are converted into solid margarine through the process of
records.sourceExplanation:
Vegetable oils contain unsaturated carbon-carbon double bonds (C=C).
Bubbling hydrogen gas through liquid oil in the presence of a nickel catalyst at ~180°C saturates the double bonds.
This raises the melting point, transforming liquid oil into solid margarine.

records.question: Which atmospheric pollutant gas reacts with hemoglobin in blood to reduce oxygen transport capacity?
records.sourceExplanation:
Carbon (II) oxide (CO) binds to blood hemoglobin with ~200 times greater affinity than oxygen.
It forms carboxyhemoglobin, blocking oxygen binding and causing asphyxiation/poisoning.

records.question: How many orbitals exist in the d-subshell of an atom?
records.sourceExplanation:
Subshell orbital counts: s-subshell = 1 orbital; p-subshell = 3 orbitals; d-subshell = 5 orbitals; f-subshell = 7 orbitals.
Each orbital holds a maximum of 2 electrons, allowing d-subshells to hold up to 10 electrons.

records.question: Structural isomers are compounds that have the same
options: structural formula but different molecular formulas
molecular formula but different structural formulas
physical properties but different chemical properties
empirical formula but different molecular weights
records.answerText: molecular formula but different structural formulas
records.sourceExplanation: Structural isomerism describes organic compounds possessing identical molecular formulas (same atom count) but different structural arrangements/connectivity of atoms.

records.question: Which gas is produced when sodium trioxocarbonate (IV) reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid?
records.sourceExplanation:
Trioxocarbonate (IV) salts react with acids to produce a salt, water, and carbon (IV) oxide gas with effervescence:
Na2CO3(aq) + 2HCl(aq) -> 2NaCl(aq) + H2O(l) + CO2(g).

records.question: Transition elements exhibit variable oxidation states due to the participation of electrons in their
records.sourceExplanation:
Transition metals have close energy levels between their outer s-orbitals (4s) and underlying d-orbitals (3d).
Electrons from both 4s and 3d orbitals can participate in chemical bonding, resulting in variable oxidation states (e.g., Fe2+ and Fe3+).

records.question: According to Faraday's First Law of Electrolysis, the mass (m) of a substance liberated at an electrode is directly proportional to the
records.sourceExplanation: Faraday's First Law states m ∝ Q => m = zQ = zIt, where m is mass liberated, Q is total electric charge in Coulombs, I is current, and t is time.

records.question: Nylon-6,6 is classified as a
records.sourceExplanation:
Nylon-6,6 is synthesized by condensing hexanedioic acid and hexane-1,6-diamine with the elimination of small water molecules.
Because water is eliminated during chain growth, it is a synthetic condensation polymer (polyamide).

records.question: A solution has a pOH of 4 at 25°C. What is its pH?
records.sourceExplanation:
For aqueous solutions at 25°C, pH + pOH = 14.
pH = 14 - pOH = 14 - 4 = 10.
A pH of 10 indicates a basic/alkaline solution.

records.question: In the industrial extraction of sulfur by the Frasch process, superheated water is pumped underground to
options: react with sulfur to form H2S
records.sourceExplanation:
Sulfur has a relatively low melting point (~115°C).
Superheated water at 170°C under high pressure is pumped down the outer pipe of a Frasch rig to melt underground elemental sulfur deposits.
Compressed air then forces liquid sulfur to the surface.

records.question: Which separation technique is best suited for separating a mixture of two miscible liquids with distinct boiling points?
records.sourceExplanation:
Fractional distillation separates miscible liquids based on differences in their boiling points using a fractionating column.
Filtration separates insoluble solids from liquids, and chromatography separates minute solutes based on differential distribution.

records.question: A dynamic chemical equilibrium is achieved when the
options: concentration of reactants equals concentration of products
rate of forward reaction equals rate of reverse reaction
records.answerText: rate of forward reaction equals rate of reverse reaction
records.sourceExplanation:
Chemical equilibrium is dynamic because both forward and reverse reactions continue occurring simultaneously.
Equilibrium is reached when forward reaction rate equals reverse reaction rate, maintaining constant macroscopic concentrations.

records.question: Which haloalkane is widely used as a refrigerant but causes depletion of the atmospheric ozone layer?
records.sourceExplanation:
Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs, e.g., Freon) were widely used in refrigeration and aerosol propellants.
UV radiation breaks CFCs in the stratosphere, releasing chlorine radicals that catalytically destroy ozone (O3) molecules.

records.question: When ammonium trioxonitrate (V) is heated, the gas evolved is
records.sourceExplanation:
Thermal decomposition of ammonium trioxonitrate (V) yields dinitrogen (I) oxide gas (laughing gas) and water vapor:
NH4NO3(s) -> N2O(g) + 2H2O(g).

records.question: Which of the following metals will displace copper from aqueous copper (II) tetraoxosulphate (VI) solution?
records.sourceExplanation:
Iron sits above copper in the electrochemical/reactivity series.
More reactive metals displace less reactive metals from solution:
Fe(s) + CuSO4(aq) -> FeSO4(aq) + Cu(s).
Silver, gold, and platinum sit below copper and cannot displace it.

records.question: The general molecular formula for the homologous series of alkanes is
records.sourceExplanation:
Alkanes (saturated hydrocarbons): CnH2n+2.
Alkenes (monounsaturated hydrocarbons): CnH2n.
Alkynes (triply bonded hydrocarbons): CnH2n-2.
JAMB CHEMISTRY PAST QUESTIONS & DETAILED EXPLANATIONS (139 - 200)

records.question: The main impurity removed during the purification of bauxite in the Bayer process is
records.sourceExplanation:
Crude bauxite ore contains significant reddish-brown iron (III) oxide (Fe2O3) impurities.
Concentrated NaOH dissolves aluminium oxide to form soluble sodium tetrahydroxoaluminate (III), leaving insoluble Fe2O3 behind as "red mud" during filtration.

records.question: What volume does 0.5 moles of carbon (IV) oxide gas occupy at STP? [Molar volume of gas at STP = 22.4 dm3]
records.sourceExplanation:
Volume at STP = Moles × Molar Volume
Volume = 0.5 mol × 22.4 dm3/mol = 11.2 dm3.

records.question: Soap forms scum with hard water because hard water contains
records.sourceExplanation:
Soap consists of sodium or potassium salts of fatty acids (e.g., C17H35COONa).
Soluble soap reacts with Ca2+ or Mg2+ ions in hard water to form insoluble calcium or magnesium alkanoates (scum):
2C17H35COONa + Ca2+ -> (C17H35COO)2Ca(s) + 2Na+.

records.question: Atoms of the same element with the same atomic number but different mass numbers are called
records.sourceExplanation: Isotopes are atoms of the same element containing equal numbers of protons (same atomic number) but differing numbers of neutrons (different mass numbers), e.g., 12C and 14C.

records.question: Which functional group test confirms the presence of unsaturation in an organic liquid?
records.sourceExplanation: Unsaturated compounds containing C=C or C≡C bonds rapidly decolorize reddish-brown bromine water (or aqueous KMnO4) via addition reactions.

records.question: The scattering of a beam of light by colloidal particles is known as the
records.sourceExplanation:
Colloidal particles are large enough (1-1000 nm) to scatter visible light rays passing through the medium.
This scattering renders the light path visible, a phenomenon called the Tyndall effect.

records.question: Which of the following oxides dissolves in water to form an acidic solution?
records.sourceExplanation:
Non-metal oxides (like SO3, CO2, NO2) are acidic anhydrides.
Sulfur trioxide (SO3) dissolves in water to produce sulfuric acid: SO3 + H2O -> H2SO4.
Metallic oxides (Na2O, CaO, MgO) form basic solutions.

records.question: Which allotrope of phosphorus is spontaneously flammable in air at room temperature?
records.sourceExplanation:
White phosphorus (P4) is highly reactive with a low ignition temperature (~30°C).
It spontaneously oxidizes in air with white smoke and luminescence, which is why it is stored under water.

records.question: The standard enthalpy of neutralization for a reaction between a strong acid and a strong base is approximately
records.sourceExplanation:
Neutralization of any strong acid by a strong base reduces to the net ionic equation: H+(aq) + OH-(aq) -> H2O(l).
The heat liberated in this reaction is constant at approximately -57.3 kJ/mol (-13.7 kcal/mol).

records.question: If doubling the concentration of a reactant quadruples the rate of reaction, the order of reaction with respect to that reactant is
records.sourceExplanation:
Rate law: Rate ∝ [A]^n.
If [A] is multiplied by 2 and Rate is multiplied by 4 (2^2):
2^n = 4 => n = 2.
The reaction is second order with respect to reactant A.

records.question: The two main crystalline allotropes of sulfur are
options: Monoclinic sulfur and Flowers of sulfur
records.sourceExplanation:
Sulfur exhibits two well-defined crystalline allotropes: Rhombic sulfur (alpha-sulfur) and Monoclinic sulfur (beta-sulfur).
Plastic, amorphous, and colloidal forms are non-crystalline/amorphous allotropes.

records.question: Which halogen is a dark-red liquid at room temperature and pressure?
records.sourceExplanation:
Physical states of halogens at room temperature:
Fluorine (F2): Pale yellow gas
Chlorine (Cl2): Greenish-yellow gas
Bromine (Br2): Dense dark-red/reddish-brown liquid
Iodine (I2): Dark purple/black crystalline solid

records.question: Which alloy is composed primarily of copper and zinc?
records.sourceExplanation:
Brass is an alloy consisting of copper (Cu) and zinc (Zn).
Bronze consists of copper and tin (Sn).
Steel consists of iron and carbon.

records.question: Gas evolution is observed when dilute hydrochloric acid is added to calcium trioxocarbonate (IV). The gas evolved turns lime water
records.sourceExplanation:
Reaction: CaCO3 + 2HCl -> CaCl2 + H2O + CO2(g).
Carbon (IV) oxide gas (CO2) reacts with lime water, Ca(OH)2, to form insoluble calcium carbonate (CaCO3), turning the solution milky/cloudy.

records.question: What is the oxidation number of manganese in potassium tetraoxomanganate (VII), KMnO4?
The hybridization of carbon orbitals in ethyne (C2H2) is
records.sourceExplanation:
In ethyne (H-C≡C-H), each carbon forms one single sigma bond with hydrogen and one triple bond (one sigma, two pi) with carbon.
Two hybrid orbitals are formed per carbon atom, corresponding to sp hybridization (linear geometry, 180° bond angle).

records.question: A catalyst alters the rate of a chemical reaction by
options: increasing the enthalpy change of the reaction
increasing the kinetic energy of reactant particles
shifting the equilibrium position to favor products
records.sourceExplanation:
A catalyst provides an alternative reaction pathway with lower activation energy (Ea).
It does not alter the enthalpy change (ΔH), nor does it change equilibrium concentrations.

records.question: Which of the following compounds is deliquescent?
records.sourceExplanation:
Deliquescent substances (e.g., CaCl2, NaOH, FeCl3) absorb sufficient water from the atmosphere to dissolve completely and form a solution.
CuSO4·5H2O and Na2CO3·10H2O are efflorescent or hydrated salts.

records.question: What is the complete combustion product of alkanes in excess oxygen?
records.sourceExplanation: Complete combustion of hydrocarbons in excess oxygen yields carbon (IV) oxide (CO2) and water vapor (H2O), releasing significant heat.

records.question: Electropositivity of alkali metals (Group 1) down the group
records.sourceExplanation:
Down Group 1, atomic radius increases and outer valence electrons are shielded by more inner shells.
The nuclear attraction on valence electrons weakens, making it easier to lose electrons (increasing metallic character/electropositivity).

records.question: The organic acid present in household vinegar is
records.sourceExplanation: Vinegar is a dilute aqueous solution (approx. 4–8% by volume) of ethanoic acid (CH3COOH), produced by fermentation of ethanol.

records.question: What is the pH of a solution with a hydrogen ion concentration [H+] of 1 × 10^-5 mol/dm3?
The conversion of starch to maltose during enzyme action is catalyzed by
records.sourceExplanation:
Diastase (amylase) converts starch into maltose.
Maltase converts maltose to glucose.
Zymase ferments glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide.

records.question: Which type of chemical bonding exists between sodium and chlorine atoms in sodium chloride?
records.sourceExplanation:
Sodium (metal) loses an electron to form Na+, while chlorine (non-metal) gains an electron to form Cl-.
The strong electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions forms an electrovalent (ionic) bond.

records.question: Which nuclear radiation carries zero electrical charge and zero mass?
records.sourceExplanation:
Gamma rays are high-energy electromagnetic radiation with zero charge and zero mass.
Alpha particles carry a +2 charge and 4 amu mass; Beta particles carry a -1 charge.

records.question: Which functional group identifies an aldehyde?
records.sourceExplanation:
Aldehydes contain the formyl group (-CHO) attached to a terminal carbon atom.
OH is alcohol, -COOH is carboxylic acid, -CO- is ketone.

records.question: Which gas possesses a characteristic rotten-egg odor?
records.sourceExplanation: Hydrogen sulfide (H2S) is a colorless, toxic gas with a distinct foul smell of rotten eggs.

records.question: The combined gas law equation is represented as
records.sourceExplanation: Combining Boyle's Law (P ∝ 1/V) and Charles's Law (V ∝ T) yields the Combined Gas Law: (P1V1)/T1 = (P2V2)/T2.

records.question: Characteristic addition reactions are typical of
records.sourceExplanation:
Unsaturated hydrocarbons (alkenes with C=C and alkynes with C≡C) undergo addition reactions to break pi bonds and form saturated products.
Alkanes undergo substitution reactions.

records.question: Controlled oxidation of a primary alkanol yields an
records.sourceExplanation:
Controlled oxidation of a primary alcohol (e.g., using acidified K2Cr2O7) produces an alkanal (aldehyde).
Further oxidation converts the alkanal to an alkanoic acid.
Oxidation of secondary alcohols yields alkanones (ketones).

records.question: Which separation method is used to separate plant pigments or inks?
records.sourceExplanation: Paper chromatography separates small quantities of dissolved solutes based on their differential partition coefficients between stationary (paper) and mobile (solvent) phases.

records.question: The chemical composition of rust is
records.sourceExplanation: Rust is hydrated iron (III) oxide, Fe2O3·xH2O, formed by prolonged exposure of iron to water and oxygen.

records.question: An apparatus used specifically for measuring heat changes during chemical processes is a
records.sourceExplanation: A calorimeter is an insulated container used to measure the thermal energy released or absorbed during chemical or physical reactions.

records.question: Which non-metal oxide is the acid anhydride of tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid (H2SO4)?
records.sourceExplanation:
Dissolving SO3 in water yields H2SO4:
SO3 + H2O -> H2SO4.
SO2 is the anhydride of H2SO3 (trioxosulphate (IV) acid).

records.question: Which element has the lowest boiling point among halogens?
records.sourceExplanation:
Down Group 17, molecular size and electron cloud density increase, resulting in stronger van der Waals forces.
Fluorine (F2) is the smallest halogen with the weakest intermolecular forces, giving it the lowest boiling point (-188°C).

records.question: Organic compounds containing the functional group -COO- are classified as
records.sourceExplanation: Alkanoates (esters) contain the -COO- functional group connecting an acyl group to an alkyl group.

records.question: Le Chatelier's Principle states that when a system in dynamic equilibrium is subjected to a change in conditions, the system will
options: shift to oppose or neutralize the effect of the change
records.answerText: shift to oppose or neutralize the effect of the change
records.sourceExplanation: Le Chatelier's Principle: If a constraint (temperature, pressure, concentration) is applied to a system at equilibrium, the system adjusts to minimize or counteract that constraint.

records.question: What are the SI units of concentration in volumetric analysis?
records.sourceExplanation: Molar concentration (molarity) is expressed as moles of solute per cubic decimeter of solution (mol/dm3).

records.question: The industrial process of breaking heavy long-chain hydrocarbon molecules into lighter, more useful short-chain alkanes and alkenes is known as
records.sourceExplanation: Cracking uses heat (thermal cracking) or catalysts (catalytic cracking) to break large petroleum fractions (gas oil/kerosene) into smaller, higher-demand fuels like petrol and ethene.

records.question: Fehling's solution gives a brick-red precipitate when heated with an
records.sourceExplanation:
Alkanals (aldehydes) are strong reducing agents. They reduce copper (II) ions in Fehling's solution to red insoluble copper (I) oxide (Cu2O).
Alkanones (ketones) do not react with Fehling's solution.

records.question: What is standard temperature in Kelvin (K)?
records.sourceExplanation: Standard Temperature is 0°C, which converts to 0 + 273.15 = 273 K (or 273.15 K).

records.question: Which of the following substances sublimes upon heating?
records.sourceExplanation: Ammonium chloride (NH4Cl), iodine, and naphthalene sublime directly from solid to gas when heated without melting.

records.question: What is the maximum number of electrons that can occupy the second main electron shell (n = 2)?
records.sourceExplanation:
Maximum electron capacity = 2(n^2).
For n = 2: Capacity = 2(2^2) = 2(4) = 8 electrons.

records.question: Which gas is evolved when amphoteric metals like zinc react with hot concentrated sodium hydroxide solution?
records.sourceExplanation:
Amphoteric metals (Zn, Al, Pb) react with strong bases to form complex salts and liberate hydrogen gas:
Zn + 2NaOH + 2H2O -> Na2[Zn(OH)4] + H2(g).

records.question: Starch, cellulose, and proteins are examples of
records.sourceExplanation:
Starch and cellulose are natural polysaccharides formed by condensation of glucose monomers.
Proteins are natural polyamides formed by condensation of amino acid monomers.
JAMB CHEMISTRY PAST QUESTIONS & DETAILED EXPLANATIONS (184 - 250)

records.question: Substances containing the same molecular and structural formulas but differing in spatial 3D arrangement of atoms exhibit
records.sourceExplanation: Stereoisomerism (including geometric and optical isomerism) occurs when atoms have the same connectivity but different three-dimensional spatial arrangements.

records.question: Which subatomic particle has no electrical charge and resides inside the nucleus?
records.sourceExplanation: Protons carry a +1 charge; Electrons carry a -1 charge; Neutrons carry no net charge (neutral) and sit inside the nucleus alongside protons.

records.question: The reaction between fats/oils and hot concentrated alkali produces glycerol and
records.sourceExplanation: Saponification (alkaline hydrolysis of triglycerides) produces propane-1,2,3-triol (glycerol) and sodium/potassium salts of fatty acids (soap).

records.question: A solution with a pH value of 7 at 25°C is
records.sourceExplanation: On the pH scale (0 to 14): pH < 7 is acidic, pH = 7 is neutral, and pH > 7 is basic/alkaline.

records.question: Which concentrated acid is commonly used as a laboratory drying and dehydrating agent?
records.sourceExplanation: Concentrated H2SO4 has a strong affinity for water. It acts as a drying agent for non-reacting gases and as a dehydrating agent removing chemically bound water from organic compounds.

records.question: Heavy water is chemically known as
records.sourceExplanation: Heavy water contains the deuterium isotope of hydrogen (2H or D). Its formula is D2O.

records.question: Polyethene is synthesized from ethene monomers through
records.sourceExplanation: Ethene (C2H4) contains a double bond. Monomers join together end-to-end without losing any small molecules, undergoing addition polymerization to form polyethene.

records.question: Gas collection by upward displacement of air is suitable for gases that are
options: lighter than air and insoluble in water
lighter than air and soluble in water
records.sourceExplanation: Dense gases (e.g., Cl2, HCl, CO2) sink to the bottom of a gas jar, displacing lighter air upward. This technique is upward displacement of air (downward delivery).

records.question: The formula relating mass number (A), atomic number (Z), and neutron number (N) is
records.sourceExplanation: Mass number (A) represents total nucleons (protons + neutrons): A = Z + N.

records.question: The solubility of most gases in liquid solvents as temperature increases generally
records.sourceExplanation: Gas dissolution is exothermic. Increasing temperature increases kinetic energy, causing gas molecules to escape the liquid solution, thereby decreasing solubility.

records.question: The mathematical relationship between empirical formula and molecular formula is
records.sourceExplanation: Molecular formula represents an integer multiple (n) of the empirical formula: Molecular Formula = n × (Empirical Formula).

records.question: Which gas is liberated when concentrated trioxonitrate (V) acid reacts with copper turnings?
records.sourceExplanation:
Concentrated HNO3 reacts with copper to produce dense reddish-brown fumes of nitrogen (IV) oxide (NO2):
Cu + 4HNO3 -> Cu(NO3)2 + 2NO2(g) + 2H2O.
Dilute HNO3 yields colorless nitrogen (II) oxide (NO).

records.question: Which technique separates a mixture of soluble solids based on differences in solubility at different temperatures?
records.sourceExplanation: Fractional crystallization separates two or more dissolved solids with different temperature-solubility curves by controlled cooling of a saturated solution.

records.question: In the test for trioxocarbonate (IV) ions (CO32-), addition of dilute HCl yields a gas that turns lime water
records.sourceExplanation: Adding acid to CO32- liberates CO2 gas, which precipitates CaCO3 in lime water, turning it milky.

records.question: Which element is present in all organic compounds?
records.sourceExplanation: Carbon is the essential element defining organic chemistry due to its unique catenation and bonding capacity.

records.question: The functional group present in alkanones (ketones) is
records.sourceExplanation: Alkanones contain a carbonyl group (>C=O) bonded to two carbon atoms (non-terminal).

records.question: Which acid is present in human gastric juice aiding digestion?
records.sourceExplanation: Parietal cells in the stomach secrete dilute hydrochloric acid (HCl, ~0.1 M) to maintain a low pH (~1.5–2.0), activating pepsin for protein digestion.

records.question: What is the organic product formed when propene reacts with hydrogen bromide (HBr)?
records.sourceExplanation: According to Markovnikov's rule, when an unsymmetrical reagent (HBr) adds to an unsymmetrical alkene (CH3-CH=CH2), the hydrogen atom attaches to the carbon with more hydrogen atoms, yielding 2-bromopropane as the major product.

records.question: The process by which a solid changes directly into a gas without passing through the liquid state is
records.sourceExplanation: Sublimation is the direct phase transition from solid to gas upon heating without forming a liquid intermediate (e.g., iodine, ammonium chloride, dry ice).

records.question: Which of the following is a neutral oxide?
records.sourceExplanation: Carbon (II) oxide (CO), dinitrogen (I) oxide (N2O), and nitrogen (II) oxide (NO) do not react with acids or bases to form salts, making them neutral oxides.

records.question: Which gas turns damp red litmus paper blue?
records.sourceExplanation: Ammonia (NH3) is the only common alkaline gas. When dissolved in moisture on damp red litmus paper, it forms ammonium hydroxide (NH4OH), turning the paper blue.

records.question: What volume of 0.1 mol/dm3 NaOH is required to neutralize 20 cm3 of 0.1 mol/dm3 H2SO4?
records.sourceExplanation:
Reaction: H2SO4 + 2NaOH -> Na2SO4 + 2H2O.
Moles of acid = 0.1 × 0.020 = 0.002 mol.
Moles of base required = 2 × 0.002 = 0.004 mol.
Volume of base = Moles / Concentration = 0.004 / 0.1 = 0.040 dm3 = 40 cm3.

records.question: The mass of an electron is approximately
options: equal to that of a proton
equal to that of a neutron
1/1840 of the mass of a proton
twice the mass of a proton
records.answerText: 1/1840 of the mass of a proton
records.sourceExplanation: An electron has a negligible relative mass of approximately 1/1840 (or 1/1836) amu relative to a proton or neutron.

records.question: Which technique is best suited for separating a mixture of iron filings and sulfur powder?
records.sourceExplanation: Iron is ferromagnetic, whereas sulfur is non-magnetic. Passing a magnet over the mixture attracts iron filings, leaving pure sulfur behind.

records.question: Which of the following halogen molecules has the highest bond dissociation energy?
records.sourceExplanation: Chlorine (Cl2) has the highest bond energy among halogens. Fluorine (F2) has an unexpectedly low bond energy due to intense electrostatic repulsion between lone pairs on its exceptionally small atoms.

records.question: The chemical formula of copper (II) tetraoxosulphate (VI) pentahydrate is
records.sourceExplanation: Blue vitriol is copper (II) sulfate pentahydrate, represented chemically as CuSO4·5H2O.

records.question: What is the concentration in g/dm3 of a 0.5 mol/dm3 solution of sodium chloride (NaCl)? [Na = 23, Cl = 35.5]
records.sourceExplanation:
Molar mass of NaCl = 23 + 35.5 = 58.5 g/mol.
Mass concentration = Molar concentration × Molar mass = 0.5 mol/dm3 × 58.5 g/mol = 29.25 g/dm3.

records.question: Which type of nuclear radiation has the highest penetrating power?
records.sourceExplanation: Gamma rays are uncharged high-energy photons with zero rest mass, allowing them to penetrate deep through matter (requiring thick lead or concrete to block).

records.question: Coal gas is a fuel gas consisting primarily of
options: Sulfur dioxide, carbon monoxide, and water vapor
records.sourceExplanation: Coal gas, produced by the destructive distillation of coal, is a gaseous mixture of hydrogen (~50%), methane (~30%), and carbon (II) oxide (~10%).

records.question: The functional group present in alkanoic acids is
records.sourceExplanation: Alkanoic (carboxylic) acids are characterized by the carboxyl functional group (-COOH).

records.question: When sodium metal reacts with cold water, the products formed are
records.sourceExplanation: Sodium reacts vigorously with cold water: 2Na(s) + 2H2O(l) -> 2NaOH(aq) + H2(g).

records.question: The Law of Definite Proportions states that
options: elements combine in simple whole number ratios by volume
a pure chemical compound always contains the same elements combined in the same proportion by mass
total mass of reactants equals total mass of products
equal volumes of gases contain equal numbers of molecules
records.answerText: a pure chemical compound always contains the same elements combined in the same proportion by mass
records.sourceExplanation: Formulated by Joseph Proust, this law states that a chemical compound always contains its component elements in fixed mass ratios regardless of source or method of preparation.

records.question: What is the oxidation number of nitrogen in the nitrate ion (NO3-)?
Which of the following is classified as a primary cell?
records.sourceExplanation: A primary cell (e.g., Leclanché dry cell) cannot be recharged because its electrochemical reactions are irreversible. Accumulators and Ni-Cd batteries are secondary (rechargeable) cells.

records.question: Esters are organic compounds widely recognized for their
records.sourceExplanation: Esters possess pleasant, sweet fruity odors and are responsible for the natural fragrances of fruits and flowers (used in perfumes and flavorings).

records.question: What is the conjugate base of hydrogen sulfate ion (HSO4-)?
records.sourceExplanation:
A conjugate base is formed when a Brønsted-Lowry acid donates a proton (H+).
HSO4- -> H+ + SO42-. Thus, SO42- is the conjugate base.

records.question: The minimum energy required for colliding reactant particles to form an activated complex and lead to product formation is called
records.sourceExplanation: Activation energy (Ea) is the energy threshold reactant molecules must overcome during collisions to break existing bonds and initiate a reaction.

records.question: Which metal is extracted commercially by the electrolysis of its fused (molten) chloride?
records.sourceExplanation: Sodium is extracted in the Downs cell by electrolyzing molten sodium chloride (NaCl) mixed with CaCl2 to lower its melting point.

records.question: Pure water boils at 100°C at 1 atm. Adding sodium chloride to pure water will
records.sourceExplanation: Dissolving a non-volatile solute (NaCl) in water lowers its vapor pressure, requiring a higher temperature to reach atmospheric pressure, thus elevating the boiling point above 100°C.

records.question: Which of the following hydrocarbon formulas represents an alkene?
records.sourceExplanation: Alkenes fit the general molecular formula CnH2n. For n = 3, C3H2(3) = C3H6 (propene).

records.question: Galvanization is the process of protecting iron from rusting by coating it with a thin layer of
records.sourceExplanation: Galvanizing involves dipping iron or steel into molten zinc. Zinc acts as a physical barrier and sacrificial anode because it is more electropositive than iron.

records.question: The term "isomerism" refers to chemical compounds having
options: same molecular formula but different structural arrangements
same empirical formula but different molecular formulas
same physical properties but different chemical properties
same structural formula but different mass numbers
records.answerText: same molecular formula but different structural arrangements
records.sourceExplanation: Isomerism is the existence of two or more compounds possessing identical molecular formulas but distinct structural arrangements and properties.

records.question: Chlorination of water during municipal treatment is carried out to
records.sourceExplanation: Adding chlorine gas or hypochlorite compounds generates hypochlorous acid (HOCl), a strong disinfectant that kills harmful bacteria and viruses.

records.question: The occurrence of an element in two or more distinct physical forms in the same physical state is called
records.sourceExplanation: Allotropy is the property of an element existing in multiple structural modifications in the same physical state (e.g., diamond and graphite for carbon).

records.question: Which gas can be collected over water because it is virtually insoluble in water?
records.sourceExplanation: Hydrogen (H2) is non-polar and virtually insoluble in water, making displacement of water an effective collection technique. NH3, HCl, and SO2 are highly soluble.

records.question: Saturated hydrocarbons (alkan) undergo primarily
records.sourceExplanation:
Alkanes contain strong single C-C and C-H sigma bonds and lack functional groups, so they undergo halogen substitution under UV light rather than addition.
